body.text: Introduction

0.1 ... tāṃ muna tattvopaplavasiṃhaiṣa viṣamo nunaṃ maya ... ... nāsti tatphalaṃ vā svargādi / satyaṃ, tāvad āttasya karmaṇaḥ sambhoktaṃ ca paramārthavidbhir api laukiko mārgo 'nusartavyaḥ a ... / lokavyavahāraṃ prati sadṛśau bālapaṇḍitau //
body.translated_text: [0.1] ... this <s>Tattvopaplavasiṃha</s> (Lion of the Dissolution of Categories), formidable indeed, by me ... ... there is no fruit thereof such as heaven and the like. True, but even those who know ultimate reality must follow the worldly path regarding actions undertaken and their enjoyment ... With respect to worldly conduct, the ignorant and the learned are alike.

children.text: 0.1 ... tāṃ muna tattvopaplavasiṃha eṣa viṣamo nunaṃ maya ... ... nāsti tatphalaṃ vā svargādi / satyaṃ, tāvad āttasya karmaṇaḥ sambha ūktaṃ ca paramārthavidbhir api laukiko mārgo 'nusartavyaḥ a ... / lokavyavahāraṃ prati sadṛśau bālapaṇḍitau //

body.text: ityādi /
body.translated_text: And so on.

children.text: ityādi /

body.text: 0.2 nanu yady upaplavas tattvānāṃ kim āyāthātas tattvaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ / pṛthivy āpas tejo vāyur iti tattvāni / tatsamudāye śarīrendriyaviṣayasañjñetyādi / nānyārthatvāt / kimartham? pratibimbanārtham / kiṃ punar atra pratibimbyate? pṛthivyādīni tattvāni loke prasiddhāni / tānyapi vicāryamāṇāni na vyavatiṣṭhante / kiṃ punar anyāni?
body.translated_text: [0.2] Objection: If there is dissolution of the categories, what reality shall we expound? We shall explain the categories as they truly are. The categories are earth, water, fire, and wind. In their aggregate they are designated as body, sense organs, and objects—and so on. Because they serve no other purpose. For what purpose then? For the purpose of reflection. What then is reflected upon here? The categories such as earth and others are well-known in the world. Even these, when critically examined, do not stand firm. How much less then other things?

children.text: 0.2 nanu yady upaplavas tattvānāṃ kim āya āthātas tattvaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ / pṛthivy āpas tejo vāyur iti tattvāni / tatsamudāye śarīrendriyaviṣayasañjñetyādi / nānyārthatvāt / kimartham? pratibimbanārtham / kiṃ punar atra pratibimbyate? pṛthivyādīni tattvāni loke prasiddhāni / tānyapi vicāryamāṇāni na vyavatiṣṭhante / kiṃ punar anyāni?

body.text: 0.3 atha kathaṃ tāni na santi? tad ucyate  sallakṣaṇanibandhanaṃ mānavyavasthānam / mānanibandhanā ca meyasthitiḥ / tadabhāve tayoḥ sadvyavahāraviṣayatvaṃ kathaṃ ... tām / atha ... na ba ... vyavahāraḥ kriyate, tadātmani rūpāstitatvavyavahāro ghaṭādau ca sukhāstitvavyavahāraḥ pravartayitavyaḥ
body.translated_text: [0.3] Now, how is it that they do not exist? It is said: the determination of valid cognition (<s>māna</s>) depends on the definition of existence. And the establishment of the object of knowledge (<s>meya</s>) depends on valid cognition. In their absence, how can they be objects of the practice of existence? ... If ... practice is carried out, then one must employ the practice of the existence of form in its own nature, and the practice of the existence of pleasure in a pot and the like.

children.text: 0.3 atha kathaṃ tāni na santi? tad ucyate - sallakṣaṇanibandhanaṃ mānavyavasthānam / mānanibandhanā ca meyasthitiḥ / tadabhāve tayoḥ sadvyavahāraviṣayatvaṃ kathaṃ ... tām / atha ... na ba ... vyavahāraḥ kriyate, tadātmani rūpāstitatvavyavahāro ghaṭādau ca sukhāstitvavyavahāraḥ pravartayitavyaḥ

body.text: Chapter 1: Examination of the Nyāya definition of perception
1. indriyārthasannikarṣotpannaṃ jñānam avyapadeśyam avyabhicāri vyavasāyātmakaṃ pratyakṣam iti tallakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: [1.] The definition of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) is: knowledge born from the contact of sense organ and object, which is non-verbal (<s>avyapadeśya</s>), non-errant (<s>avyabhicāri</s>), and of the nature of determinate cognition (<s>vyavasāyātmaka</s>)—such is its definition.

children.text: 1. indriyārthasannikarṣotpannaṃ jñānam avyapadeśyam avyabhicāri vyavasāyātmakaṃ pratyakṣam iti tallakṣaṇam /

body.text: 1.1 tac cāvyabhicāritvam ... kim aduṣṭakārakasandohotpādyatvenāhosvid bādhārahitatvena pravṛttisāmarthyenānyathā vā?
body.translated_text: [1.1] And that non-errancy (<s>avyabhicāritva</s>) ... is it established by being produced from an aggregate of undefective causal factors, or by being free from sublation (<s>bādhā</s>), or by the capacity for successful activity (<s>pravṛttisāmarthya</s>), or in some other way?

children.text: 1.1 tac cāvyabhicāritvam ... kim aduṣṭakārakasandohotpādyatvenāhosvid bādhārahitatvena pravṛttisāmarthyenānyathā vā?

body.text: 1.11 tad yady aduṣṭakārakasandohotpādyatvenāvyabhicāritvaṃ, saiva kāraṇānām aduṣṭatā kenāvagamyate?
body.translated_text: [1.11] If non-errancy consists in being produced from an aggregate of undefective causal factors, then by what means is this very undefectiveness of the causes ascertained?

children.text: 1.11 tad yady aduṣṭakārakasandohotpādyatvenāvyabhicāritvaṃ, saiva kāraṇānām aduṣṭatā kenāvagamyate?

body.text: na pratyakṣeṇa, nayanakuśalāder atīndriyatvāt / nāpy anumānena, liṅgāntarānavagateḥ / nanv idam eva jñānaṃ lingaṃ tadutthaṃ tasya viśiṣṭatāṃ gamayati /
body.translated_text: Not by perception, because the skill of the eye and other factors are beyond sensory reach. Nor by inference, because no other inferential mark is apprehended. Objection: This very cognition is the inferential mark; being produced from those causes, it indicates their specific nature.

children.text: na pratyakṣeṇa, nayanakuśalāder atīndriyatvāt / nāpy anumānena, liṅgāntarānavagateḥ / nanv idam eva jñānaṃ lingaṃ tadutthaṃ tasya viśiṣṭatāṃ gamayati /

body.text: yady evam itaretarāśrayatvaṃ duruttaram āpanīpadyate /
body.translated_text: If so, then the fault of mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>), which is difficult to answer, is incurred.

children.text: yady evam itaretarāśrayatvaṃ duruttaram āpanīpadyate /

body.text: kiṃ cendriyāṇāṃ guṇadoṣāśrayatve tadutthe vijñāne doṣāśaṅkā nātivartate, puṃvyāpārotpāditaśabdavijñāneva /
body.translated_text: Moreover, since the sense organs are the locus of both merits and defects, the suspicion of defect in cognition arising from them is never overcome—just as with cognition of sound produced by human effort.

children.text: kiṃ cendriyāṇāṃ guṇadoṣāśrayatve tadutthe vijñāne doṣāśaṅkā nātivartate, puṃvyāpārotpāditaśabdavijñāna iva /

body.text: 1.12 atha bādhānutpattyāvyabhicāritvaṃ jñāyate, bādhānutpattir vijñānasya kiṃ yathārthagṛhītitvenāhosvid bādhakajñānotpādakakārakavaikalyād iti sandihmaḥ / dṛśyate hi bādhakajñānotpādakakārakavaikalyād bādhānutpādaḥ / yathā dūre marīcinicaye jalajñāne jāte bādhā na sampadyate, 'bhyāsadeśāvasthitasya kārakopanipāte saty utpadyate / sā copajāyamānā saṃvatsarādikālavikalpena sañjāyate / kadācic ca kārakavaikalyān naiva sampadyate / na caitāvatā tasya yathārthatopapadyate /
body.translated_text: [1.12] If non-errancy is known through the non-occurrence of sublation—we doubt whether the non-occurrence of sublation of a cognition is due to its having grasped the object correctly, or due to the deficiency of causal factors that would produce a sublating cognition. For it is observed that non-occurrence of sublation results from the deficiency of causal factors for the sublating cognition. For example, when the cognition of water arises regarding a distant collection of mirages, sublation does not occur; but it arises when causal factors present themselves to one stationed nearby. And that sublation, when it does arise, arises after a temporal interval of a year or the like. And sometimes, due to the deficiency of causal factors, it never occurs at all. Yet this alone does not establish the veridicality of that cognition.

children.text: 1.12 atha bādhānutpattyāvyabhicāritvaṃ jñāyate, bādhānutpattir vijñānasya kiṃ yathārthagṛhītitvenāhosvid bādhakajñānotpādakakārakavaikalyād iti sandihmaḥ / dṛśyate hi bādhakajñānotpādakakārakavaikalyād bādhānutpādaḥ / yathā dūre marīcinicaye jalajñāne jāte bādhā na sampadyate, 'bhyāsadeśāvasthitasya kārakopanipāte saty utpadyate / sā copajāyamānā saṃvatsarādikālavikalpena sañjāyate / kadācic ca kārakavaikalyān naiva sampadyate / na caitāvatā tasya yathārthatopapadyate /

body.text: api ca bādhāvirahaiva na bādhāsadbhāvāvedakas, tadupalabdhatvena tatsadbhāvopalabdheḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, the mere absence of sublation does not indicate the non-existence of sublation, since the existence of sublation is apprehended only when it is perceived.

children.text: api ca bādhāviraha eva na bādhāsadbhāvāvedakas, tadupalabdhatvena tatsadbhāvopalabdheḥ /

body.text: 1.12ānyac ca bādhāvirahaḥ kiṃ sarvapuruṣāpekṣayāhosvit pratipattrapekṣayā? tad yadi sarvapuruṣāpekṣayā tadvirahopya ... sarvajñāḥ syuḥ / bhavantu nāma sarve sarvajñāḥ, ko doṣaḥ? asarvajñavyavahārābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: [1.12a] Furthermore, is the absence of sublation relative to all persons or relative to the cognizer alone? If relative to all persons, then even their freedom from it ... they would all be omniscient. Let all be omniscient then—what fault? The unwanted consequence that the conduct of non-omniscient persons would cease.

children.text: 1.12a anyac ca bādhāvirahaḥ kiṃ sarvapuruṣāpekṣayāhosvit pratipattrapekṣayā? tad yadi sarvapuruṣāpekṣayā tadvirahopya ... sarvajñāḥ syuḥ / bhavantu nāma sarve sarvajñāḥ, ko doṣaḥ? asarvajñavyavahārābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /

body.text: atha pratipattrapekṣayā bādhānutpādaḥ  pratipattur bādhakaṃ vijñānaṃ notpadyate, tena tad avyabhicāri / tad ayuktaṃ, pratipattur bādhakajñānānutpāde 'pi deśāntaragamanamaraṇādinā maṇimarīcyādiviparyayajñānadarśanāt / athavā tad viparyayajñānaṃ tathāvidham evotpannaṃ svaprabhavasvabhāvānupraveśena, yad bādhakavijñānotpādapratibandhakṛt / taddhvaṃso 'pi tathābhataiva pareṣṭasamyagjñānavat / evaṃ sati yad uktaṃ yasya ca duṣṭaṃ karaṇaṃ yatra ca mithyeti pratyayaḥ saivāsamīcīnaḥ pratyayety etad evāsamīcīnam /
body.translated_text: If the non-occurrence of sublation is relative to the cognizer alone—the sublating cognition does not arise for the cognizer, therefore that original cognition is non-errant. This is unjustified, because even when no sublating cognition arises for the cognizer, erroneous cognition regarding gems, mirages, and the like is observed due to traveling to another place, death, and so on. Alternatively, that erroneous cognition, having arisen in just that manner, through the penetration of its own nature of origination, prevents the arising of sublating cognition. Its destruction too would be of the same nature, just like what opponents hold to be valid cognition. This being so, the statement 'one whose instrument is defective and whose cognition is erroneous—that alone is an incorrect cognition'—this itself is incorrect.

children.text: atha pratipattrapekṣayā bādhānutpādaḥ -- pratipattur bādhakaṃ vijñānaṃ notpadyate, tena tad avyabhicāri / tad ayuktaṃ, pratipattur bādhakajñānānutpāde 'pi deśāntaragamanamaraṇādinā maṇimarīcyādiviparyayajñānadarśanāt / athavā tad viparyayajñānaṃ tathāvidham evotpannaṃ svaprabhavasvabhāvānupraveśena, yad bādhakavijñānotpādapratibandhakṛt / taddhvaṃso 'pi tathābhata eva pareṣṭasamyagjñānavat / evaṃ sati yad uktaṃ yasya ca duṣṭaṃ karaṇaṃ yatra ca mithyeti pratyayaḥ sa evāsamīcīnaḥ pratyaya ity etad evāsamīcīnam /

body.text: 1.13 atha pravṛttisāmarthyenāvyabhicāritāṃ vetsi / pravṛttisāmarthyaṃ phalenābhisambandhaḥ, phalaṃ ca srakcandanavanitodakādi, teṣu satyaphalaniṣpattes teṣu phalopacāras, taddehasambandhaḥ pravṛttisāmarthyam / pravṛttiḥ kāyasthā kriyā, tatsāmarthyam avyabhicāritāṃ gamayati / tat kim avagatam anavagataṃ vā? yadi nāvagataṃ, tad astīti kathaṃ vetsi? athāvagataṃ, tadavagater avyabhicāritā katham avagamyateti pūrvoktam anusartavyam /
body.translated_text: [1.13] If you claim non-errancy through the capacity for successful activity—the capacity for successful activity is the connection with a result; the result is a garland, sandalwood, butter, water, and the like; since in their case the real result is accomplished, the designation of 'result' applies to them; the connection with that body is the capacity for successful activity. Activity is bodily action; its capacity indicates non-errancy. Is that capacity known or unknown? If unknown, how do you know that it exists? If known, then how is the non-errancy of the cognition of that capacity ascertained?—the previously stated argument must be followed.

children.text: 1.13 atha pravṛttisāmarthyenāvyabhicāritāṃ vetsi / pravṛttisāmarthyaṃ phalenābhisambandhaḥ, phalaṃ ca srakcandanavanitodakādi, teṣu satyaphalaniṣpattes teṣu phalopacāras, taddehasambandhaḥ pravṛttisāmarthyam / pravṛttiḥ kāyasthā kriyā, tatsāmarthyam avyabhicāritāṃ gamayati / tat kim avagatam anavagataṃ vā? yadi nāvagataṃ, tad astīti kathaṃ vetsi? athāvagataṃ, tadavagater avyabhicāritā katham avagamyata iti pūrvoktam anusartavyam /

body.text: 1.13odakaprāptyā pūrvotpannodakavijñānasyāvyabhicāritā vyavasthāpyate / kiṃ tatpratibhātodakaprāptyāhosvit tajjātīyodakaprāptyā tadvaṃśajajalaprāptyā vā?
body.translated_text: Is the non-errancy of a previously arisen water-cognition established by the attainment of water? Is it by the attainment of that very water that appeared in cognition, or by the attainment of water of the same kind, or by the attainment of water belonging to that lineage?

children.text: 1.13a udakaprāptyā pūrvotpannodakavijñānasyāvyabhicāritā vyavasthāpyate / kiṃ tatpratibhātodakaprāptyāhosvit tajjātīyodakaprāptyā tadvaṃśajajalaprāptyā vā?

body.text: 1.13a tad yadi pratibhātodakaprāptyā, tad ayuktam / pratibhātodakasyāvasthānaṃ nopapadyate, jhaṣamahiṣaparivartanābhighātopajātāvayavakriyānyāyena pratyastamayasambhavāt /
body.translated_text: [1.13a] If by the attainment of that very water that appeared—this is unjustified. The persistence of the water that appeared in cognition is not established, because its disappearance is possible through the principle that parts undergo change from the impact of the movements of fish, buffaloes, and the like.

children.text: 1.13a1 tad yadi pratibhātodakaprāptyā, tad ayuktam / pratibhātodakasyāvasthānaṃ nopapadyate, jhaṣamahiṣaparivartanābhighātopajātāvayavakriyānyāyena pratyastamayasambhavāt /

body.text: 1.13a atha tajjātīyodakaprāptyā, evaṃ tarhy asatyodakajñāne 'pi jate kvacit toyam āsādayanti pumāṃsaḥ / tad apy avitathaṃ syāt / atha taddeśakālasaṃlagnam udakaṃ na prāpayati mithyājñānaṃ, samyagjñānaṃ tu taddeśakālasaṃlagnam udakaṃ prāpayati, tena tad avyabhicārīti ced,
body.translated_text: If by the attainment of water of the same kind—then even when a false water-cognition arises, people sometimes encounter water elsewhere. That too would be non-erroneous. If you say: false cognition does not lead to water connected with that place and time, while valid cognition leads to water connected with that place and time, and therefore it is non-errant—

children.text: 1.13a2 atha tajjātīyodakaprāptyā, evaṃ tarhy asatyodakajñāne 'pi jate kvacit toyam āsādayanti pumāṃsaḥ / tad apy avitathaṃ syāt / atha taddeśakālasaṃlagnam udakaṃ na prāpayati mithyājñānaṃ, samyagjñānaṃ tu taddeśakālasaṃlagnam udakaṃ prāpayati, tena tad avyabhicārīti ced,

body.text: yan na prāpayati, tad vyabhicāri; tarhi mumarṣupadā jñānaṃ candrārkagrahanakṣatratārakādisaṃvedanaṃ ca vyabhicāri prāpnoti / na ca taddeśakālasaṃlagnodakaprāpakatvam asti, deśasyāpy udakavad vināśasambhavāt /
body.translated_text: what does not lead to the object is errant; then the cognition of a dying person, and the perception of moon, sun, planets, constellations, and stars would also be errant. Nor is there the capacity to lead to water connected with that place and time, since the place too, like water, is subject to destruction.

children.text: yan na prāpayati, tad vyabhicāri; tarhi mumarṣupadā jñānaṃ candrārkagrahanakṣatratārakādisaṃvedanaṃ ca vyabhicāri prāpnoti / na ca taddeśakālasaṃlagnodakaprāpakatvam asti, deśasyāpy udakavad vināśasambhavāt /

body.text: a. na ca jāteḥsambhavo 'sti / saiva katham? kathyate  sodakavyaktibhyo 'bhinnā bhinnā bhinnābhinnā veti /
body.translated_text: Nor is the existence of a universal (<s>jāti</s>) possible. How is that so? It is asked: is the universal identical with the individual instances of water, different from them, or both identical and different?

children.text: a. na ca jāteḥsambhavo 'sti / sa eva katham? kathyate -- sodakavyaktibhyo 'bhinnā bhinnā bhinnābhinnā veti /

body.text: a.1 tad yadi tādātmyavyavasthitā, tadeha tāsāṃ nānātvena tasyāpi nānātvopapattiḥ / tadekatve ca sarvāsām ekatāpattiḥ / ekatve ca niḥsāmānyatā tādātmyaviparyāso vā /
body.translated_text: [a.1] If it is established as identical with the particulars, then since those particulars are many, its plurality too would follow. And if it is one, the oneness of all particulars would follow. And in oneness, there would be the absence of universality, or a reversal of identity.

children.text: a.1 tad yadi tādātmyavyavasthitā, tadeha tāsāṃ nānātvena tasya āpi nānātvopapattiḥ / tadekatve ca sarvāsām ekatāpattiḥ / ekatve ca niḥsāmānyatā tādātmyaviparyāso vā /

body.text: a.2 athārthāntarabhūtā sā vyāvṛttākārānugatākārā vā /
body.translated_text: [a.2] Or if it is a separate entity, is it of an exclusive form or of a pervading form?

children.text: a.2 athārthāntarabhūtā sā vyāvṛttākārānugatākārā vā /

body.text: tad yadi vyāvṛttākārā, na tasyāḥ sāmānyarūpatvaṃ vyāvṛttaikasvabhāvatvāt toyādivat / athānusyūtarūpā, tat kim ātmarūpānusyūtā pararūpānusyūtā vā?
body.translated_text: If of exclusive form, then it cannot have the nature of a universal, because it has a single exclusive nature, like water and the like. If of pervading form, then is it pervading by its own form or pervading by the form of others?

children.text: tad yadi vyāvṛttākārā, na tasyāḥ sāmānyarūpatvaṃ vyāvṛttaikasvabhāvatvāt toyādivat / athānusyūtarūpā, tat kim ātmarūpānusyūtā pararūpānusyūtā vā?

body.text: tad yady ātmarūpānusyūtā, tad ayuktam, ātmany anugamābhāvāt / atha pararūpānusyūtā, keyaṃ pararūpānusyūtatā kiṃ tattādātmyaṃ tatsamavāyo vā?
body.translated_text: If pervading by its own form, this is unjustified, since there is no pervasion within itself. If pervading by the form of others, what is this pervasion by the form of others—is it identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) with them or inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) with them?

children.text: tad yady ātmarūpānusyūtā, tad ayuktam, ātmany anugamābhāvāt / atha pararūpānusyūtā, keyaṃ pararūpānusyūtatā kiṃ tattādātmyaṃ tatsamavāyo vā?

body.text: tad yadi tādātmyaṃ, sāmānyatadvator abhedaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: If identity, then the unwanted consequence of non-difference between the universal and its possessor follows.

children.text: tad yadi tādātmyaṃ, sāmānyatadvator abhedaprasaṅgaḥ /

body.text: atha pararūpasamavāyo 'nusyūtākāratā, tad ayuktam / sāmānyād bhinnaḥ samavāyaḥ / sāmānyasyānugataṃ rūpam ālocayitum ārabdhaṃ, na tato 'nyasya /
body.translated_text: If the pervading form consists in inherence with the form of others, this is unjustified. Inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) is different from the universal. We began to examine the pervading form of the universal, not of something else.

children.text: atha pararūpasamavāyo 'nusyūtākāratā, tad ayuktam / sāmānyād bhinnaḥ samavāyaḥ / sāmānyasyānugataṃ rūpam ālocayitum ārabdhaṃ, na tato 'nyasya /

body.text: a.2a yadi codakajātīyārthaprāptyāvyabhicāritā pūrvoditodakavijñānasya vyavasthāpyate, tadodakajāter gavādāv api sambhavo 'sti, gavādiprāptyāvyabhicāritodakavijñānasya syāt / athodakatvasya gavādāv abhāveti cet, kim itaretarābhāvaḥ prāgabhāvaḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvo 'tyantābhāvo vā?
body.translated_text: [a.2a] If the non-errancy of the previously mentioned water-cognition is established by the attainment of an object belonging to the water-class, then since the water-universal can exist in cows and the like too, the water-cognition would be non-errant through the attainment of cows and the like. If you say waterness is absent in cows and the like, then what kind of absence is it—mutual absence, prior absence, absence through destruction, or absolute absence?

children.text: a.2a yadi codakajātīyārthaprāptyāvyabhicāritā pūrvoditodakavijñānasya vyavasthāpyate, tadodakajāter gavādāv api sambhavo 'sti, gavādiprāptyāvyabhicāritodakavijñānasya syāt / athodakatvasya gavādāv abhāva iti cet, kim itaretarābhāvaḥ prāgabhāvaḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvo 'tyantābhāvo vā?

body.text: tad yadītaretarābhāvas tadodakādāv api samānam udakatvasyābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / udakarūpatā nodakatvasyodakatvarūpatā ca nodakasyal /
body.translated_text: If mutual absence, then the unwanted consequence is that waterness would be equally absent in water and the like too. The form of water is not waterness, and the form of waterness is not water.

children.text: tad yadītaretarābhāvas tadodakādāv api samānam udakatvasyābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / udakarūpatā nodakatvasyodakatvarūpatā ca nodakasyal /

body.text: atha prāgabhāvas tadodake 'py udakatvasyābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: If prior absence, then the unwanted consequence is that waterness would also be absent in water itself.

children.text: atha prāgabhāvas tadodake 'py udakatvasyābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /

body.text: atha pradhvaṃsābhāvas tadodake 'py abhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: If absence through destruction, then too the unwanted consequence of absence in water follows.

children.text: atha pradhvaṃsābhāvas tadodake 'py abhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /

body.text: athānyatrāsti, naikatra pratyastamitasyānyatra sambhavopapadyate /
body.translated_text: If it exists elsewhere, it is not established that what has disappeared in one place can exist in another.

children.text: athānyatrāsti, naikatra pratyastamitasyānyatra sambhava upapadyate /

body.text: athātyantābhāvas tadodake 'pi tasyābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: If absolute absence, then the unwanted consequence is its absence in water too.

children.text: athātyantābhāvas tadodake 'pi tasyābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ /

body.text: atha sambandhābhāvād gavādāv udakatvābhāveti cet, tatrāpi kim itaretarābhāvaḥ prāgabhāvaḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvo 'tyantābhāvo veti pūrvavad vaktavyam / nimittāntarābhāvād gavādāv udakatvābhāveti cet, so 'trāpi samānaḥ /
body.translated_text: If you say waterness is absent in cows and the like due to the absence of a connection, then regarding that absence too the same must be asked as before: is it mutual absence, prior absence, absence through destruction, or absolute absence? If you say waterness is absent in cows and the like due to the absence of another cause, the same problem applies here too.

children.text: atha sambandhābhāvād gavādāv udakatvābhāva iti cet, tatrāpi kim itaretarābhāvaḥ prāgabhāvaḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvo 'tyantābhāvo veti pūrvavad vaktavyam / nimittāntarābhāvād gavādāv udakatvābhāva iti cet, so 'trāpi samānaḥ /

body.text: a.2b na codakavyaktīnāṃ nānātvam upapādayituṃ pāryate / udakam anudakākārād udakākāratayā vyāvartata, udakākārāt tu kathaṃ vyāvartate? kim udakākāratayāhosvid ākārāntareṇa?
body.translated_text: [a.2b] Nor can the plurality of water-particulars be established. Water is distinguished from non-water by virtue of having the form of water; but from another water-form, how is it distinguished? By having the form of water, or by a different form?

children.text: a.2b na codakavyaktīnāṃ nānātvam upapādayituṃ pāryate / udakam anudakākārād udakākāratayā vyāvartata, udakākārāt tu kathaṃ vyāvartate? kim udakākāratayāhosvid ākārāntareṇa?

body.text: tad yady udakākāratayā vyāvartate, tadānyāsām udakavyaktīnām anudakākāratā prāpnoti rasāder iva /
body.translated_text: If it is distinguished by having the form of water, then the other water-particulars would have a non-water form, just like taste and the like.

children.text: tad yady udakākāratayā vyāvartate, tadānyāsām udakavyaktīnām anudakākāratā prāpnoti rasāder iva /

body.text: athānudakākāratayodakākārān nivartate, tato dahanāder ivānudakatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, if it removes water-forms by being of non-water form, then there would be the unwanted consequence that it is non-water, like fire and such.

children.text: athānudakākāratayodakākārān nivartate, tato dahanāder ivānudakatvaprasaṅgaḥ /

body.text:
athodakākārarūpatāviśeṣe 'py avāntaragaṇikākārabhedaparikḹptir iti cet, satyam avāntaragaṇikākāras toyatādātmyavyavasthito 'tādātmyavyavasthito vā / tad yadi tādātmyavyavasthitas, tadodakākāratayodakāntarād bhidyate / evaṃ cānyāsām udakavyaktīnām anudakarūpatā prāpnoti / pūrvoditam eva dūṣaṇam / athātādātmyavyavasthitas, tarhy anudakatvaṃ rasāder iva / athodakatvavyāvṛttyānudakākārād vyāvartate / śṛṇvantv amī bālalapitaṃ vipaścitaḥ / yady udakatvavyāvṛttyānudakād vyāvartate toyam, udakatvaṃ codakād anudakāc ca kathaṃ vyāvartate? na jātyantaraṃ vyāvartakam asti / abhyupagame vāniṣṭhopaplavānubandhaḥ syāt / tasmāt svenaiva rūpeṇetaretarātmanā vyāvartate, na jātyādinā vyāvartate, jātyāder avyāvṛttiprasaṅgāt / tasmāt sthitam etan nodakavyaktīnāṃ nānātvopapattiḥ
/ tadanupapattau nodakatvaṃ nāma sāmānyam asti svatvavat /
body.translated_text: If it is said that even though there is no distinction in having water-form, the distinction of subsidiary particular forms is constructed — true; is the subsidiary particular form established as identical with waterness or as non-identical? If established as identical, then it differs from other water by being of water-form, and thus the other water-instances would have non-water form — the same refutation as stated before. If established as non-identical, then it is non-water, like taste and such. Or if water is distinguished from non-water-form by the exclusion of waterness — let the wise hear this childish prattle! If water is distinguished from non-water by the exclusion of waterness, then how is waterness itself distinguished from water and non-water? There is no other universal to serve as the distinguisher. Or if one admits another, there would follow an infinite regress. Therefore, things are distinguished by their own form, by their mutual nature, not by universals etc., because universals etc. would themselves not be distinguished. Therefore it is established: the plurality of water-instances is not proven. And when that is not proven, there is no universal called 'waterness,' just as there is no universal called 'own-ness.'

/ tadanupapattau nodakatvaṃ nāma sāmānyam asti svatvavat /

body.text: a.2c ito 'pi na vidyate sāmānyaṃ  nityasya sato vijñānajanakatvāyogāt / tad eva katham? vyutpādyate vijñānajanakāvasthāyāṃ yad eva svarūpaṃ sāmānyātmakaṃ śaktimac chaktirūpaṃ ca kārakāntarānapekṣayājanakāvasthāyāṃ tad eva rūpam, ataḥ pūrvam api kāryotpādaprasaṅgaḥ / anutpāde vā prāg ivedānīm api na janayet /
body.translated_text: Moreover, universals do not exist because a permanent entity cannot be the cause of cognition. How is that? It is explained: the very nature that exists in the state of producing cognition — being of the nature of a universal, possessing capacity and being of the nature of capacity — without dependence on other causal factors, is the same form in the state of not producing. Therefore, there would be the unwanted consequence of the effect being produced even before the auxiliary causes come together. Or if it does not produce then, it would not produce now either, just as before.

children.text: a.2c ito 'pi na vidyate sāmānyaṃ -- nityasya sato vijñānajanakatvāyogāt / tad eva katham? vyutpādyate vijñānajanakāvasthāyāṃ yad eva svarūpaṃ sāmānyātmakaṃ śaktimac chaktirūpaṃ ca kārakāntarānapekṣaya ājanakāvasthāyāṃ tad eva rūpam, ataḥ pūrvam api kāryotpādaprasaṅgaḥ / anutpāde vā prāg ivedānīm api na janayet /

body.text: atha kārakāntaram apekṣyotpādayati kāryam / kiṃ tena kārakāntareṇa tasya kriyate kārakatvaṃ jñāpyate vā?
body.translated_text: Now, if it is said that it produces the effect depending on another causal factor — does that other causal factor create its causality or merely reveal it?

children.text: atha kārakāntaram apekṣyotpādayati kāryam / kiṃ tena kārakāntareṇa tasya kriyate kārakatvaṃ jñāpyate vā?

body.text: tad yady utpādyate susthitaṃ nityatvam / uta jñāpyate siddhaṃ tarhi kārakatvaṃ, tadabhāve 'pi vidyamānasyāvadyotanāt / bhavatu nāma kārakatvaṃ, ko doṣaḥ? kāryotpattiprasaṅgaḥ / atha kārakatve 'pi kāryaṃ na janayed, aho rājājñā garīyasī naiyāyikapaśoḥ /
body.translated_text: If the causality is produced, then its permanence is well undermined. Or if it is merely revealed, then the causality is already established, since even in the absence of the auxiliary cause, it exists without being manifested. Let there be causality — what is the fault? The unwanted consequence of the effect being produced even without auxiliary causes. If even with causality it does not produce the effect — ah, how weighty is the royal decree of the <s>Naiyāyika</s> beast!

children.text: tad yady utpādyate susthitaṃ nityatvam / uta jñāpyate siddhaṃ tarhi kārakatvaṃ, tadabhāve 'pi vidyamānasyāvadyotanāt / bhavatu nāma kārakatvaṃ, ko doṣaḥ? kāryotpattiprasaṅgaḥ / atha kārakatve 'pi kāryaṃ na janayed, aho rājājñā garīyasī naiyāyikapaśoḥ /

body.text: a.2d ito 'pi nāsti sāmānyaṃ  tadupapādakamānavyatirekāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, universals do not exist because of the absence of a means of knowledge that establishes them through <s>anvaya-vyatireka</s> (agreement and difference).

children.text: a.2d ito 'pi nāsti sāmānyaṃ -- tadupapādakamānavyatirekāt /

body.text: nanv asti pramāṇamanayoḥ sādṛśyam, eṣāṃ sārūpyaṃ, tena sadṛśo 'yam, asau vā tena sadṛśetyādijñānaṃ sāmānyasattāvabodhakam apratipannasāmānyasya nopapadyate / asti tv idaṃ vijñānaṃ bādhāvikalaṃ jātitanuvyavasthāpakam / tad etad ayuktam / kiṃ nimittabhūtena tenaivaṃvidhaṃ jñānam utpādyate karmatāpannena vā?
body.translated_text: Objection: There is a means of knowledge — similarity. The similarity of these, the cognition that 'this is similar to that' or 'that is similar to this,' reveals the existence of a universal and is not possible for one who has not apprehended a universal. But this cognition, being uncontradicted, establishes the relation of <s>jāti</s> (universal) and <s>vyakti</s> (particular). This is not correct. Is such cognition produced by the universal being the efficient cause, or by it being the object?

children.text: nanv asti pramāṇamanayoḥ sādṛśyam, eṣāṃ sārūpyaṃ, tena sadṛśo 'yam, asau vā tena sadṛśa ityādijñānaṃ sāmānyasattāvabodhakam apratipannasāmānyasya nopapadyate / asti tv idaṃ vijñānaṃ bādhāvikalaṃ jātitanuvyavasthāpakam / tad etad ayuktam / kiṃ nimittabhūtena tenaivaṃvidhaṃ jñānam utpādyate karmatāpannena vā?

body.text: tad yadi nimittabhūtenotpādyate, tadā na sāmānyaṃ kalpanīyam / asāmānyātmakam eva nimittam, itthambhūtasāmānyajñānotpādanāyālaṃ sāmānyakalpanayā /
body.translated_text: If it is produced by it being the efficient cause, then a universal need not be postulated. The cause itself, which is not of the nature of a universal, is sufficient for producing the cognition of universals of this sort — there is no need for postulating a universal.

children.text: tad yadi nimittabhūtenotpādyate, tadā na sāmānyaṃ kalpanīyam / asāmānyātmakam eva nimittam, itthambhūtasāmānyajñānotpādanāyālaṃ sāmānyakalpanayā /

body.text: atha karmatāpannenotpādyate, tad asat / naivāvabhāti vijñāne sāmānyaṃ dhūrtair aviparyāsitasaṃvidām / nanu sādṛśyam avabhāti / satyam, avabhāti, nāpahnūyate, 'pi tu dravyaguṇakarmātmakaṃ sat pācakādibhedeṣu yathaiṣāṃ pācakatvam, ete pācakās, tatpācakasadṛśo 'yam, asāv anena sadṛśeti viśeṣādāv api draṣṭavyam / atrāpi sāmānyaparijñaptir iti cen, na sūtravyāghātāt sāmānyaviśeṣeṣu sāmānyaviśeṣābhāvāt tataiva jñānam / aniṣṭhā ca viśeṣeṣu sāmānye parikalpyamāne sati sandehaḥ, sati sandehe teṣu viśeṣāntaraṃ parikalpanīyaṃ, punaḥ sāmānyam ity aniṣṭhety alam asadgrahābhiniveśena /
body.translated_text: If it is produced by the universal being the object — that is not so. A universal does not appear in cognition for those whose awareness has not been corrupted by rogues. Objection: Similarity does appear. True, it appears, it is not denied. But being of the nature of substance, quality, and action, it should be understood in distinctions such as 'cook' etc. — just as 'these are cooks,' 'this is similar to that cook,' 'that is similar to this' — it should be seen even in particular things. If you say that there too is the apprehension of a universal — no, because of the contradiction with your own rule, since in universals and particulars there are no further universals and particulars; knowledge arises from them directly. And there is an infinite regress: if a universal is postulated in particulars, there is doubt; if there is doubt, another particular must be postulated in them, then again a universal — thus an infinite regress. Enough with clinging to false beliefs!

children.text: atha karmatāpannenotpādyate, tad asat / naivāvabhāti vijñāne sāmānyaṃ dhūrtair aviparyāsitasaṃvidām / nanu sādṛśyam avabhāti / satyam, avabhāti, nāpahnūyate, 'pi tu dravyaguṇakarmātmakaṃ sat pācakādibhedeṣu yathaiṣāṃ pācakatvam, ete pācakās, tatpācakasadṛśo 'yam, asāv anena sadṛśa iti viśeṣādāv api draṣṭavyam / atrāpi sāmānyaparijñaptir iti cen, na sūtravyāghātāt sāmānyaviśeṣeṣu sāmānyaviśeṣābhāvāt tata eva jñānam / aniṣṭhā ca viśeṣeṣu sāmānye parikalpyamāne sati sandehaḥ, sati sandehe teṣu viśeṣāntaraṃ parikalpanīyaṃ, punaḥ sāmānyam ity aniṣṭhety alam asadgrahābhiniveśena /

body.text: a.3 atha bhinnābhinnaṃ sāmānyaṃ bhavadbhiḥ pratipādyata  ākārabhedena vyaktibhyopalabhyatety arthāntaraṃ, deśabhedena tu naivopalabhyatety avyatiriktam / tad etan mahāsubhāṣitam / na deśabhedenaiva vastūnāṃ bhedo, 'pi tv ākārabhedenaiva bhāvā bhedam upayānti / yathā cākārabhedo nāsti tathānantaram eva niveditam /
body.translated_text: Now, is a universal that is both different and non-different from its instances being taught by you? It is perceived as something different from particulars by difference in form, but it is not perceived as different by difference in location, hence non-different. This is a great saying indeed! Things are not differentiated only by difference in location; rather, entities are differentiated precisely by difference in form. And how there is no difference in form has been stated immediately before.

children.text: a.3 atha bhinnābhinnaṃ sāmānyaṃ bhavadbhiḥ pratipādyata -- ākārabhedena vyaktibhya upalabhyata ity arthāntaraṃ, deśabhedena tu naivopalabhyata ity avyatiriktam / tad etan mahāsubhāṣitam / na deśabhedenaiva vastūnāṃ bhedo, 'pi tv ākārabhedenaiva bhāvā bhedam upayānti / yathā cākārabhedo nāsti tathānantaram eva niveditam /

body.text: b. sāmānyaṃ samavāyavṛttyā vyaktiṣu vartateti na cāsau vidyate /
body.translated_text: It is claimed that a universal exists in particulars through the relation of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) — but that inherence does not exist.

children.text: b. sāmānyaṃ samavāyavṛttyā vyaktiṣu vartata iti na cāsau vidyate /

body.text: b.1 samavāyo hi vyāvṛttaikasvabhāvo 'nugataikasvabhāvo vā / tad yadi vyāvṛttaikasvabhāvaḥ, kasyāsau samavāyaḥ sarvato vyāvṛtter nīlādivat? athānugataikasvabhāvaḥ, sāmānyaṃ tarhi, na samavāyo, nityasya sato 'nekatra vṛtter gotvādivat /
body.translated_text: For <s>samavāya</s> has either a unique nature that is exclusive or a unique nature that pervades all instances. If of exclusive nature, then whose inherence is it, since being excluded from everything it would be like blue etc.? If of pervading nature, then it is a universal, not inherence, since being permanent and subsisting in many, it would be like <s>gotva</s> (cowness) etc.

children.text: b.1 samavāyo hi vyāvṛttaikasvabhāvo 'nugataikasvabhāvo vā / tad yadi vyāvṛttaikasvabhāvaḥ, kasyāsau samavāyaḥ sarvato vyāvṛtter nīlādivat? athānugataikasvabhāvaḥ, sāmānyaṃ tarhi, na samavāyo, nityasya sato 'nekatra vṛtter gotvādivat /

body.text: b.2 upapādakapramāṇābhāvāc ca /
body.translated_text: And also because of the absence of a means of knowledge that establishes it.

children.text: b.2 upapādakapramāṇābhāvāc ca /

body.text: b.21 nanu pratyakṣabuddhyavaseyo 'sau / tad ayuktam / kiṃ sambandhabuddhyādhyavasīyatāhosvid ihabuddhyā samavāyabuddhyā vocyate?
body.translated_text: Objection: It is ascertained by perceptual cognition. That is not correct. Is it ascertained by a cognition of relation, or by a cognition of 'hereness,' or by a cognition of inherence?

children.text: b.21 nanu pratyakṣabuddhyavaseyo 'sau / tad ayuktam / kiṃ sambandhabuddhyādhyavasīyatā ahosvid ihabuddhyā samavāyabuddhyā vocyate?

body.text: b.211 tad yadi sambandhabuddhyā, ko 'yaṃ sambandhaḥ?
body.translated_text: If by a cognition of relation — what is this relation?

children.text: b.211 tad yadi sambandhabuddhyā, ko 'yaṃ sambandhaḥ?

body.text: kiṃ sambandhajātiyuktaḥ sambandhāhosvid anekopādānajanito 'nekāśrito vā sambandhabuddhiviśeṣo vā sambandhabuddhyutpādako vā sambandhākāro vā?
body.translated_text: Is it a relation possessing the universal of relation, or a relation produced by multiple causes, or one subsisting in multiple loci, or a specific cognition that produces cognition of relation, or one that is ascertained by cognition of relation, or the form of relation?

children.text: kiṃ sambandhajātiyuktaḥ sambandhā ahosvid anekopādānajanito 'nekāśrito vā sambandhabuddhiviśeṣo vā sambandhabuddhyutpādako vā sambandhākāro vā?

body.text: tad yadi sambandhajātiyuktas te sambandhaḥ, so 'nupapannaḥ, samavāyāsambandhatvaprasaṅgaḥ / athānekopādānajanitaḥ sambandhas, tadā kumbhāder api sambandhatvaprasaṅgaḥ / athānekāśritaḥ sambandhas, tadā ghaṭajātyādeḥ sambandhatvaṃ prasajyate / atha sambandhabuddhyutpādakas te sambandhocyate, tadā locanāder api sambandhatvaprasaṅgaḥ / atha sambandhabuddhyavaseyaḥ sambandho 'bhidhīyate, tadā kauleyakakarikumārādiṣv api sambandhaśabdavyutpādane sambandhatvaprasaṅgaḥ / sambandhetarayor ekavijñānaviṣayatvetarasya sambandharūpatā prāptā /
body.translated_text: If your relation possesses the universal of relation, that is untenable, for there would be the unwanted consequence that <s>samavāya</s> is not a relation. If a relation is produced by multiple causes, then a pot etc. would also be a relation. If a relation subsists in multiple loci, then <s>jāti</s> (universal) etc. would be a relation. If what you call a relation produces cognition of relation, then the eye etc. would also be relations. If what is called a relation is ascertained by cognition of relation, then in the case of a puppy, a she-donkey, a boy, etc., when the word 'relation' is applied, they too would be relations. When two relata and one other become objects of a single cognition, that other attains the status of relation.

children.text: tad yadi sambandhajātiyuktas te sambandhaḥ, so 'nupapannaḥ, samavāyāsambandhatvaprasaṅgaḥ / athānekopādānajanitaḥ sambandhas, tadā kumbhāder api sambandhatvaprasaṅgaḥ / athānekāśritaḥ sambandhas, tadā ghaṭajātyādeḥ sambandhatvaṃ prasajyate / atha sambandhabuddhyutpādakas te sambandha ucyate, tadā locanāder api sambandhatvaprasaṅgaḥ / atha sambandhabuddhyavaseyaḥ sambandho 'bhidhīyate, tadā kauleyakakarikumārādiṣv api sambandhaśabdavyutpādane sambandhatvaprasaṅgaḥ / sambandhetarayor ekavijñānaviṣayatva itarasya sambandharūpatā prāptā /

body.text: atha sambandhākāraḥ sambandhaḥ, saṃyogābhedaprasaṅgaḥ / avāntaragaṇikākāras tu yathā na bhedakas tathā purastād uktam eva dūṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: If the form of relation is the relation, there would be the unwanted consequence of non-difference from <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction). And that the subsidiary particular form is not a differentiator has been stated before as a refutation.

children.text: atha sambandhākāraḥ sambandhaḥ, saṃyogābhedaprasaṅgaḥ / avāntaragaṇikākāras tu yathā na bhedakas tathā purastād uktam eva dūṣaṇam /

body.text: b.212 atheha tantuṣu paṭetīhabuddhyādhyavasīyate, nehabuddher adhikaraṇasaṃvidrūpatvāt / na cānyasminn ākāre pratīyamāne 'nyat parikalpayituṃ nyāyyam atiprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: If it is ascertained by the 'here'-cognition, as in 'the cloth is here in the threads' — it is not [established], because the 'here'-cognition is of the nature of a cognition of locus. And it is not correct to postulate something else when something else is being perceived, due to overextension.

children.text: b.212 atheha tantuṣu paṭa itīhabuddhyādhyavasīyate, nehabuddher adhikaraṇasaṃvidrūpatvāt / na cānyasminn ākāre pratīyamāne 'nyat parikalpayituṃ nyāyyam atiprasaṅgāt /

body.text: b.213 atha samavāyabuddhyātmasātkriyate / so 'py anupapannaiva, samavāyabuddher anupapatteḥ / ayaṃ tantur ayaṃ paṭo 'yam anayoḥ samavāyeti na jātu jānate janāḥ /
body.translated_text: If it is apprehended through a cognition of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) — that too is untenable, because a cognition of inherence itself is not established. People never cognize: 'this is the thread, this is the cloth, and this is the inherence between them.'

children.text: b.213 atha samavāyabuddhyātmasātkriyate / so 'py anupapanna eva, samavāyabuddher anupapatteḥ / ayaṃ tantur ayaṃ paṭo 'yam anayoḥ samavāya iti na jātu jānate janāḥ /

body.text: b.22 athānumānenānumīyate / dve 'numāne  dṛṣṭaṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ ca / na dṛṣṭaṃ, pratyakṣavyatirekāt / sāmānyato drṣṭam api nāsti, tatprabhavakāryānupalabdheḥ / nanv ihabuddhir eva samavāyajñāpikā  iha tantuṣu paṭeti pratyayaḥ sambandhanimitto, 'bādhitehapratyayatvād iha kuṇḍe dadhīti pratyayavat / kim anenānumīyate? kiṃ nimittamātram uta sambandhaḥ?
body.translated_text: If it is inferred by inference — there are two kinds of inference: <s>dṛṣṭa</s> (based on observed cases) and <s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s> (based on general observation). Not <s>dṛṣṭa</s>, because of the absence of a distinct perceptual basis. Nor <s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s>, because no effect originating from it is apprehended. Objection: The 'here'-cognition itself indicates <s>samavāya</s> — the cognition 'the cloth is here in the threads' is caused by a relation, being an uncontradicted 'here'-cognition, like the cognition 'the curd is here in the pot.' What is inferred by this? Merely a cause, or a specific relation?

children.text: b.22 athānumānenānumīyate / dve 'numāne -- dṛṣṭaṃ sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ ca / na dṛṣṭaṃ, pratyakṣavyatirekāt / sāmānyato drṣṭam api nāsti, tatprabhavakāryānupalabdheḥ / nanv ihabuddhir eva samavāyajñāpikā -- iha tantuṣu paṭa iti pratyayaḥ sambandhanimitto, 'bādhitehapratyayatvād iha kuṇḍe dadhīti pratyayavat / kim anenānumīyate? kiṃ nimittamātram uta sambandhaḥ?

body.text: yadi nimittamātraṃ, tataḥ siddhasādhyatayā sambodhayitavyaḥ / atha sambandhaḥ, saṃyogaḥ samavāyo vā / saṃyogānumānopagamahāniḥ / samavāyānumāne sambandhavyatirekaḥ / na cānyasya sambandhe 'nyasya gamakatvam atiprasaṅgāt / na jātu devadattanayanakuṭasambandhe yajñadattendriyaṃ rūpādikam arthaṃ karaṇatvasāmyāt prakāśayad dṛṣṭam / evaṃ sati sāmānyasamavāyavirahe kathaṃ dravyādivyavastheti cintyate /
body.translated_text: If merely a cause, then one should be informed that it is already established, and you are proving what is already proven. If a relation, is it <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) or <s>samavāya</s> (inherence)? Admitting an inference of conjunction would be a loss for you. And in the inference of inherence, there is a deviation in the relation, for the establishment of one thing through something else in a relation is not valid, due to overextension. It is never observed that in <s>Devadatta</s>'s eye-mountain connection, <s>Yajñadatta</s>'s sense organ illuminates an object such as color etc., despite the equality of instrumentality. This being so, in the absence of universals and inherence, it is to be considered: how is the classification of substance etc. established?

children.text: yadi nimittamātraṃ, tataḥ siddhasādhyatayā sambodhayitavyaḥ / atha sambandhaḥ, saṃyogaḥ samavāyo vā / saṃyogānumāna upagamahāniḥ / samavāyānumāne sambandhavyatirekaḥ / na cānyasya sambandhe 'nyasya gamakatvam atiprasaṅgāt / na jātu devadattanayanakuṭasambandhe yajñadattendriyaṃ rūpādikam arthaṃ karaṇatvasāmyāt prakāśayad dṛṣṭam / evaṃ sati sāmānyasamavāyavirahe kathaṃ dravyādivyavastheti cintyate /

body.text: 1.13a atha tadvaṃśajajalaprāptyāvyabhicāritā jñāyate / tad ayuktam, antyāvayavidravyāṇāṃ janakatvavyatirekāt / na codakavyaktīnāṃ nānātvam asti / yathā ca na vidyate tathā niveditaṃ purastāt /
body.translated_text: Now, if the invariable concomitance is known through the obtaining of water of the same lineage — that is not correct, because of the absence of productivity in ultimate-atom substances. Nor is there plurality of water-instances. How there is none has been stated before.

children.text: 1.13a3 atha tadvaṃśajajalaprāptyāvyabhicāritā jñāyate / tad ayuktam, antyāvayavidravyāṇāṃ janakatvavyatirekāt / na codakavyaktīnāṃ nānātvam asti / yathā ca na vidyate tathā niveditaṃ purastāt /

body.text: 1.13b kiṃ ca pravṛttisāmarthyenāvyabhicāritā pūrvoditajñānasya jñāpyate  kiṃ liṅgabhūtenāho 'dhyakṣātmakena?
body.translated_text: Moreover, is the invariable concomitance of the aforementioned cognition known through the capacity for activity — by an inferential mark or by direct perception?

children.text: 1.13b kiṃ ca pravṛttisāmarthyenāvyabhicāritā pūrvoditajñānasya jñāpyate -- kiṃ liṅgabhūtenāho 'dhyakṣātmakena?

body.text: tad yadi liṅgabhūtena, tad ayuktaṃ, tena sākaṃ sambandhānavagateḥ / avagatau vālaṃ pravṛttisāmarthyena /
body.translated_text: If by an inferential mark, that is not correct, because the relation with it is not apprehended. Or if it is apprehended, then the capacity for activity is sufficient by itself.

children.text: tad yadi liṅgabhūtena, tad ayuktaṃ, tena sākaṃ sambandhānavagateḥ / avagatau vālaṃ pravṛttisāmarthyena /

body.text: athādhyakṣātmakena, tad ayuktaṃ, pūrvoditapratyastamitena sākaṃ sannikarṣābhāvāt / tadviṣayavijñānaṃ na pratyakṣaphalaṃ nirālambanatvāt keśoṇḍukādisaṃvedanavat / na vijñānasyābhāvo 'vabhāti, na bhāvas tadabhāvāt / avidyamānasya viṣayārtho vaktavyaḥ kim ākārārpakatvena vā mahattvādidharmopetatvena vā sattāmātreṇa vā sahotpādena vā? sarvasya pratyastamitatvāt katham asau viṣayaḥ? tadviṣayatve keśoṇḍukādivijñānasyaiva mithyātve bījam anveṣaṇīyam / ātmasattāmātreṇa mithyātve sarvasya mithyātvam āpadyate / tatas tattvopaplavaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: Now, if by means of perception—that is not proper, because there is no contact with what has previously arisen and subsequently ceased. The cognition of that object is not the fruit of perception, since it lacks a support (<s>nirālambana</s>), like the perception of hair-nets and the like. Neither the non-existence of cognition appears, nor its existence, since cognition itself is absent. For what does not exist, the meaning of 'object' must be stated: is it by imparting its form, by possessing properties like magnitude, by mere existence, or by simultaneous arising? Since everything has ceased, how can it be an object? If it is granted to be an object, the root of the falsity of cognitions like those of hair-nets must be sought. If falsity is merely by virtue of self-existence, everything would become false. Then there would be an upheaval of all principles (<s>tattvopaplava</s>).

children.text: athādhyakṣātmakena, tad ayuktaṃ, pūrvoditapratyastamitena sākaṃ sannikarṣābhāvāt / tadviṣayavijñānaṃ na pratyakṣaphalaṃ nirālambanatvāt keśoṇḍukādisaṃvedanavat / na vijñānasyābhāvo 'vabhāti, na bhāvas tadabhāvāt / avidyamānasya viṣayārtho vaktavyaḥ kim ākārārpakatvena vā mahattvādidharmopetatvena vā sattāmātreṇa vā sahotpādena vā? sarvasya pratyastamitatvāt katham asau viṣayaḥ? tadviṣayatve keśoṇḍukādivijñānasyaiva mithyātve bījam anveṣaṇīyam / ātmasattāmātreṇa mithyātve sarvasya mithyātvam āpadyate / tatas tattvopaplavaḥ syāt /

body.text: 1.14 athānyathāvyabhicāritvaṃ gṛhyatātmāntaḥkaraṇasambandhenotpannaṃ vijñānam avyabhicāritāviśiṣṭaṃ pradyotyate / tad ayuktam / tad avyabhicāritvaṃ taddharmo vā tatsvarūpaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: 1.14 Now let it be accepted that the non-erroneousness is illuminated—the cognition produced from the contact of the self with the internal organ, characterized by non-deviation (<s>avyabhicāritā</s>). That is not proper. Is that non-erroneousness its property or its essential nature?

children.text: 1.14 athānyathāvyabhicāritvaṃ gṛhyatā atmāntaḥkaraṇasambandhenotpannaṃ vijñānam avyabhicāritāviśiṣṭaṃ pradyotyate / tad ayuktam / tad avyabhicāritvaṃ taddharmo vā tatsvarūpaṃ vā /

body.text: 1.141 tad yadi taddharmaḥ, sa nityo 'nityo vā /
body.translated_text: 1.141 If it is its property, is it permanent or impermanent?

children.text: 1.141 tad yadi taddharmaḥ, sa nityo 'nityo vā /

body.text:
yadi nityas, tadā jātidoṣeṇāpodito veditavyaḥ / athānityaḥ, sa pūrvotpannaḥ saha paścād vā jātaḥ / tad yadi pūrvotpannas, tadā kasyāsau dharmaḥ? na hi dharmiṇam antareṇa dharmo bhavitum arhati / sarvato vyāvṛttarūpatvāt kaḥ kasyeti vaktavyam / atha sahotpannaḥ, kas tayoḥ sambandheti vaktavyam / tādātmyatadutpattisamavāyasambandhābhāve sati ṣaṣṭhyartho vaktavyas tasyāvyabhicāritvam ity atha pṛṣṭhotpannas tarhi pūrvaṃ vyabhicāritā vijñānasya prāpnoti / na cādhyātmiko 'vyabhicārirūpo dharmo 'sti sukhādivyatiriktas, tatpratītyasambhavena svayam anabhyupagamāt / yadi cāvyabhicārādayo dharmārthāntarabhūtābhyupagamyante tair avacchinnaṃ vijñānaṃ sāmagryāvasthāpakam udghuṣyate / tac cānupapannaṃ, pratyekamanekaviśeṣaṇāvacchinnavijñānapratipattikālāvasthānāyogāt / jñāpyajñāpakayor
abhāve kartṛmātraprabandhi jñānaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: If permanent, then it must be understood as refuted by the defect of universals (<s>jāti</s>). If impermanent, did it arise before, simultaneously, or after? If it arose before, then of what is it a property? For a property cannot exist without a property-bearer. Since its nature is excluded from everything, one must state 'which belongs to which.' If it arises simultaneously, one must state what the relation between the two is. In the absence of the relations of identity, causation, and inherence, the meaning of the genitive case in 'its non-erroneousness' must be explained. If it arises after, then the cognition would previously have the character of erroneousness. And there is no internal property in the form of non-erroneousness distinct from pleasure and the like, because the cognition of such is impossible, since it is not accepted by oneself. And if non-erroneousness and other properties are accepted as distinct entities, the cognition delimited by them is proclaimed to be the establisher of the aggregate. But that too is untenable, because at the time of cognizing the cognition delimited by multiple qualifiers, there is no possibility of each remaining individually present. In the absence of what is to be known and the knower, knowledge would depend on the knower alone.

body.text: 1.142 atha tatsvarūpam avyabhicāritvaṃ tat kiṃ svasattāmātrānurodhenārthāntarasattānurodhena vā?
body.translated_text: 1.142 Now if non-erroneousness is its essential nature, is it in accordance with its own mere existence or in accordance with the existence of something else?

children.text: 1.142 atha tatsvarūpam avyabhicāritvaṃ --tat kiṃ svasattāmātrānurodhenārthāntarasattānurodhena vā?

body.text:
tad yadi jñānasattāmātrataivāvyabhicāritvam ucyate, tadā keśoṇḍukasaṃvido'py avyabhicāritā syāt / na ca jñānasattāmātrānurodhena jñānaṃ vyabhicāry avyabhicāri vodgīyate / athārthāntarasattānurodhenāvyabhicāritvaṃ kim anupakārakārthāntarasattānurodhenāhosvid upakārakārthāntarasattānurodhena? tad yadi tāvad anupakārakārthāntarasattānurodhena, tadā keśoṇḍukendudvayasaṃvido 'py avyabhicāritāprasaṅgaḥ / athopakārakārthāntarasattānurodhenāvyabhicāritā kiṃ pratīyamānārthāntaropakārakasattānurodhena tadviparītārthāntaropakārakasattānurodhena vā? tad yadi pūrvapakṣābhyupagamas, tadātītānāgatānumānavijñānasya yogipratyakṣasya ca codanāvacanajanitavijñānasya vāvyabhicāritā na bhavet, tadavagatopakārakārthābhāvāt / bhāve vā vitānakriyālopaprasaṅgaḥ / athottaro matas, tadā
keśoṇḍukendudvayasaṃvido 'vyabhicāritvaṃ prasajyatety asadgṛhītam /
body.translated_text: If non-erroneousness is said to be merely the existence of cognition itself, then even the cognition of hair-nets would be non-erring. And cognition is not proclaimed as erring or non-erring merely in accordance with the existence of cognition. If non-erroneousness is in accordance with the existence of something else, is it in accordance with the existence of something else that is non-instrumental or in accordance with the existence of something else that is instrumental? If it is in accordance with the existence of something else that is non-instrumental, then the absurd consequence follows that even cognitions of hair-nets and double moons would be non-erring. If non-erroneousness is in accordance with the existence of something else that is instrumental, is it in accordance with the existence of what is instrumental to the perceived object, or in accordance with the existence of what is instrumental to the opposite object? If the former position is accepted, then the non-erroneousness of inferential cognition of past and future objects, of yogic perception, and of cognition born from injunctive statements would not obtain, because of the absence of the object perceived as instrumental. Or if it does obtain, the absurd consequence follows that purposeful activity would be rendered void. If the latter view is held, then the non-erroneousness of cognitions of hair-nets and double moons would absurdly follow—thus this is wrongly grasped.

body.text:
1.14a kiṃ ca tad vijñānam avyabhicāry avagataṃ sāmagryā jñāpakam anavagataṃ vā / yady avagataṃ tasyāvagatir ātmasaṃvidrūpā vā jñānāntaravedyā vā / tad yady ātmasaṃvedanarūpāvagatis, tad ayuktaṃ, svayam anabhyupagamāt / abhyupagame vopagamavirodhaḥ / atha jñānāntaravedyaṃ vetsi, vijñānayor bhede bījam anveṣṭavyam / jñanam ajñānākārāj jñānātmatayā vyāvartate, jñānāntarāt tu kathaṃ vyāvartate? kiṃ jñānātmatayā vyāvartatāhosvid ākārāntareṇa? tad yadi jñānātmatayā vyāvartate, tadānyasya jñānātmatā nivartate toyāder yathā / athākārāntareṇa, ākārāntarasvīkaraṇe jñānākāravirahaḥ syād, ākārayos tādātmyāyogāt / tādātmye vaikaṃ tad vastu jñānam ajñānaṃ vā / yadi jñānaṃ, na tarhy ākārāntareṇa vyāvartate, kiṃ tu jñānātmatayaiva / anyasyājñānātmakatvaprasaṭgaḥ
/ athājñānaṃ siddhaṃ naḥ samīhitam / atha jñānatvaṃ
vyāvartakaṃ, tat kena vyāvartateti pūrvoktam anusartavyam / vijñānāntaravedyam api na sambhavati / atha na vedyate, tad astīti kathaṃ punar vetsi?
body.translated_text: 1.14a Moreover, is that non-erring cognition apprehended by the aggregate as its indicator, or not apprehended? If apprehended, is the apprehension of it in the form of self-awareness or cognizable by another cognition? If the apprehension is in the form of self-awareness, that is not proper, since it is not accepted by oneself. Or if accepted, there is contradiction with one's own position. If you hold that it is cognizable by another cognition, the root of the difference between the two cognitions must be sought. Cognition is distinguished from what is not of the nature of cognition by virtue of its nature as cognition; but how is it distinguished from another cognition? Is it distinguished by its nature as cognition, or by some other form? If it is distinguished by its nature as cognition, then the other's nature as cognition would be negated, just as with water and the like. If by some other form, then in accepting another form, there would be the absence of the cognition-form, since the two forms cannot be identical. If they are identical, that entity is either cognition or non-cognition. If cognition, then it is not distinguished by another form, but precisely by its nature as cognition—and the absurd consequence follows that the other is not of the nature of cognition. If non-cognition, then what we desire is established. If cognition-ness is the distinguisher, then by what is it distinguished—the previously stated argument must be pursued. Cognizability by another cognition is also not possible. If it is not cognized, then how do you know that it exists?

1.14a kiṃ ca tad vijñānam avyabhicāry avagataṃ sāmagryā jñāpakam anavagataṃ vā / yady avagataṃ tasyāvagatir ātmasaṃvidrūpā vā jñānāntaravedyā vā / tad yady ātmasaṃvedanarūpāvagatis, tad ayuktaṃ, svayam anabhyupagamāt / abhyupagame vopagamavirodhaḥ / atha jñānāntaravedyaṃ vetsi, vijñānayor bhede bījam anveṣṭavyam / jñanam ajñānākārāj jñānātmatayā vyāvartate, jñānāntarāt tu kathaṃ vyāvartate? kiṃ jñānātmatayā vyāvartatā ahosvid ākārāntareṇa? tad yadi jñānātmatayā vyāvartate, tadānyasya jñānātmatā nivartate toyāder yathā / athākārāntareṇa, ākārāntarasvīkaraṇe jñānākāravirahaḥ syād, ākārayos tādātmyāyogāt / tādātmye vaikaṃ tad vastu jñānam ajñānaṃ vā / yadi jñānaṃ, na tarhy ākārāntareṇa vyāvartate, kiṃ tu jñānātmatayaiva / anyasyājñānātmakatvaprasaṭgaḥ
/ athājñānaṃ siddhaṃ naḥ samīhitam / atha jñānatvaṃ
vyāvartakaṃ, tat kena vyāvartata iti pūrvoktam anusartavyam / vijñānāntaravedyam api na sambhavati / atha na vedyate, tad astīti kathaṃ punar vetsi?

body.text: anenaiva vartmanā satyetaravijñānayor vibhāgābhāvo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ / ato 'vyabhicāripadam apārthakam /
body.translated_text: By this very path, it must be accepted that there is no distinction between true and false cognitions. Therefore the term 'non-erring' is meaningless.

children.text: anenaiva vartmanā satyetaravijñānayor vibhāgābhāvo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ / ato 'vyabhicāripadam apārthakam /

body.translated_text: 1.1e This too is meaningless, because it is already excluded by the phrase 'contact of sense-organ and object.' For cognition of hair-nets does not arise from the contact of the eye with an object.

body.text: tan na, yatodakaṃ pratibhāti, na ca tena saha sambandho 'sti / vidyamānena sākaṃ sambadhyate, nāvidyamānena / tatsambandhe vā na tadviṣayajñānasya mithyātvam ihopapadyate satyodakasaṃvedanavat /
body.translated_text: That is not so. What appears is water, and there is no contact with it. Contact occurs with what is present, not with what is absent. body.translated_text: with the heap of mirages, since that alone is the support (<s>ālambana</s>), because activity is directed toward that location. Hence the falsity: the support is one thing, and what appears is another.
