body.text: 1.1a ko 'yam ālambanārtho nāma yenedam udghuṣyate'nyad ālambanaṃ cānyat pratibhāti? kiṃ vijñānajanakatvam ākārārpakatvaṃ vijñānādhikaraṇatvaṃ vijñānāvabhāsitatā vā?
body.translated_text: 1.1a What is this meaning of 'support' (<s>ālambana</s>) by which it is proclaimed that 'the support is one thing and what appears is another'? Is it (1) being the cause of cognition, (2) imparting its form to cognition, (3) being the locus of cognition, or (4) being illuminated by cognition?

children.text: 1.1a1 ko 'yam ālambanārtho nāma yenedam udghuṣyate-'nyad ālambanaṃ cānyat pratibhāti? kiṃ vijñānajanakatvam ākārārpakatvaṃ vijñānādhikaraṇatvaṃ vijñānāvabhāsitatā vā?

body.text: tad yadi vijñānajanakatvam ālambanārthas, tadā nayanālokāder apy ālambanatvaṃ prasajyate / athākārārpakatvam ālambanatvaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, naiyāyikasamaye 'nabhyupagamāt / yathā ca viṣayākāro vijñāne na yujyate tathopariṣṭāt pratipādayiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the meaning of 'support' is being the cause of cognition, then even the eye, light, and other factors would absurdly become supports. If 'support' means imparting its form, that is not proper, since it is not accepted in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> system. And we shall demonstrate later that the form of the object in cognition is not tenable.

children.text: tad yadi vijñānajanakatvam ālambanārthas, tadā nayanālokāder apy ālambanatvaṃ prasajyate / athākārārpakatvam ālambanatvaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, naiyāyikasamaye 'nabhyupagamāt / yathā ca viṣayākāro vijñāne na yujyate tathopariṣṭāt pratipādayiṣyāmaḥ /

body.text: atha vijñānādhikaraṇatvam ālambanatvaṃ, na marīcicakrotkalitam udīyate jñānam, api tv ātmasamavetam ātmānam āsādayate / atha vijñānāvabhāsitatālambanatvaṃ, tadodakavijñānodakaṃ pratīyate, na marīcayaḥ / athodakākāratayā marīcayaiva pratīyante, sodakākāro marīcibhyo vyatirikto 'vyatirikto vā /
body.translated_text: If 'support' means being the locus of cognition, cognition does not arise as housed in the mirage-heap; rather, it is inherent in the self and pertains to the self. If 'support' means being illuminated by cognition, then in the water-cognition, water is perceived, not mirages. If mirages themselves are perceived in the form of water, is the water-form different from or identical with the mirages?

children.text: atha vijñānādhikaraṇatvam ālambanatvaṃ, na marīcicakrotkalitam udīyate jñānam, api tv ātmasamavetam ātmānam āsādayate / atha vijñānāvabhāsitatālambanatvaṃ, tadodakavijñāna udakaṃ pratīyate, na marīcayaḥ / athodakākāratayā marīcaya eva pratīyante, sa udakākāro marīcibhyo vyatirikto 'vyatirikto vā /

body.text: tad yady avyatiriktaḥ, sa tāttviko 'tāttviko vā /
body.translated_text: If it is identical, is it real or unreal?

children.text: tad yady avyatiriktaḥ, sa tāttviko 'tāttviko vā /

body.text: yadi tāttvikaḥ kathaṃ tadavagater mithyātvam? athātāttvikas, tad /ā marīcīnām apy atāttvikatvaṃ prasajyate / atāttvikodakatādātmye sati tad udakajñānam atathyaṃ kim uktaṃ bhavati? marīcivijñānam atathyam / ekasmiṃś codakākāre pratīyamāne kenaitad ākhyātaṃ marīcayaḥ pratibhānti devānāmpriyasya?
body.translated_text: If real, how can the cognition of it be false? If unreal, then the mirages themselves would absurdly become unreal. When identity with unreal water is assumed, what does it mean to say that the water-cognition is untrue? It means that the mirage-cognition is untrue. And when only a water-form is being perceived, who has declared to this 'dear one of the gods' that mirages appear?

children.text: yadi tāttvikaḥ kathaṃ tadavagater mithyātvam? athātāttvikas, tad /ā marīcīnām apy atāttvikatvaṃ prasajyate / atāttvikodakatādātmye sati tad udakajñānam atathyaṃ kim uktaṃ bhavati? marīcivijñānam atathyam / ekasmiṃś codakākāre pratīyamāne kenaitad ākhyātaṃ marīcayaḥ pratibhānti devānāmpriyasya?

body.text: athārthāntarabhūtas, tarhi na vaktavyaṃ marīcayodakākāratayā pratīyanta, udakākārāntaritā marīcayaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the water-form is a different entity, then one should not say 'mirages are perceived in the form of water,' but rather 'mirages concealed by the water-form.'

children.text: athārthāntarabhūtas, tarhi na vaktavyaṃ marīcaya udakākāratayā pratīyanta, udakākārāntaritā marīcayaḥ /

body.text: atha keśoṇḍukavijñāne kim avabhāti? kim ālambate? keśoṇḍukasyaivālambanatvaṃ pratīyamānatvaṃ ca, tathodakasyaivālambanatvaṃ pratīyamānatvaṃ ca, nālambanāntaraṃ parikalpyam / na codakajñānasya pratīyamānodakānyālambanatvena mithyātvam, api tv abhāvāt tāttvikatvena / anyathā keśoṇḍukasaṃvido 'pi mithyātvaṃ na prāpnoty, anyālambanavyatirekāt /
body.translated_text: Now in hair-net cognition, what appears? What is the support? The hair-net itself is both the support and what appears. Similarly, water itself is both the support and what appears, and no other support should be imagined. The water-cognition is not false because its support is something other than the perceived water; rather, it is false because of the non-existence of water in reality. Otherwise, even the cognition of hair-nets would not be false, since there is no support other than the hair-net.

children.text: atha keśoṇḍukavijñāne kim avabhāti? kim ālambate? keśoṇḍukasyaivālambanatvaṃ pratīyamānatvaṃ ca, tathodakasyaivālambanatvaṃ pratīyamānatvaṃ ca, nālambanāntaraṃ parikalpyam / na codakajñānasya pratīyamānodakānyālambanatvena mithyātvam, api tv abhāvāt tāttvikatvena / anyathā keśoṇḍukasaṃvido 'pi mithyātvaṃ na prāpnoty, anyālambanavyatirekāt /

body.text: 1.1a yad apy uktaṃ marīcideśaṃ prati gamanān marīcīnām ālambanatvam / yady evaṃ deśasyāpy ālambanatvam anayā rītyopapadyate / na cāvabhātodakabhinnārthasannikarṣajatvam udakavijñānasyopapadyate, satyodakajñāne 'dṛṣṭatvāt / anyathānumeyadahanajñānasyāpīndriyārthasannikarṣaja tvam āpanīpadyeta, ātmamanaḥsannikarṣajatvāt /
body.translated_text: 1.1a As for the claim that the mirages are the support because of movement toward the mirage-location—if so, the location itself would also become a support by this reasoning. Nor is it tenable that water-cognition arises from the contact of the sense organ with an object different from the apparent water, since this is not observed in the case of cognition of real water. Otherwise, even the cognition of inferred fire would absurdly be born of sense-object contact, since it arises from the contact of self and mind.

children.text: 1.1a2 yad apy uktaṃ marīcideśaṃ prati gamanān marīcīnām ālambanatvam / yady evaṃ deśasyāpy ālambanatvam anayā rītyopapadyate / na cāvabhātodakabhinnārthasannikarṣajatvam udakavijñānasyopapadyate, satyodakajñāne 'dṛṣṭatvāt / anyathānumeyadahanajñānasyāpīndriyārthasannikarṣaja tvam āpanīpadyeta, ātmamanaḥsannikarṣajatvāt /

body.text: atha pratīyamānadahanena saha manaso nāsti sambandhas, tad ihāpi pratīyamānenāmbhasā saha nāsti sambandhaś cakṣuṣaḥ / tasmād avyabhicāripadaṃ na yuktam indriyārthasannikarṣapadenāpoditatvāt /
body.translated_text: Now, if the mind has no connection with the perceived fire, then here too the eye has no connection with the perceived water. Therefore, the criterion of 'non-deviation' (<s>avyabhicāri</s>) is not justified, since it is set aside by the criterion of 'sense-object contact' (<s>indriyārthasannikarṣa</s>).

children.text: atha pratīyamānadahanena saha manaso nāsti sambandhas, tad ihāpi pratīyamānenāmbhasā saha nāsti sambandhaś cakṣuṣaḥ / tasmād avyabhicāripadaṃ na yuktam indriyārthasannikarṣapadenāpoditatvāt /

body.text: 1.1b ito 'py anupapannam apohyajñānāsambhavāt / atha marīcyudakavijñānāpaninīṣayopādīyate, tat katham apanīyate?
body.translated_text: [1.1b] This is also untenable from another angle, because of the impossibility of cognition that is to be sublated. Now, if [the criterion] is introduced with the desire to remove the cognition of mirage-water, then how is it removed?

children.text: 1.1b ito 'py anupapannam apohyajñānāsambhavāt / atha marīcyudakavijñānāpaninīṣayopādīyate, tat katham apanīyate?

body.text: avidyamānodakaviṣayatvāt / yady avidyamānaṃ, ko 'yaṃ viṣayārthaḥ? pūrvoditam anusaraṇīyam / yadi tatrodakaṃ pratibhāti, kathaṃ nāsti? satyaṃ, pratibhāti, kiṃ tv atathyaṃ pratibhāti / atathyatā kā? kiṃ pratīyamānasyābhāvota pratīyamānaivābhāvaḥ?
body.translated_text: Because its object is non-existent water. If it is non-existent, what is the meaning of 'object'? The previously stated argument should be followed. If water appears there, how can it not exist? True, it appears, but it appears falsely. What is this falsity? Is it the non-existence of what is perceived, or is the perceived thing itself non-existence?

children.text: avidyamānodakaviṣayatvāt / yady avidyamānaṃ, ko 'yaṃ viṣayārthaḥ? pūrvoditam anusaraṇīyam / yadi tatrodakaṃ pratibhāti, kathaṃ nāsti? satyaṃ, pratibhāti, kiṃ tv atathyaṃ pratibhāti / atathyatā kā? kiṃ pratīyamānasyābhāva uta pratīyamāna evābhāvaḥ?

body.text: 1.1b1 tad yadi pratīyamānasyābhāvaḥ, sa kiṃ tadaivāhosvit kālāntareṇa? yadi tadaiva, sa kim avagato 'navagato vā? yady avagataḥ, sa kenāvagamyate? kim udakavijñānena jñānāntareṇa vā?
body.translated_text: [1.1b1] If it is the non-existence of what is perceived, does that non-existence occur at that very time or at a later time? If at that very time, is it cognized or not cognized? If cognized, by what is it cognized? By the water-cognition or by another cognition?

children.text: 1.1b1 tad yadi pratīyamānasyābhāvaḥ, sa kiṃ tadaivāhosvit kālāntareṇa? yadi tadaiva, sa kim avagato 'navagato vā? yady avagataḥ, sa kenāvagamyate? kim udakavijñānena jñānāntareṇa vā?

body.text: tad yady udakajñānena, tan na, tasyodakaviṣayatvāt / tadviṣayatve vā na tarhy udakajñānaṃ bhrāntam ity upapadyate, 'bhāvaviṣayasya paramārthasattvāt /
body.translated_text: If by the water-cognition, that is not possible, because that cognition has water as its object. Or, if water is indeed its object, then it cannot be established that the water-cognition is erroneous, because what has an existent object is ultimately real.

children.text: tad yady udakajñānena, tan na, tasyodakaviṣayatvāt / tadviṣayatve vā na tarhy udakajñānaṃ bhrāntam ity upapadyate, 'bhāvaviṣayasya paramārthasattvāt /

body.text: na codakākārāvagāhini vijñāne toyavinivṛttayo 'vabhāntyatiprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: Nor do the removals of water appear in a cognition that plunges into the form of water, for that would lead to overextension.

children.text: na codakākārāvagāhini vijñāne toyavinivṛttayo 'vabhāntyatiprasaṅgāt /

body.text: atha jñānāntareṇa, na, jñānayaugapadyāsambhavāt / yadi cābhāvajñānenābhāvavyavasthā kriyate bhāvajñānena ca bhāvavyavasthā, tadodakasya bhāvābhāvāv ekakālau syātām /
body.translated_text: If by another cognition — that is not possible either, because two cognitions cannot occur simultaneously. And if absence is determined by absence-cognition and existence is determined by existence-cognition, then the existence and non-existence of water would occur at the same time.

children.text: atha jñānāntareṇa, na, jñānayaugapadyāsambhavāt / yadi cābhāvajñānenābhāvavyavasthā kriyate bhāvajñānena ca bhāvavyavasthā, tadodakasya bhāvābhāvāv ekakālau syātām /

body.text: atha bhāvajñānaṃ bhāvavyavasthāṃ na karoty abhāvajñānaṃ cābhāvavyavasthāṃ karoty, aho rājājñā naiyāyikapaśoḥ / yadi ca bhāvajñānaṃ bhāvavyavasthāṃ na karoti, tadā sarvabhāveṣv anāśvāsaprasaṅgaḥ / tatprasaktāv abhāvasyāpy anavasthitiḥ / tadanavasthitau ca tattvopaplavaḥ syāt / athānavagataḥ, so 'stīti kathaṃ punar vetsi?
body.translated_text: If existence-cognition does not determine existence but absence-cognition determines absence — oh, what a royal decree of the <s>Naiyāyika</s> beast! And if existence-cognition does not determine existence, then there would be the consequence of no confidence in any existing thing. In that eventuality, even absence would be unestablished. And if that is unestablished, there would be an upheaval of all categories (<s>tattvopaplava</s>). But if the non-existence is not cognized, how do you then know that it exists?

children.text: atha bhāvajñānaṃ bhāvavyavasthāṃ na karoty abhāvajñānaṃ cābhāvavyavasthāṃ karoty, aho rājājñā naiyāyikapaśoḥ / yadi ca bhāvajñānaṃ bhāvavyavasthāṃ na karoti, tadā sarvabhāveṣv anāśvāsaprasaṅgaḥ / tatprasaktāv abhāvasyāpy anavasthitiḥ / tadanavasthitau ca tattvopaplavaḥ syāt / athānavagataḥ, so 'stīti kathaṃ punar vetsi?

body.text: atha kālāntare, tadā na kiñcid bādhyate, satyodakasyāpi kālāntare 'bhāvopapatteḥ /
body.translated_text: If at a later time — then nothing is sublated, because even real water can cease to exist at a later time.

children.text: atha kālāntare, tadā na kiñcid bādhyate, satyodakasyāpi kālāntare 'bhāvopapatteḥ /

body.text: 1.1b2 atha pratīyamānaivābhāvaḥ, kathaṃ tadviṣayajñānasya mithyātvam upapadyate, pratīyamānasyaivābhāvasyopapatteḥ? na ca bhāvākāre pratīyamane 'bhāvakalpanā nyāyyātiprasaṅgāt / anyathā rūpādau pratīyamāne rasādikalpanā kartavyā / na cakriyate, tathehāpy udakaṃ pratīyate / nanu pratīyate, kiṃ tv atathyam / yady evam udakaprapañco 'yaṃ dīrghodakaṃ madhurodakam iti yathā / nanv atra sarvāsv avasthāsūdakaṃ pratīyate, tena tāsv ambhaḥ prakalpyate / yady evaṃ tad ihāpy avasthādvaye 'py udakaṃ pratīyate satyodakam asatyodakaṃ ca / satyodakajñāne satyodakam avabhāti, nāsatyodakam anudakaṃ vā / tathāsatyodakajñāne 'satyodakaṃ pratibhāti, na satyodakam anudakaṃ vā, svaviṣayaparyavasāyinyo hi buddhayaḥ /
body.translated_text: [1.1b2] If the perceived itself is non-existence, how can the falsity of the cognition having it as its object be established, since the perceived itself is admitted to be non-existence? Nor is it reasonable to attribute non-existence to what appears as an existent form, for that would lead to overextension. Otherwise, when color and the like is perceived, one would have to attribute taste and the like to it. And that is not done; similarly here too water is perceived. Objection: it is perceived, but falsely. If so, this is merely an elaboration about water — 'deep water,' 'sweet water,' and so on. Objection: in all those cases, water is perceived, and therefore water is attributed to those cases. If so, then here too in both conditions water is perceived — real water and unreal water. In the cognition of real water, real water appears, not unreal water or non-water. Similarly, in the cognition of unreal water, unreal water appears, not real water or non-water — for cognitions are confined to their own objects.

children.text: 1.1b2 atha pratīyamāna evābhāvaḥ, kathaṃ tadviṣayajñānasya mithyātvam upapadyate, pratīyamānasyaivābhāvasyopapatteḥ? na ca bhāvākāre pratīyamane 'bhāvakalpanā nyāyyātiprasaṅgāt / anyathā rūpādau pratīyamāne rasādikalpanā kartavyā / na cakriyate, tathehāpy udakaṃ pratīyate / nanu pratīyate, kiṃ tv atathyam / yady evam udakaprapañco 'yaṃ dīrghodakaṃ madhurodakam iti yathā / nanv atra sarvāsv avasthāsūdakaṃ pratīyate, tena tāsv ambhaḥ prakalpyate / yady evaṃ tad ihāpy avasthādvaye 'py udakaṃ pratīyate satyodakam asatyodakaṃ ca / satyodakajñāne satyodakam avabhāti, nāsatyodakam anudakaṃ vā / tathāsatyodakajñāne 'satyodakaṃ pratibhāti, na satyodakam anudakaṃ vā, svaviṣayaparyavasāyinyo hi buddhayaḥ /

body.text: 1.1bātha bādhyamānatvena mithyātvam iti cet,
body.translated_text: [1.1bā] If it is objected that falsity consists in being sublated (<s>bādhā</s>),

children.text: 1.1ba atha bādhyamānatvena mithyātvam iti cet,

body.text: kiṃ bādhyate 'rtho jñānam ubhayaṃ vā?
body.translated_text: What is sublated — the object, the cognition, or both?

children.text: kiṃ bādhyate 'rtho jñānam ubhayaṃ vā?

body.text: 1.1ba yady arthasya bādhā, sa kena bādhyate? kiṃ svayam evātmānaṃ bādhatāho 'rthāntareṇa jñānena vā?
body.translated_text: [1.1ba] If the object is sublated, by what is it sublated? Does it sublate itself, or by another object, or by cognition?

children.text: 1.1ba1 yady arthasya bādhā, sa kena bādhyate? kiṃ svayam evātmānaṃ bādhatā aho 'rthāntareṇa jñānena vā?

body.text: yadi Svayam evātmānaṃ bādhate, tadā bādhā tena kriyate jñāpyate vā / yadi kriyate, 'vyatiriktāvyatiriktā vā /
body.translated_text: If it sublates itself, then the sublation is either produced by it or made known by it. If produced, the sublation is either non-different or different from the object.

children.text: yadi Svayam evātmānaṃ bādhate, tadā bādhā tena kriyate jñāpyate vā / yadi kriyate, 'vyatiriktāvyatiriktā vā /

body.text: yady avyatiriktā, tadā bādhā kriyatety ātmānenotpādyate / tac ca na jāghaṭīti svātmani kriyāvirodhāt / atha vyatiriktā kriyate, tathāpi vidyamānasya kartṛtvaṃ, na pratīyamānasyāpalāpaḥ / atha bādhā jñāpyate, sāpy abhinnā bhinnā vā / yadyabhinnā, tadā bādhā tena jñāpyate kim uktaṃ bhavati? udakaṃ jñāpyate / atha bhinnā, tadā vidyamānasya jñāpakatvaṃ siddhaṃ pratīyamānasya cāstitvam / athārthāntareṇa bādhyate, tathāpi vidyamānayor bādhyabādhakabhāvo bhūpālayor iva, na caikasya bādhyabādhakabhāvopapadyate / bādhāpi tena pratīyamānasya kiṃ kriyate jñāpyate vā?
body.translated_text: If non-different, then to say 'sublation is produced' means 'it is produced by itself.' And that does not work, because there is a contradiction of action with respect to oneself. If different sublation is produced, even so there is agency of something that exists, not the denial of what is perceived. If sublation is made known rather than produced, it too is either non-different or different. If non-different, then to say 'sublation is made known by it' — what does that mean? It means 'water is made known.' If different, then the capacity to make known belongs to something that exists, and the existence of what is perceived is established. If it is sublated by another object, even so the relation of sublater and sublated is between two existing things, like two kings; and it is not possible for one thing to be both sublater and sublated. Moreover, is the sublation of the perceived by that other object produced or made known?

children.text: yady avyatiriktā, tadā bādhā kriyata ity ātmānenotpādyate / tac ca na jāghaṭīti svātmani kriyāvirodhāt / atha vyatiriktā kriyate, tathāpi vidyamānasya kartṛtvaṃ, na pratīyamānasyāpalāpaḥ / atha bādhā jñāpyate, sāpy abhinnā bhinnā vā / yadyabhinnā, tadā bādhā tena jñāpyate kim uktaṃ bhavati? udakaṃ jñāpyate / atha bhinnā, tadā vidyamānasya jñāpakatvaṃ siddhaṃ pratīyamānasya cāstitvam / athārthāntareṇa bādhyate, tathāpi vidyamānayor bādhyabādhakabhāvo bhūpālayor iva, na caikasya bādhyabādhakabhāva upapadyate / bādhāpi tena pratīyamānasya kiṃ kriyate jñāpyate vā?

body.text: yadi kriyate vyatiriktā vyatiriktā vā yady avyatiriktā, tadāvyatiriktā bādhotpādyate kim uktaṃ bhavet? udakam utpādyate / tadutpādane ca tatsaṃvido 'mithyātvam / atha vyatiriktotpādyate, tathāpi toyasambandhitayopalabdher ambhasopapattiḥ / na jātu devadattasyāsattve tannayanavyavahārasiddhiḥ / atha jñāpyate, tadā sāvyatiriktā vyatiriktā vā / yady avyatiriktā jñāpyate, tadā bādhā tena jñāpyate kim uktaṃ bhavati? udakaṃ jñāpyate / atha vyatiriktā satī jñāpyate, tathāpy udakasyeyaṃ bādhety anyatantratayā pratibhāsanān nātyantābhāvopapattiḥ / tasmād arthāntareṇāpi na bādhopapattiḥ / atha jñānena bādhyate kiṃ tadviṣayeṇānyaviṣayeṇa nirviṣayeṇa vā? yadi tadviṣayeṇa, tadā tat svarūpaṃ vidhatte na tu viparyāsayati tadākāraparyavasitarūpatvāt
body.translated_text: If produced — either non-different or different. If non-different, then to say 'non-different sublation is produced' — what does that mean? It means 'water is produced.' And in that production, the cognition of it would not be false. If different sublation is produced, even so, since it is perceived as connected with water, water is established. <s>Devadatta</s>'s eye-related practical activity is never established when <s>Devadatta</s> does not exist. If made known, then it is either non-different or different. If non-different is made known, then 'sublation is made known by it' — what does that mean? It means 'water is made known.' If it is made known as different, even so, since sublation appears as dependent on another entity — namely 'this is the sublation of water' — absolute non-existence is not established. Therefore, sublation is not established by another object either. If sublated by cognition — is it by cognition having the same object, a different object, or no object? If by cognition having the same object, then that cognition establishes the object's own nature and does not reverse it, since it is confined to the form of that object.

children.text: yadi kriyate vyatiriktā vyatiriktā vā yady avyatiriktā, tadāvyatiriktā bādhotpādyate kim uktaṃ bhavet? udakam utpādyate / tadutpādane ca tatsaṃvido 'mithyātvam / atha vyatiriktotpādyate, tathāpi toyasambandhitayopalabdher ambhasa upapattiḥ / na jātu devadattasyāsattve tannayanavyavahārasiddhiḥ / atha jñāpyate, tadā sāvyatiriktā vyatiriktā vā / yady avyatiriktā jñāpyate, tadā bādhā tena jñāpyate kim uktaṃ bhavati? udakaṃ jñāpyate / atha vyatiriktā satī jñāpyate, tathāpy udakasyeyaṃ bādhety anyatantratayā pratibhāsanān nātyantābhāvopapattiḥ / tasmād arthāntareṇāpi na bādhopapattiḥ / atha jñānena bādhyate kiṃ tadviṣayeṇānyaviṣayeṇa nirviṣayeṇa vā? yadi tadviṣayeṇa, tadā tat svarūpaṃ vidhatte na tu viparyāsayati tadākāraparyavasitarūpatvāt

body.text: athānyaviṣayaṃ bādhakaṃ, tad api na yujyate / yad yadviṣayaṃ tat tasyaiva sattāṃ vidhatte, na tv anyasya vidhāyakaṃ pratiṣedhakaṃ vā / svaviṣayaparyavasāyinyo hi buddhayaḥ / atha nirviṣayeṇa bādhyate, na kiñcid vidadhāti pratiṣedhati vā nirviṣayatvād eva /
body.translated_text: If the sublating cognition has a different object, that too is not justified. For whatever has a given object establishes the existence of that object alone, but neither establishes nor negates another — for cognitions are confined to their own objects. If sublated by a cognition without an object, it neither establishes nor negates anything, precisely because it has no object.

children.text: athānyaviṣayaṃ bādhakaṃ, tad api na yujyate / yad yadviṣayaṃ tat tasyaiva sattāṃ vidhatte, na tv anyasya vidhāyakaṃ pratiṣedhakaṃ vā / svaviṣayaparyavasāyinyo hi buddhayaḥ / atha nirviṣayeṇa bādhyate, na kiñcid vidadhāti pratiṣedhati vā nirviṣayatvād eva /

body.text: 1.1ba atha jñānaṃ bādhyate, tasyāpi bādhā kā? kiṃ svarūpavyāvṛttirūpā svarūpāpahnavarūpā vā viṣayāpdhāralakṣaṇā vā? tad yadi svarūpavyāvṛttirūpā bādhā, tadā sarvaṃ bādhitaṃ syād, vijñānasya vijñānāntareṇa nivartyamānatvāt / atha svarūpāpahnavarūpā, tad ayuktaṃ, mithyodakavijñānasyāpyanubhūyamānatvāt / atha viṣayāpahāralakṣaṇā bādhocyate, sāpi na yuktā / yathā ca viṣayāpahāro na śakyate kartuṃ tathānāntaram eva niveditam /
body.translated_text: [1.1ba] If the cognition is sublated, what is this sublation of it? Is it in the form of cessation of its own nature, or denial of its own nature, or characterized by removal of its object? If sublation consists in cessation of its own nature, then everything would be sublated, since every cognition is superseded by another cognition. If in the form of denial of its own nature, that is not justified, because even the erroneous water-cognition is actually experienced. If sublation is said to consist in removal of the object, that too is not justified. And why the removal of the object cannot be accomplished has been explained just above.

children.text: 1.1ba2 atha jñānaṃ bādhyate, tasyāpi bādhā kā? kiṃ svarūpavyāvṛttirūpā svarūpāpahnavarūpā vā viṣayāpdhāralakṣaṇā vā? tad yadi svarūpavyāvṛttirūpā bādhā, tadā sarvaṃ bādhitaṃ syād, vijñānasya vijñānāntareṇa nivartyamānatvāt / atha svarūpāpahnavarūpā, tad ayuktaṃ, mithyodakavijñānasyāpyanubhūyamānatvāt / atha viṣayāpahāralakṣaṇā bādhocyate, sāpi na yuktā / yathā ca viṣayāpahāro na śakyate kartuṃ tathānāntaram eva niveditam /

body.text: 1.1bā yadi na bādhyate kim ity asāv arthakriyāṃ na karoti bhāvaḥ? keyam arthakriyā yā tena na sampādyate puṃsām? kiṃ vijñānarūpā pravṛttirūpā prāptirūpā sukhaduḥkhotpādabhogarūpā vā?
body.translated_text: [1.1bā] If it is not sublated, why does that entity not produce <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy)? What is this causal efficacy that it fails to accomplish for people? Is it of the nature of cognition, of the nature of activity, of the nature of attainment, or of the nature of producing the experience of pleasure and pain?

children.text: 1.1bā yadi na bādhyate kim ity asāv arthakriyāṃ na karoti bhāvaḥ? keyam arthakriyā yā tena na sampādyate puṃsām? kiṃ vijñānarūpā pravṛttirūpā prāptirūpā sukhaduḥkhotpādabhogarūpā vā?

body.text: tad yadi vijñānalakṣaṇāṃ na karoti, tad ayuktaṃ, vijñānalakṣaṇām arthakriyāṃ karoty eva toyam /
body.translated_text: If it does not produce causal efficacy in the form of cognition, that is not justified — for water indeed produces causal efficacy in the form of cognition.

children.text: tad yadi vijñānalakṣaṇāṃ na karoti, tad ayuktaṃ, vijñānalakṣaṇām arthakriyāṃ karoty eva toyam /

body.text: atha pravṛttirūpāṃ na karoti, tad ayuktaṃ, pravṛttir hi puruṣecchānuvidhāyinī, nārthasvarūpabhāvābhāvāv anugamayati / puruṣo hi kāmataḥ pravartate vā na vā / na hy etāvatā tadabhāvasiddhiḥ / atha prāptirūpām arthakriyāṃ na karoti, tenāsattvam /
body.translated_text: If it does not produce causal efficacy in the form of activity, that is not justified — for activity follows the wish of the person, not the existence or non-existence of the object's own nature. A person may or may not act as he desires. This alone does not establish its non-existence. If it does not produce causal efficacy in the form of attainment, and therefore it is unreal —

children.text: atha pravṛttirūpāṃ na karoti, tad ayuktaṃ, pravṛttir hi puruṣecchānuvidhāyinī, nārthasvarūpabhāvābhāvāv anugamayati / puruṣo hi kāmataḥ pravartate vā na vā / na hy etāvatā tadabhāvasiddhiḥ / atha prāptirūpām arthakriyāṃ na karoti, tenāsattvam /

body.text: tad apy ayuktaṃ, candrārkagrahanakṣatratārakādeḥ prāptyabhāve 'pi sattvasambhavāt / atha sukhaduḥkharūpām arthakriyāṃ na karoti, kiṃ darśanajaṃ sukhaṃ na karoty āho dehasambandhajam? tad yadi darśanajaṃ na karoti, tad ayuktaṃ, karoty eva / atha dehasambandhajaṃ na karoti, tadā candrārkagrahanakṣatrādau vyabhicāras, teṣāṃ dehasambandhajasukhajanakatvaṃ nāsty, atha ca sattvam / na cārthakriyākartṛtvena vastūnām asattvaṃ, svahetor eva vijñānajananamātrasyotpatteḥ, sahakārivirahād vā na karoti /
body.translated_text: That too is not justified, because even in the absence of attainment of the moon, sun, planets, stars, and constellations, their existence is possible. If it does not produce causal efficacy in the form of pleasure and pain — does it not produce the pleasure arising from seeing, or the pleasure arising from bodily contact? If it does not produce the pleasure arising from seeing, that is not justified — for it does produce it. If it does not produce the pleasure arising from bodily contact, then there is deviation in the case of the moon, sun, planets, stars, and the like, for they do not produce pleasure arising from bodily contact, and yet they exist. Nor is it the case that things are unreal because of not producing causal efficacy, since cognition arises merely from its own cause, or the thing does not produce the effect due to the absence of auxiliary conditions.

children.text: tad apy ayuktaṃ, candrārkagrahanakṣatratārakādeḥ prāptyabhāve 'pi sattvasambhavāt / atha sukhaduḥkharūpām arthakriyāṃ na karoti, kiṃ darśanajaṃ sukhaṃ na karoty āho dehasambandhajam? tad yadi darśanajaṃ na karoti, tad ayuktaṃ, karoty eva / atha dehasambandhajaṃ na karoti, tadā candrārkagrahanakṣatrādau vyabhicāras, teṣāṃ dehasambandhajasukhajanakatvaṃ nāsty, atha ca sattvam / na cārthakriyākartṛtvena vastūnām asattvaṃ, svahetor eva vijñānajananamātrasyotpatteḥ, sahakārivirahād vā na karoti /

body.text: 1.1bab kiṃ cārthakriyāṃ na karoti kim ekasya pratipattuḥ sarvapratipattṝṇāṃ vā?
body.translated_text: [1.1bab] Furthermore, it does not produce causal efficacy — for one cognizer or for all cognizers?

children.text: 1.1bab kiṃ cārthakriyāṃ na karoti kim ekasya pratipattuḥ sarvapratipattṝṇāṃ vā?

body.text: tad yady ekasya pratipattur arthakriyāṃ na karoti tenāsattvaṃ, tadā candrārkagrahanakṣatratārakādau vyabhicāro, mumūrṣvarthe ca /
body.translated_text: If it does not produce causal efficacy for one cognizer and therefore is unreal, then there is deviation in the case of the moon, sun, planets, stars, and the like, and also in the case of objects for a dying person.

children.text: tad yady ekasya pratipattur arthakriyāṃ na karoti tenāsattvaṃ, tadā candrārkagrahanakṣatratārakādau vyabhicāro, mumūrṣvarthe ca /

body.text: atha sarvapratipattṝṇām arthakriyāṃ na karoti tenāsattvam, evaṃ tarhi sarvabhāvānām asattvaprasaṅgaḥ / na hi sarve bhāvāḥ sarvapuruṣārthahetavaḥ / na ca sarvapuruṣārthakriyāvihīnam etad ity avagantuṃ pāryate 'rvāgvidā / tasmāt sthitam etad avyabhicāripadam anarthakam /
body.translated_text: If it does not produce causal efficacy for all cognizers and therefore is unreal, then there would be the consequence that all entities are unreal. For not all entities serve the purposes of all persons. Nor can it be ascertained by one of limited vision that this entity is devoid of causal efficacy for all persons. Therefore, it is established that the criterion of 'non-deviation' (<s>avyabhicāri</s>) is meaningless.

children.text: atha sarvapratipattṝṇām arthakriyāṃ na karoti tenāsattvam, evaṃ tarhi sarvabhāvānām asattvaprasaṅgaḥ / na hi sarve bhāvāḥ sarvapuruṣārthahetavaḥ / na ca sarvapuruṣārthakriyāvihīnam etad ity avagantuṃ pāryate 'rvāgvidā / tasmāt sthitam etad avyabhicāripadam anarthakam /

body.text: c. anye tu marīcyudakavijñānasya smṛtitvaṃ pratipadyante, na bhrāntirūpatām / tasya kathaṃ smṛtitvam? kim udakagṛhītitvena gṛhītodakagṛhītitvena vodakagrahaṇānantarakālabhāvitvena vā nirviṣayatvena vā yam aham adrākṣam ity anenākāreṇopajāyamānatvena vā?
body.translated_text: c. Others, however, accept that mirage-water cognition is of the nature of memory (<s>smṛti</s>), not of the nature of error. How is it memory? Is it (1) by having grasped water, (2) by having grasped previously-grasped water, (3) by arising at a time subsequent to the grasping of water, (4) by being objectless, or (5) by arising with the form 'I have seen this'?

children.text: c. anye tu marīcyudakavijñānasya smṛtitvaṃ pratipadyante, na bhrāntirūpatām / tasya kathaṃ smṛtitvam? kim udakagṛhītitvena gṛhītodakagṛhītitvena vodakagrahaṇānantarakālabhāvitvena vā nirviṣayatvena vā yam aham adrākṣam ity anenākāreṇopajāyamānatvena vā?

body.text: tad yady udakagṛhītitvena tadā sarvodakavijñānānāṃ smṛtitvaprasaṅgaḥ / atha gṛhītodakagṛhītitvena smṛtitvaṃ, tadādyasyāpi gṛhītodakagṛhītitve smṛtitvaṃ prasajyate gṛhītodakagrāhitvāviśeṣāt /
body.translated_text: If by having grasped water, then the absurd consequence follows that all water-cognitions would be memory. If memory is defined as having grasped previously-grasped water, then the first cognition too would absurdly become memory if it grasps previously-grasped water, since there is no difference in its grasping of grasped water.

children.text: tad yady udakagṛhītitvena tadā sarvodakavijñānānāṃ smṛtitvaprasaṅgaḥ / atha gṛhītodakagṛhītitvena smṛtitvaṃ, tadādyasyāpi gṛhītodakagṛhītitve smṛtitvaṃ prasajyate gṛhītodakagrāhitvāviśeṣāt /

body.text:
athādyasya gṛhītodakagrāhitvaṃ nāsti / tadānīṃ bhinnaviṣayatvam / bhinnaviṣayatve ca dvitīyasyāpi gṛhītagrāhitvaṃ vihīyate / athaikaviṣayatvam, āyātaṃ tarhi prathamasyāpi gṛhītagrāhitvam aviśiṣṭārthagṛhītirūpatvāt prathamottaravijñānavat / yathaikanīlasvalakṣaṇagrāhakayugapadutpannānekavijñānānāṃ nīlajñānarūpatā na bhidyate tathehāpi / tathā dhārāvāhivijñānānāṃ smṛtirūpatā prāpnoti / tathā pratyabhijñānasya ca gṛhītagrāhitvena smṛtitvaṃ prasajyate / atha pratyabhijñānasya gṛhītārthagrāhitvaṃ na vidyate, tadā pratyabhijñānatvaṃ nivartate / na hy ādyaṃ darśanaṃ saivāyam ity upajāyate / tathānumānikam api vijñānaṃ gṛhītārthagrāhitvena smṛtitvam āpadyate / athodakagrahaṇottarakālabhāvitvena smṛtitvaṃ, tadā saṃskārasya smaraṇarūpatā prāpnoty,
udakagrahaṇottarakālabhāvitvena rasasaṃvedanasya ca /
body.translated_text: If the first cognition does not grasp previously-grasped water, then they have different objects. And if they have different objects, the second cognition's grasping of the previously-grasped is also undermined. If they have the same object, then the first cognition too would have the character of grasping the previously-grasped, since both the first and subsequent cognitions have the form of grasping an indistinguishable object. Just as among multiple simultaneously-arisen cognitions grasping one and the same particular blue, their nature as blue-cognitions is not different, so too here. Likewise, the stream-like succession of cognitions would absurdly become memory in nature. Similarly, recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) would absurdly become memory by virtue of grasping the previously-grasped. If recognition does not have the character of grasping a previously-grasped object, then its nature as recognition would be negated. For the initial seeing does not arise in the form 'this is that very same thing.' Likewise, inferential cognition too would absurdly become memory by virtue of grasping a previously-grasped object. If memory is defined by arising at a time subsequent to the grasping of water, then the latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) would absurdly become memory in nature, and so would the perception of taste that arises after the grasping of water.

udakagrahaṇottarakālabhāvitvena rasasaṃvedanasya ca /

body.text: atha nirviṣayatvena smṛtirūpatocyate, tad ayuktaṃ, pūrvoditānubhavāveditārthākārāvedakatvenodīyamānāyāḥ kathaṃ nirviṣayatvam? atha pūrvānubhūtārthapratyastamaye sati samānakālārthābhāvān nirviṣayatā, tadā codanājanitavi
body.translated_text: If memory is said to be characterized by objectlessness (<s>nirviṣayatva</s>), that is not proper. How can objectlessness be attributed to what arises as a cognizer of the form of an object not cognized by a prior experience? body.translated_text: the cognition born from Vedic injunction would absurdly become memory through objectlessness, since the object in the form of what-ought-to-be-done does not then exist. Or if it does exist, then its nature as what-ought-to-be-done would not be tenable. If that is untenable, the absurd consequence follows that the activity of weaving with seven threads would be voided. And if objectlessness defines memory, then the remembering of an existing pot-universal and the like would absurdly become non-memory. If memory is defined as arising with the form 'I have seen this,' that is not proper. How can what arises with the form 'here is water' come to have the form 'I have seen'?

body.text: atha vipramuṣitatayānayā bhaṅgyopajāyate, ko 'yaṃ vipramoṣo nāma? kim anubhavākārasvīkaraṇaṃ smaraṇākārapradhvaṃso vāpūrvārthagṛhītitvaṃ vendriyārthasannikarṣajatvaṃ vendriyārthāsannikarṣajatvaṃ vā?
body.translated_text: If it arises in this manner through confusion (<s>vipramoṣa</s>), what is this so-called confusion? Is it (1) the adoption of the form of experience, (2) the destruction of the form of memory, (3) the grasping of a previously-ungrasped object, (4) arising from sense-object contact, or (5) not arising from sense-object contact?

children.text: atha vipramuṣitatayānayā bhaṅgyopajāyate, ko 'yaṃ vipramoṣo nāma? kim anubhavākārasvīkaraṇaṃ smaraṇākārapradhvaṃso vāpūrvārthagṛhītitvaṃ vendriyārthasannikarṣajatvaṃ vendriyārthāsannikarṣajatvaṃ vā?

body.text: tad yady anubhavākārasvīkaraṇaṃ, tadā smṛtirūpatā nopapadyate / atha smṛtirūpatā, tadānubhavākārasvīkaraṇaṃ nopapadyate, smṛtyanubhavākārayor itaretaraparihārasthitilakṣaṇatvāt / atha smaraṇākārapradhvaṃsas, tad ayuktaṃ, vijñānasya svayaṃ smṛtitvenābhyupagamāt / pradhvaṃso hy avijñānātmakaḥ, kathaṃ smṛtirūpatāṃ vidhatte?
body.translated_text: If it is the adoption of the form of experience, then its nature as memory would not be tenable. If it has the nature of memory, then the adoption of the form of experience would not be tenable, since the forms of memory and experience are defined by mutual exclusion. If it is the destruction of the form of memory, that is not proper, since the cognition is itself accepted as being of the nature of memory. For destruction is not of the nature of cognition—how can it produce the nature of memory?

children.text: tad yady anubhavākārasvīkaraṇaṃ, tadā smṛtirūpatā nopapadyate / atha smṛtirūpatā, tadānubhavākārasvīkaraṇaṃ nopapadyate, smṛtyanubhavākārayor itaretaraparihārasthitilakṣaṇatvāt / atha smaraṇākārapradhvaṃsas, tad ayuktaṃ, vijñānasya svayaṃ smṛtitvenābhyupagamāt / pradhvaṃso hy avijñānātmakaḥ, kathaṃ smṛtirūpatāṃ vidhatte?

body.text: athāpūrvārthaviṣayagṛhītitvaṃ smṛtipramoṣocyate, tadātyantānanubhūtakanakapanasādisaṃvittīnaṃ smṛtivipramoṣatvam āpadyate / athendriyārthasannikarṣajatvaṃ smṛtivipralnoṣocyate, tadā saṃvittīnāṃ smṛtivipramoṣatva prasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the confusion of memory is said to be the grasping of a previously-ungrasped object, then cognitions of things like a golden breadfruit tree, which have never been experienced at all, would absurdly become confused memory. If the confusion of memory is said to be arising from sense-object contact, then the absurd consequence follows that all cognitions would be confused memory.

children.text: athāpūrvārthaviṣayagṛhītitvaṃ smṛtipramoṣa ucyate, tadātyantānanubhūtakanakapanasādisaṃvittīnaṃ smṛtivipramoṣatvam āpadyate / athendriyārthasannikarṣajatvaṃ smṛtivipralnoṣa ucyate, tadā saṃvittīnāṃ smṛtivipramoṣatva prasaṅgaḥ /

body.text: athendriyāsannikarṣajatvaṃ smṛtivipramoṣocyate, tadā codanājanitavijñānasyānumānopamānavijñānasya ca smṛtivipramoṣatvam āpadyate / tasmād yathā yathā vicāryate smṛtivipramoṣas tathā tathā nyāyaṃ na viṣahateti / tasmān marīcyudakavijñānasya na smṛtivipramoṣarūpatā, api tu viparītakhyātitvaṃ samyagjñānatvaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: If the confusion of memory is said to be not arising from sense-object contact, then cognition born from Vedic injunction, as well as inferential and analogical cognition, would absurdly become confused memory. Therefore, however one examines the confusion of memory, it does not withstand logical scrutiny. Therefore, mirage-water cognition is not of the nature of confused memory, but rather is either erroneous cognition (<s>viparītakhyāti</s>) or valid cognition.

children.text: athendriyāsannikarṣajatvaṃ smṛtivipramoṣa ucyate, tadā codanājanitavijñānasyānumānopamānavijñānasya ca smṛtivipramoṣatvam āpadyate / tasmād yathā yathā vicāryate smṛtivipramoṣas tathā tathā nyāyaṃ na viṣahata iti / tasmān marīcyudakavijñānasya na smṛtivipramoṣarūpatā, api tu viparītakhyātitvaṃ samyagjñānatvaṃ vā /

body.text: 1.2 tathā vyavasāyātmakapadam api nopādeyam apaneyābhāvāt / nanu sthāṇvādike 'rthendriyārthasannikarṣāt sāmānyamātradarśanād viśeṣānupalabdhau sandehajñānam upajāyate / tad apanīyate / tasmin sandehajñāne jāte kiñcit pratibhāty āho na pratibhāti / tad yadi pratibhāti, sa kiṃ dharmī dharmo vā?
body.translated_text: 1.2 Likewise, the qualifier 'of the nature of determination' (<s>vyavasāyātmaka</s>) is also not to be adopted, since there is nothing to be excluded by it. Objection: When a post or the like is the object, from the contact of sense and object there arises only the seeing of a general form, and when the particular is not apprehended, doubt-cognition arises. That is what needs to be excluded. When that doubt-cognition arises, does something appear in it or does nothing appear?  If something appears, is it the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) or the property (<s>dharma</s>)?

children.text: 1.2 tathā vyavasāyātmakapadam api nopādeyam apaneyābhāvāt / nanu sthāṇvādike 'rtha indriyārthasannikarṣāt sāmānyamātradarśanād viśeṣānupalabdhau sandehajñānam upajāyate / tad apanīyate / tasmin sandehajñāne jāte kiñcit pratibhāty āho na pratibhāti / tad yadi pratibhāti, sa kiṃ dharmī dharmo vā?

body.translated_text: If the property-bearer appears, is it real or unreal?

children.text: tad yadi dharmī pratibhāti, sa tāttviko 'tāttviko vā /

body.text: yadi tāttviko, nāpaneyatā tadviṣayavijñānasya / athātāttvikas, tadāvyabhicāripadenāpanītatvān na vyavasāyātmakapadam upādeyam / atha dharmaḥ pratibhāti, sa sthāṇutvalakṣaṇaḥ puruṣatvalakṣaṇobhayaṃ vā / tad yadi sthāṇutvalakṣaṇo dharmaḥ pratibhāti, sa tāttviko 'tāttviko vā / yadi tāttvikaḥ, kathaṃ tadbuddheḥ sandeharūpatā, tāttvikārthagṛhītirūpatvena satyodakasaṃvedanavat?
body.translated_text: If real, then the cognition of that object is not to be excluded. If unreal, then since it is already excluded by the qualifier 'non-erring,' the qualifier 'of the nature of determination' is not to be adopted. If a property appears, is it characterized as post-ness, person-ness, or both? If the property characterized as post-ness appears, is it real or unreal? If real, how can that cognition be of the nature of doubt, since it has the form of grasping a real object, like the cognition of real water?

children.text: yadi tāttviko, nāpaneyatā tadviṣayavijñānasya / athātāttvikas, tadāvyabhicāripadenāpanītatvān na vyavasāyātmakapadam upādeyam / atha dharmaḥ pratibhāti, sa sthāṇutvalakṣaṇaḥ puruṣatvalakṣaṇa ubhayaṃ vā / tad yadi sthāṇutvalakṣaṇo dharmaḥ pratibhāti, sa tāttviko 'tāttviko vā / yadi tāttvikaḥ, kathaṃ tadbuddheḥ sandeharūpatā, tāttvikārthagṛhītirūpatvena satyodakasaṃvedanavat?

body.text:
athātāttvikas, tadāvyabhicāripadenāpoditatvān na vyavasāyātmakapadam upādeyam / atha puruṣatvalakṣaṇo dharmaḥ pratibhāty, asāv api tāttviko 'tāttviko vā / yadi tāttvikaḥ, kathaṃ tatbuddheḥ sandeharūpatā? athātāttvikas, tadāvyabhicāripadenāpoditatvād vyavasāyātmakapadaṃ na sādhīyaḥ / athobhayaṃ pratibhāti, tadobhayos tāttvikatvam atāttvikatvaṃ vāthaikasya tāttvikatvam anyasyātāttvikatvam / tad yady ubhayos tāttvikatvaṃ, tada tadvijñānasya tāttvikatvam eva, na sandehātmatā / athobhāv apy atāttvikau, tadā tadvijñānasya viparyayarūpatā, na sandehātmatā / athaikasya tāttvikatvam anyasyātāttvikatvaṃ, tadā tad eva jñānaṃ vyabhicāri tad evāvyabhicāri / atāttvikārthagṛhītirūpatvād vyabhicāri, tāttvikārthagṛhītirūpatvād avyabhicāri / etena dvicandrajñānam udghāṭitam / tatra hi dravyākāraḥ pratibhāti,
na guṇākāraḥ / atha sandigdhārthākārapratibhāsi sandehajñānam iti cet,
sasandigdho 'rtho vidyate vā na vā / tad yadi vidyate, kathaṃ tatsaṃvedanasya sandeharūpatābādhitārthagṛhītirūpatvāt satyodakasaṃvedanavat?
body.translated_text: If unreal, then since it is already excluded by the qualifier 'non-erring,' the qualifier 'of the nature of determination' is not to be adopted. If the property characterized as person-ness appears, is it too real or unreal? If real, how can that cognition be of the nature of doubt? If unreal, then since it is already excluded by the qualifier 'non-erring,' the qualifier 'of the nature of determination' is not the better option. If both appear, then either both are real, both are unreal, or one is real and the other unreal. If both are real, then the cognition is simply real, not of the nature of doubt. If both are unreal, then the cognition is of the nature of error, not of doubt. If one is real and the other unreal, then that very cognition is both erring and non-erring—erring because it grasps an unreal object, non-erring because it grasps a real object. By this, the cognition of a double moon is also explained. For there, the substance-form appears, but not the quality-form. If one says that doubt-cognition is that which presents the form of a doubtful object, then does the doubtful object exist or not? If it exists, how can the cognition of it be of the nature of doubt, since it has the form of grasping an unobstructed object, like the cognition of real water?

That contact is like a goblin, an atom, or <s>Maheśvara</s>. How is the dependence of cognition on it known?

body.translated_text: And how does cognition indicate that sense-object contact? Is it by virtue of its nature as cognition, by virtue of being an effect, or by virtue of its nature as something born from sense-object contact? If by virtue of its nature as cognition, that is not proper, since the cognition-form exists even in its absence, as in the case of cognition from analogy and the like.

body.translated_text: Now if it indicates [the sense-organ] by virtue of being an effect, that too is unjustified, because the existence of that [effect-nature] is established in cognitions of comparison, inference, mirage, blue, water, and the like. body.translated_text: If it is said that it indicates [the sense-organ] by virtue of having a form produced by the contact of sense-organ and object, then is that form produced by sense-object contact non-different from the cognition-form, or different?

body.text: yady avyatiriktas, tadā jñānātmatāmātraṃ, nākārātireko 'nyo 'sti vibhāvyamāno 'numānādijñāneṣu yathā / ākārāntarātireke vā j ānarūpatā hīyate / atha vyatiriktas, tasyaiva tarhi gamakatvaṃ, na jñānākārasya / tasyāpy agamakatvaṃ tadavedanāt / kiṃ ca tadutpannam indriyārthasannikarṣād vijñānaṃ svarūpeṇāvagāhanīyaṃ, tato vyāptismaraṇaṃ, tadanu parāmarśajñānaṃ, tato 'numeyāvagatir iti na caitāvantaṃ kālaṃ vijñānaṃ sthitipadaṃ badhnāty, āśubhāvitvena pratyastamitatvāt / atha buddhyārūḍhena dharmadharminyāyena parikalpyate 'numānaṃ, tadāvāstavaṃ prāpnoti sugatānumānavat /
body.translated_text: If non-different, then it is merely of the nature of cognition, and there is no other form beyond the cognition-form that is discernible, as in inferential and other cognitions. Or if there is an additional form beyond, the nature of cognition would be lost. Now if different, then it is that alone which has indicative capacity, not the cognition-form. But even that lacks indicative capacity, because it is not experienced. Moreover, the cognition produced from sense-object contact must first be apprehended in its own form, then there is the recollection of the invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>), then the reflective cognition (<s>parāmarśa</s>), and then the cognition of the inferable — but cognition does not persist for that entire duration, since it has already ceased due to being momentary. Now if inference is constructed through the method of property and property-bearer superimposed upon cognition, then it becomes unreal, like the Buddhist inference.

body.text: 1.42 tathendriyotpādyatvam api nopapadyatendriyotpādyatvātirekānavagateḥ / vijñānaṃ svabhāvatayaiva vedyate, nākārāntareṇa / tajjñaptau vā jñānākāravirahaprasaṅgaḥ / na ca jñānam indriyasambaddhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ, yena tad upalabhyamānam indriyaṃ gamayati /
body.translated_text: 1.42 Likewise, being produced by the sense-organ is also not tenable, because there is no apprehension of anything beyond being produced by the sense-organ. Cognition is known by its own nature alone, not through another form. Or in the cognition of that, the absurd consequence of the absence of the cognition-form would follow. Nor is cognition observed as connected with the sense-organ, such that when perceived, it would indicate the sense-organ.

body.text: saiva gamikāstu, yasyāḥ karaṇasambandho 'vagataḥ / na cānyasya sambandhe 'nyasya gamakatvaṃ kiñcitsāmyād upapadyate / na jātu devadattanayananīlasambandhe sati yajñadattendriyaṃ ghaṭādikam artham asati sambandhe karaṇatvasāmyād prakāśayad dṛṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Only that [action] is indicative whose connection with the instrument is apprehended. And the indicative capacity of one thing based on the connection of another is not established merely from some similarity. It is never observed that when there is a connection between <s>Devadatta</s>'s eye and blue, <s>Yajñadatta</s>'s sense-organ illuminates an object such as a pot in the absence of connection, merely because of the similarity of being instruments.

body.translated_text: Likewise, the form produced by the object in cognition should also be understood as refuted in the same manner.

body.text: 1.43 tathārtho 'pi vijñānam utpādayaty anupajātātiśayopajātātiśayo vāvyatiriktopajātātiśayo vā vyatiriktopajātātiśayo vā / tad yady anupajātātiśayaḥ karoti, tadā sarvadā kuryān na vā / karaṇam akaraṇaṃ ca nopapadyeta tatsvarūpānativṛtteḥ /
body.translated_text: 1.43 Likewise, does the object produce cognition without any arisen excellence, with a non-distinct arisen excellence, or with a distinct arisen excellence? If it produces without any arisen excellence, then it would always produce or never produce. Both production and non-production would be untenable, since its own nature is not transcended.

body.text: tathāvyatiriktopajātātiśayo 'pi na karoty akārakākārasyānugateḥ / ananugatau vā na tarhi tadavyatirikto 'tiśayaḥ / atha vyatiriktopajātātiśayena janyate, tathāpi nopapadyate 'kārakākārānativṛtteḥ / ativṛttau vāyātaṃ kṣaṇikatvam / tataś ca nendriyārthasannikarṣajaṃ vijñānaṃ pratyakṣalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Likewise, [the object] with a non-distinct arisen excellence also does not produce, because the non-productive form persists. Or if it does not persist, then the excellence is not non-distinct from it. Now if it is produced by a distinct arisen excellence, even so it is not tenable, because the non-productive form is not transcended. Or if it is transcended, then momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) is established. And therefore, cognition born from the contact of sense-organ and object is not the definition of perception.

body.text: Chapter 2: Examination of the Mīmāṃsā definition of valid cognition:

2. anye tv anadhigatārthagantṛtvena pramāṇalakṣaṇam abhidadhati / te tv ayuktavādino draṣṭavyāḥ / katham ayuktavāditā teṣam iti ced, ucyate vibhinnakārakotpāditaikārthavijñānānāṃ yathāvyavasthitaikārthagṛhītirūpatvāviśeṣe ' pi pūrvotpannavijñānasya prāmāṇyaṃ nottarasyety atra niyāmakaṃ vaktavyam /
body.translated_text: 2. Others, however, define the characteristic of a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) as the capacity to reach an object not previously apprehended. But they should be regarded as proponents of untenable doctrines. If asked how their doctrine is untenable, it is said: among cognitions of the same object produced by different causal instruments, even though there is no distinction in having the form of grasping the same established object, a determining factor must be stated for why the earlier-produced cognition has validity but not the later one.

body.text: 2.1 atha yathāvyavasthitārthagṛhītirūpatvāviśeṣe 'pi pūrvotpannavijñānasya prāmāṇyam upapadyate, na prathamottaravijñānasya, tadānenaiva nyāyena prathamasyāpy aprāmāṇyaṃ prasaktaṃ gṛhītārthagrāhitvāviśeṣāt / yathaikanīlasvalakṣaṇāvabhāsitayugapadutpannānekanīlavijñānānāṃ nīlaikārthagṛhītirūpatā na bhidyate, tathā pūrvāparotpannavijñānānām api gṛhītārthagṛhītirūpatā na nivartsyati /
body.translated_text: 2.1 Now if the validity of the earlier-produced cognition is tenable despite there being no distinction in having the form of grasping the established object, but not of the later cognition after the first, then by this very reasoning the invalidity of the first also follows, since there is no distinction in grasping an already-grasped object. Just as among multiple cognitions of blue simultaneously produced by a single blue particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), the nature of grasping a single object — blue — does not differ, so too among cognitions produced earlier and later, the nature of grasping an already-grasped object cannot be prevented.

body.text: atha niyataviṣayatvaṃ pūrvottaravijñānayoḥ pūrvotpannavijñānam anadhigatārthākārasvīkaraṇamukhenopādīyata, uttaraṃ tv adhigatārthākāraviṣayam upajāyate /
body.translated_text: Objection: The determinate objecthood of the earlier and later cognitions is as follows — the earlier-produced cognition is accepted through the appropriation of the form of an object not previously apprehended, while the later one arises having as its object the form of an already-apprehended object.

body.text: yadi gṛhītārthaviṣayatvaṃ kathaṃ pratiniyataviṣayatvam? atha pratiniyataviṣayatvaṃ kathaṃ gṛhītārthagrāhitvaṃ, niyataviṣayatvagṛhītagrāhitvayor virodhāt? yadi ca niyataviṣayatvaṃ, tadobhayor api prāmāṇyam anadhigatārthagantṛtvāviśeṣāt / athaikaviṣayatvaṃ, tadobhayor api prāmāṇyam aprāmāṇyaṃ vā gṛhītagrāhitvāviśeṣāt / so 'yaṃ gaḍupraveśākṣitārakavinirgamanyāyopanipātaḥ śrutilālasānāṃ duruttaraḥ /
body.translated_text: If it has an already-grasped object as its domain, how can it have a determinate object? And if it has a determinate object, how can it grasp an already-grasped object, since having a determinate object and grasping what is already grasped are contradictory? And if both have determinate objects, then both would be valid, since there would be no distinction in reaching an object not previously apprehended. If they have the same object, then both would be valid or both invalid, since there is no distinction in grasping what is already grasped. This falls under the maxim of 'when a boil enters, the pupil of the eye exits' — an unanswerable difficulty for those who delight in scriptural authority.

body.translated_text: 2.11 Objection: Even if validity is accepted when the object is already apprehended, the consequence would follow that memory too has validity, or has the status of a result of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇaphala</s>).

body.text: ko 'tra nivārayitā? smṛtir ihopajāyamānādyānubhavāveditārthākāraviṣayā vānyaviṣayā vā nirviṣayā vā /
body.translated_text: Who can prevent that? Is memory here directed toward the form of the object revealed by the initial experience that arises, or toward another object, or is it objectless?

body.text: tad yadi pūrvoditānubhavāveditārthākāraviṣayā, tadā tasyāḥ pramāṇaphalatā naiva nivārayituṃ pāryate gṛhītārthagrāhitvāviśeṣād ity uktam / evaṃ ca smṛtisañjñakaṃ saptamaṃ pramāṇaṃ prasaktaṃ mīmāṃsakānām / atha pūrvavijñānānavadhāritārthaviṣayā / yady evaṃ kathaṃ tasyāḥ pramāṇaphalatvam apanetuṃ pāryate? ādyānubhavasyeva smṛtirūpatā ca na prāpnoti / dṛṣṭaśrutārthaviṣayā hi smṛtir nāgṛhītārthaviṣayā /
body.translated_text: Now if it is directed toward the form of the object revealed by the aforementioned initial experience, then its status as a result of valid knowledge cannot be prevented at all, since there is no distinction in grasping an already-grasped object — as stated. And thus a seventh <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) called memory would be entailed for the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>. If it is directed toward an object not ascertained by the prior cognition — if so, how can its status as a result of valid knowledge be removed? And the character of memory would not apply to it, just as with the initial experience. For memory is directed toward objects that have been seen or heard, not toward objects not previously grasped.

children.text: tad yadi pūrvoditānubhavāveditārthākāraviṣayā, tadā tasyāḥ pramāṇaphalatā naiva nivārayituṃ pāryate gṛhītārthagrāhitvāviśeṣād ity uktam / evaṃ ca smṛtisañjñakaṃ saptamaṃ pramāṇaṃ prasaktaṃ mīmāṃsakānām / atha pūrvavijñānānavadhāritārthaviṣayā / yady evaṃ kathaṃ tasyāḥ pramāṇaphalatvam apanetuṃ pāryate? ādyānubhavasyeva smṛtirūpatā ca na prāpnoti / dṛṣṭaśrutārthaviṣayā hi smṛtir nāgṛhītārthaviṣayā /

body.text: atha nirviṣayeṣyate, tadā na gṛhītārthagrāhitvena smṛter aprāmāṇyam, api tu keśoṇḍukasaṃvedanavan nirviṣayatvena /
body.translated_text: Now if it is held to be objectless, then the invalidity of memory is not due to grasping an already-grasped object, but rather due to being objectless, like the perception of a hair-net (<s>keśoṇḍuka</s>).

body.text: api ca yadi nirviṣayā, tadā gṛhītārthagrāhiṇī katham? gṛhītārthagrāhiṇīti cen, nirviṣayeti na vaktavyam / na ca nirviṣayā / mātaraṃ pitaraṃ śuśrūṣitavān ahaṃ, santi me pañcabhṛtyeti pūrvānubhavāveditārthākāraparyavasāyinyo hi smṛtayaḥ, smṛtijñānena pūrvānubhavāveditārthākārasya pratibhāsanāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if it is objectless, then how does it grasp an already-grasped object? If it is said to grasp an already-grasped object, then it should not be called objectless. And it is not objectless. For memories such as 'I served my mother and father' and 'I have five servants' terminate in the form of an object revealed by prior experience, because the form of the object revealed by prior experience appears through the cognition of memory.

body.translated_text: Objection: At the time of the memory-cognition, the object that was made the domain of the prior awakening has ceased to exist, hence it is not the object of memory. And thus the invalidity of memory is due to objectlessness, not due to grasping an already-grasped object — so it was stated.

body.text: 2.2 yadi cāvadhāritārthaviṣayaṃ pramāṇam apramānam upapādyate, tadānumānajñānasyāprāmāṇyam āpanīpadyeta /
body.translated_text: 2.2 And if a means of knowledge directed toward an already-ascertained object is shown to be invalid, then the invalidity of inferential cognition would also follow.

body.text: tad eva katham? kathyate yad evāvinābhāvasambandhagrahaṇakālāvadhāritam agnitvasāmānyaṃ liṅgājahadvṛttitvena pratyakṣeṇa tad evānumānād avagacchaty āhosvit pāvakasvarūpaṃ matvarthaṃ vā liṅgavyāpārasamānakālīnāstitvaṃ vā liṅgopasarjanatvaṃ vāgnivyaktipāratantryaṃ vāgnitvasāmānyasya?
body.translated_text: How exactly? It is said: does one cognize through inference the very same universal of fire-ness (<s>agnitvasāmānya</s>) that was ascertained at the time of grasping the invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāvasambandha</s>) — since the inferential mark does not relinquish its function with respect to what was directly perceived — or does one cognize the essential nature of fire, or the possessive sense (indicated by the suffix '-mat'), or the existence contemporaneous with the operation of the inferential mark, or the subordination to the inferential mark, or the dependence of the fire-universal on the fire-particular?

body.text: 2.21 tad yadi pūrvāvadhāritasāmānyaviṣayam abhyupeyate, tadā prāmāṇyaṃ naiva samāsādayati gṛhītārthagrāhitvena smṛtivad eva / tadaprāmāṇye nāgnimattvavyavasthopapattiḥ / tadanupapattau ca nārthāpattyāgnivyaktisaṃsthitiḥ / tataś cāmutrāgnir agnir ānīyatām iti sakalalokavyavahāravira /haḥ syāt / atha mā bhūd etadvyavahārahānir iti cet pūrvāvadhārite 'py arthe 'numānasya prāmāṇyam abhyupeyate, tadānadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇam apārthakaṃ śrotriyāṇām iti /
body.translated_text: 2.21 If it is accepted that inference has the previously ascertained universal as its object, then it does not attain validity at all, since it grasps an already-grasped object, just like memory. If it is invalid, then the determination of the property of possessing fire is not established. And if that is not established, then the existence of the fire-particular through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) would not be established either. And consequently, the entire worldly practice of 'there is fire there' and 'let fire be brought' would be undermined. If it is said 'let there not be this loss of practical activity,' and validity of inference is accepted even regarding a previously ascertained object, then the qualifying term 'reaching an object not previously apprehended' would be meaningless for the learned.

body.text: 2.22 atha pāvakasvarūpam anumimīṣe, tal liṅgājahadvṛttitvena pūrvam avadhāritaṃ vā na vā / yadi pūrvopalabdham adhigatārthaviṣayatvam āyātam anumānasya / atha na pūrvopalabdham, avyāpako 'gnir anumānāt tarhi pratīyate / tadabhyupagame tṛṇajalādiviṣayam apy anumānaṃ prasajyate /
body.translated_text: 2.22 Now if you wish to infer the essential nature of fire — was that previously ascertained through the non-relinquishing function of the inferential mark, or not? If previously perceived, then the consequence of having an already-apprehended object follows for inference. If not previously perceived, then fire that does not pervade [smoke] would be cognized through inference. And if that is accepted, inference directed toward straw, water, and such would also absurdly follow.

body.text: 2.23 atha matvartho 'numīyate, sa pūrvāvadhārito vā na vā / yady avadhāritaḥ, katham anadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇam anumāne sambhavati?
body.translated_text: 2.23 Now if the possessive sense (indicated by '-mat') is what is inferred — was that previously ascertained or not? If ascertained, how can the qualifying term 'reaching an object not previously apprehended' apply to inference?

children.text: 2.23 atha matvartho 'numīyate, sa pūrvāvadhārito vā na vā / yady avadhāritaḥ, katham anadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇam anumāne sambhavati?

body.text: atha naivāvagatas, tadānīṃ jalatṛṇādiviṣayam apy anumānaṃ prasajyetety uktam /
body.translated_text: And if it was not apprehended, then — as stated — inference directed toward water, straw, and the like would also absurdly follow.

children.text: atha naivāvagatas, tadānīṃ jalatṛṇādiviṣayam apy anumānaṃ prasajyetety uktam /

body.text: 2.24 atha liṅgavyāpārasamānakālīnāstitvam agnitvasāmānyasyānumīyate, tad anumānavyāpārasamānakālīnāstitvam agnitvasāmānyād vyatiriktam avyatiriktaṃ vā / tad yady avyatiriktaṃ, tadānīṃ pūrvopalabdhāstitvaviṣayam evānumānam / katham anadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇam apārthakaṃ na bhavet?
body.translated_text: Now if the existence of the universal of <s>agnitva</s> (fireness) contemporaneous with the operation of the inferential mark is inferred, that existence contemporaneous with the operation of inference is either different from or identical with the universal of fireness. If identical, then the inference has as its object existence already previously apprehended. How would it not be meaningless, failing the qualification of being a cognizer of what is not previously known?

children.text: 2.24 atha liṅgavyāpārasamānakālīnāstitvam agnitvasāmānyasyānumīyate, tad anumānavyāpārasamānakālīnāstitvam agnitvasāmānyād vyatiriktam avyatiriktaṃ vā / tad yady avyatiriktaṃ, tadānīṃ pūrvopalabdhāstitvaviṣayam evānumānam / katham anadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇam apārthakaṃ na bhavet?

body.text: atha vyatiriktaṃ, tat kiṃ pūrvopalabdham anupalabdhaṃ vā?
body.translated_text: If different, is it previously apprehended or not apprehended?

children.text: atha vyatiriktaṃ, tat kiṃ pūrvopalabdham anupalabdhaṃ vā?

body.text: yadi pūrvopalabdhaṃ tadviṣayatve 'numānasya nānadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇam upapadyate / atha nopalabdhaṃ, tat katham anumīyate jalādikalpaṃ dhūmena?
body.translated_text: If previously apprehended, then with the inference having it as its object, the qualification of cognizing what is not previously known is not satisfied. If not apprehended, then how is it inferred by smoke — it being like water and such?

children.text: yadi pūrvopalabdhaṃ tadviṣayatve 'numānasya nānadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇam upapadyate / atha nopalabdhaṃ, tat katham anumīyate jalādikalpaṃ dhūmena?

body.text: 2.25 atha liṅgopasarjanatvam agnitvasāmānyasyānumānāt pratīyate, tal liṅgopasarjanatvam agnitvasāmānyād bhinnam abhinnaṃ vā / yady abhinnaṃ pūrvopalabdhāgnitvasāmānyaviṣayam evānumānaṃ, kathaṃ prāmāṇyabhāg bhavati? atha bhinnaṃ, tadavinābhāvasambandhagrahaṇakāle liṅgavyāpakatvenāvadhāritaṃ vā na vā /
body.translated_text: Now if the subordination to the inferential mark of the universal of fireness is apprehended through inference, that subordination to the inferential mark is either different from or identical with the universal of fireness. If identical, the inference has as its object the previously apprehended universal of fireness — how can it be authoritative? If different, then at the time of grasping the relation of invariable concomitance, was it ascertained as pervaded by the inferential mark, or not?

children.text: 2.25 atha liṅgopasarjanatvam agnitvasāmānyasyānumānāt pratīyate, tal liṅgopasarjanatvam agnitvasāmānyād bhinnam abhinnaṃ vā / yady abhinnaṃ pūrvopalabdhāgnitvasāmānyaviṣayam evānumānaṃ, kathaṃ prāmāṇyabhāg bhavati? atha bhinnaṃ, tadavinābhāvasambandhagrahaṇakāle liṅgavyāpakatvenāvadhāritaṃ vā na vā /

body.text: yady avadhāritaṃ katham anadhigatārthaviṣayam anumānam?
body.translated_text: If it was ascertained, how can the inference have as its object what is not previously known?

children.text: yady avadhāritaṃ katham anadhigatārthaviṣayam anumānam?

body.text: atha liṅgavyāpakatvenānavagataṃ, tadā tadviṣayatve 'numānasya parikalpyamāne tribhuvanāvedakatvaṃ dhūmasya kiṃ na parikalpyate sambandhābhāvāviśeṣāt?
body.translated_text: If it was not ascertained as pervaded by the inferential mark, then if the inference is constructed as having that as its object, why not construct smoke as the indicator of everything in the three worlds, since there is no difference in the absence of a relation?

children.text: atha liṅgavyāpakatvenānavagataṃ, tadā tadviṣayatve 'numānasya parikalpyamāne tribhuvanāvedakatvaṃ dhūmasya kiṃ na parikalpyate sambandhābhāvāviśeṣāt?

body.text: 2.26 athāgnivyaktipāra /tantryam anumīyate dhūmenāgnitvasāmānyasyeti cet, tat pāratantryam agnitvasāmānyasya dhūmavyāpakatvenāvadhāritaṃ vā na vā /
body.translated_text: If it is said that the dependence of the universal of fireness upon fire-instances is inferred by smoke — that dependence of the universal of fireness, was it ascertained as pervaded by smoke, or not?

children.text: 2.26 athāgnivyaktipāra /tantryam anumīyate dhūmenāgnitvasāmānyasyeti cet, tat pāratantryam agnitvasāmānyasya dhūmavyāpakatvenāvadhāritaṃ vā na vā /

body.text: yady avadhāritaṃ, punar api gṛhītagrāhitvaṃ nātivartate 'numānam / atha nāvadhāritaṃ dhūmavyāpakatvena pāratantryam agnisāmānyasyeti cet, katham anumīyatety uktaṃ purastāt /
body.translated_text: If it was ascertained, then once again the inference does not go beyond apprehending what is already grasped. If the dependence of the universal of fireness was not ascertained as pervaded by smoke — how is it inferred? This has been stated before.

children.text: yady avadhāritaṃ, punar api gṛhītagrāhitvaṃ nātivartate 'numānam / atha nāvadhāritaṃ dhūmavyāpakatvena pāratantryam agnisāmānyasyeti cet, katham anumīyata ity uktaṃ purastāt /

body.text: 2.3 etena pūrvopalabdhagotvādipratipādakatvena gośabdāder aprāmāṇyam udghāṭitam / tad eva katham? kathyate kiṃ saṅketagrahaṇakālāvagatagotvārthavācakatvaṃ tadvyatiriktārthavācakatvaṃ vā pratipādyate gośabdasya?
body.translated_text: By this, the non-authoritativeness of the word 'cow' and such, insofar as they convey the previously apprehended universal of <s>gotva</s> (cowness), has been exposed. How so? It is explained: does the word 'cow' convey the meaning of cowness as known at the time of learning the convention, or does it convey a meaning different from that?

children.text: 2.3 etena pūrvopalabdhagotvādipratipādakatvena gośabdāder aprāmāṇyam udghāṭitam / tad eva katham? kathyate -kiṃ saṅketagrahaṇakālāvagatagotvārthavācakatvaṃ tadvyatiriktārthavācakatvaṃ vā pratipādyate gośabdasya?

body.text: tad yadi saṅketagrahaṇakālādhigatagotvasvarūpāvedakatvaṃ jegīyate gośabdasya, tadā viditārthākārāvedakatvena na mānatvam āsādayati gośabdaḥ / atha veditārthākārāvedakatve 'pi prāmāṇyam āvahati, tadānadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇasya viṣayovaktavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the supremacy of the word 'cow' in making known the nature of cowness as apprehended at the time of learning the convention is proclaimed, then the word 'cow,' being a conveyor of an already known content, does not attain the status of a means of knowledge. If it is authoritative even though conveying already known content, then the object for which the qualification of cognizing what is not previously known applies must be stated.

children.text: tad yadi saṅketagrahaṇakālādhigatagotvasvarūpāvedakatvaṃ jegīyate gośabdasya, tadā viditārthākārāvedakatvena na mānatvam āsādayati gośabdaḥ / atha veditārthākārāvedakatve 'pi prāmāṇyam āvahati, tadānadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇasya viṣayovaktavyaḥ /

body.text: atha tadvyatiriktārthavācakatvaṃ, tadānīm asaṅketitaivārthaḥ pratīyate gośabdāt /tataś ca svasiddhāntapratītivirodho dumivāraḥ / atha gotvam evāvagamyate gośabdeneti cet, tatrāpi prapañcitam evāprāmāṇyakāraṇaṃ gṛhītagrāhitvam / tadaprāmāṇye na gotvavyavasthitiḥ / tadanavasthitau nārthāpattyādhikaraṇavyavasthitiḥ /
body.translated_text: If it conveys a meaning different from that, then what is understood from the word 'cow' would be a meaning not conventionally established. And thus the contradiction with one's own established doctrine is an irremovable thorn. If it is said that cowness alone is apprehended by the word 'cow' — there too the already-explained reason for non-authoritativeness, namely grasping what is already grasped, has been elaborated. If that is not authoritative, then the classification of cowness is not established. If that is not established, there is no establishment of the locus through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption).

children.text: atha tadvyatiriktārthavācakatvaṃ, tadānīm asaṅketita evārthaḥ pratīyate gośabdāt /tataś ca svasiddhāntapratītivirodho dumivāraḥ / atha gotvam evāvagamyate gośabdeneti cet, tatrāpi prapañcitam evāprāmāṇyakāraṇaṃ gṛhītagrāhitvam / tadaprāmāṇye na gotvavyavasthitiḥ / tadanavasthitau nārthāpattyādhikaraṇavyavasthitiḥ /

body.text: 2.31 ito 'pi nārthāpattyādhikaraṇavyavasthitir upapadyate kim arthāpattyā pūrvāvadhāritādhikaraṇapratyāyanaṃ kriyatāhosvid apūrvādhikaraṇapratyāyanam?
body.translated_text: Moreover, the establishment of the locus through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is not tenable. Does <s>arthāpatti</s> convey a locus that was previously ascertained, or does it convey a novel locus?

children.text: 2.31 ito 'pi nārthāpattyādhikaraṇavyavasthitir upapadyate -kim arthāpattyā pūrvāvadhāritādhikaraṇapratyāyanaṃ kriyatā ahosvid apūrvādhikaraṇapratyāyanam?

body.text: tad yadi pūrvāvadhāritādhikaraṇaparyavasitārthāpattis, tadā pratipāditārthapratipādakatvena na pramāṇam /
body.translated_text: If the <s>arthāpatti</s> is limited to a previously ascertained locus, then it is not a means of knowledge, being a conveyor of what has already been conveyed.

children.text: tad yadi pūrvāvadhāritādhikaraṇaparyavasitārthāpattis, tadā pratipāditārthapratipādakatvena na pramāṇam /

body.text: athādṛṣṭapiṇḍāvedakatvaṃ tadā gotvānyathānupapattyā gajavājikalpanāpi kāryā / atha pūrvāvadhāritasyedānīntanam astitvam arthāpattyāvasīyateti cet
body.translated_text: If it makes known a previously unseen individual, then by the impossibility of cowness being otherwise, the postulation of an elephant or horse should also be made. If it is said that the present existence of what was previously ascertained is determined through <s>arthāpatti</s> —

children.text: athādṛṣṭapiṇḍāvedakatvaṃ tadā gotvānyathānupapattyā gajavājikalpanāpi kāryā / atha pūrvāvadhāritasyedānīntanam astitvam arthāpattyāvasīyata iti cet

tad idānīntanam astitvaṃ pūrvāvadhāritād vyatiriktam avyatiriktaṃ vā /
tad yady avyatiriktaṃ, tadā pūrvāvadhāritārthapratipādakatvena katham arthāpatteḥ prāmāṇyaṃ vedavido vadanti?
body.translated_text: that present existence is either different from or identical with what was previously ascertained. If identical, then by conveying what was previously ascertained, how do the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s> proclaim the authoritativeness of <s>arthāpatti</s>?

body.translated_text: This being so, the statement that 'the present existence was not known by the prior cognition' is childish prattle.

body.translated_text: By this, the authoritativeness of <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) is also to be understood as refuted.
