body.text: Chapter 3: The Buddhist definition of means of valid cognition
3.1 tathā tāthāgatānām apy anadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇam apārthakam apohyajñānāsambhavāt / na hi pūrvāparakālabhāvinī vijñāna ekaviṣaye sto, na svalakṣaṇaikaviṣaye, na sāmānyaikaviṣaye,
body.translated_text: Likewise, even for the followers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Buddhists), the qualifier 'cognizer of what is not previously known' is meaningless, because the cognition of what is to be excluded (<s>apoha</s>) is impossible. For cognitions arising at earlier and later times do not have a single object — neither a single <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), nor a single <s>sāmānya</s> (universal),

children.text: 3.1 tathā tāthāgatānām apy anadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇam apārthakam apohyajñānāsambhavāt / na hi pūrvāparakālabhāvinī vijñāna ekaviṣaye sto, na svalakṣaṇaikaviṣaye, na sāmānyaikaviṣaye,

body.text: 3.11 svalakṣaṇasyābhinnaikasvabhāvasya kramavṛttyanekavijñānajananaśaktivyatirekāt / atha yugapadekaviṣayotpannānekavijñānāpanodārthaṃ,
body.translated_text: because the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, having a single undivided nature, lacks the capacity to produce multiple cognitions occurring in succession. If it is to refute multiple cognitions arising simultaneously with respect to a single object —

children.text: 3.11 svalakṣaṇasyābhinnaikasvabhāvasya kramavṛttyanekavijñānajananaśaktivyatirekāt / atha yugapadekaviṣayotpannānekavijñānāpanodārthaṃ,

body.text: tad apy ayuktam / ekaviṣayotpannānekapuruṣasaṃvedanasyāprāmāṇyam āpanīpadyeta /
body.translated_text: that too is not correct. The non-authoritativeness of the awareness of multiple persons produced by a single object would absurdly follow.

children.text: tad apy ayuktam / ekaviṣayotpannānekapuruṣasaṃvedanasyāprāmāṇyam āpanīpadyeta /

body.text: 3.12 atha sāmānyaikaviṣayānekavijñānāpanodārthaṃ viśeṣaṇam upādīyate, tad apy ayuktam / na sāmānYaikaṃ vijñānam asti, nāpy anekaṃ vijñānaṃ, tasya svayam asambhavāt / tadākāravirahe sāmānyaviṣayaṃ vijñānam iti pratikarmavyavasthāhetur vaktavyaḥ / tadākāre vā sāmānyasya sadātmatā / atāttvikākāratādātmye vā jñānātāttvikatvaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the qualifier is adopted to refute multiple cognitions having a single universal as their object — that too is not correct. There is neither a single cognition having a universal as its object, nor multiple cognitions, since the universal itself is non-existent. In the absence of the universal-form, the basis for the classification 'this is a cognition having a universal as its object' must be stated. Or if the universal's nature always consists of the form [of cognition] — or if identity with the non-real form is [granted], there would be the unwanted consequence of the unreality of cognition itself.

children.text: 3.12 atha sāmānyaikaviṣayānekavijñānāpanodārthaṃ viśeṣaṇam upādīyate, tad apy ayuktam / na sāmānYa ekaṃ vijñānam asti, nāpy anekaṃ vijñānaṃ, tasya svayam asambhavāt / tadākāravirahe sāmānyaviṣayaṃ vijñānam iti pratikarmavyavasthāhetur vaktavyaḥ / tadākāre vā sāmānyasya sadātmatā / atāttvikākāratādātmye vā jñānātāttvikatvaprasaṅgaḥ /

body.text: 3.1a kiṃ caikaviṣaye pravartamānayor ekasyāprāmāṇyaṃ pramāṇāntaratvābhāvo vā /
body.translated_text: Moreover, when two cognitions operate on a single object, is one of them non-authoritative, or is there no difference as a means of knowledge?

children.text: 3.1a kiṃ caikaviṣaye pravartamānayor ekasyāprāmāṇyaṃ pramāṇāntaratvābhāvo vā /

body.text: 3.1a tad yady aprāmāṇyaṃ, tad ayuktam / aviśiṣṭaikārthagṛhī tirūpatvobhayoḥ prāmāṇyam aprāmāṇyaṃ vā vikalpānupapatteḥ / vikalpe vaikaviṣayotpannānekapuruṣavijñānabhedaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: If non-authoritative — that is not correct. Since both have the undifferentiated form of grasping one object, both must be either authoritative or non-authoritative, because an alternative is untenable. And if an alternative is admitted, there would be the unwanted consequence that different cognitions of different persons produced by a single object would differ [in authority].

children.text: 3.1a1 tad yady aprāmāṇyaṃ, tad ayuktam / aviśiṣṭaikārthagṛhī tirūpatva ubhayoḥ prāmāṇyam aprāmāṇyaṃ vā vikalpānupapatteḥ / vikalpe vaikaviṣayotpannānekapuruṣavijñānabhedaprasaṅgaḥ /

body.text: 3.1a athāpramāṇāntaratvaṃ, tad apy anupapannam / kim ekaviṣayotpāditānekapratyakṣādijñānānāṃ vyaktinānātvaṃ nopapadyatāhākāranānātvam? tad yadi vyaktinānātvaṃ na jāghaṭīti, tad asad, ekanīlotpāditānekanīlālokavijñānānāṃ vyaktinānātvadarśanāt /
body.translated_text: If there is no difference as means of knowledge — that too is untenable. Is it the case that the plurality of instances among multiple perceptual cognitions etc. produced by a single object is not tenable, or that the plurality of forms is not tenable? If the plurality of instances is not tenable — that is wrong, because we observe the plurality of instances among multiple cognitions of blue produced by a single blue object, such as the cognition of sight and the cognition of illumination.

children.text: 3.1a2 athāpramāṇāntaratvaṃ, tad apy anupapannam / kim ekaviṣayotpāditānekapratyakṣādijñānānāṃ vyaktinānātvaṃ nopapadyatā ahā akāranānātvam? tad yadi vyaktinānātvaṃ na jāghaṭīti, tad asad, ekanīlotpāditānekanīlālokavijñānānāṃ vyaktinānātvadarśanāt /

body.text: athānekākāratā nopapadyate, tad ayuktaṃ, nīlālokavijñānānām anekākāratvadarśanāt / na ca tadutpādako nīlaprapañco 'sty, ekātmatayā svayam abhyupagamāt /
body.translated_text: If the plurality of forms is not tenable — that is not correct, because we observe the plurality of forms among cognitions of sight, illumination, and blue. And there is no manifold blue that produces them, since you yourself accept it as having a single nature.

children.text: athānekākāratā nopapadyate, tad ayuktaṃ, nīlālokavijñānānām anekākāratvadarśanāt / na ca tadutpādako nīlaprapañco 'sty, ekātmatayā svayam abhyupagamāt /

body.text: athaikaviṭayatve pratyakṣānumānavyapadeśānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: If having a single object makes the designation as perception and inference untenable —

children.text: athaikaviṭayatve pratyakṣānumānavyapadeśānupapattiḥ /

body.text: tad etad ayuktaṃ, bhinnakaraṇakāryatvena vyapadeśopapatteḥ / yathaikanīlotpannānekadevadattādijñānānāṃ bhinnakartṛkāryatvena devadattādijñānavyapadeśas tathehāpi /
body.translated_text: that is not correct, because the designation is tenable by virtue of being the products of different instruments. Just as among multiple cognitions of <s>Devadatta</s> etc. produced by a single blue object, the designation as '<s>Devadatta</s>'s cognition' etc. is possible by virtue of being the products of different agents, so too here.

children.text: tad etad ayuktaṃ, bhinnakaraṇakāryatvena vyapadeśopapatteḥ / yathaikanīlotpannānekadevadattādijñānānāṃ bhinnakartṛkāryatvena devadattādijñānavyapadeśas tathehāpi /

body.text: 3.2 anye tv avisaṃvādi jñānaṃ pramāṇam abhidadhati / ko 'yam avisaṃvādārthaḥ? kiṃ yathāvyavasthitārthagṛhītitvaṃ bādhārahitatvaṃ vā pratīyamānārthajanyatā vā pratīyamānārthaṃ prati pravartakatvaṃ vārthaprāpakatvaṃ vā?
body.translated_text: Others, however, define a means of knowledge as a cognition that is <s>avisaṃvādi</s> (non-deceptive). What is the meaning of 'non-deceptive'? Is it (1) grasping an object as it is established, (2) being free from sublation, (3) being produced by the apprehended object, (4) prompting activity toward the apprehended object, or (5) leading to the attainment of the object?

children.text: 3.2 anye tv avisaṃvādi jñānaṃ pramāṇam abhidadhati / ko 'yam avisaṃvādārthaḥ? kiṃ yathāvyavasthitārthagṛhītitvaṃ bādhārahitatvaṃ vā pratīyamānārthajanyatā vā pratīyamānārthaṃ prati pravartakatvaṃ vārthaprāpakatvaṃ vā?

body.text: 3.21 tad yadi yathāvyavasthitārthagṛhītitvaṃ, tad anumānajñāne nopapadyate /
body.translated_text: If it is grasping an object as it is established, that does not apply to inferential cognition.

children.text: 3.21 tad yadi yathāvyavasthitārthagṛhītitvaṃ, tad anumānajñāne nopapadyate /

body.text: 3.22 atha bādhārahitatvaṃ, tad apy anumānajñāne nopapadyate /
body.translated_text: If it is being free from sublation, that too does not apply to inferential cognition.

children.text: 3.22 atha bādhārahitatvaṃ, tad apy anumānajñāne nopapadyate /

body.text: 3.23 atha pratīyamānārthotpādyatvaṃ, tad apy anumānajñānasya nopapadyate, sāmānyākārasya janakatvavyāvṛtteḥ /
body.translated_text: If it is being produced by the apprehended object, that too does not apply to inferential cognition, because the universal-form is excluded from being a producer.

children.text: 3.23 atha pratīyamānārthotpādyatvaṃ, tad apy anumānajñānasya nopapadyate, sāmānyākārasya janakatvavyāvṛtteḥ /

body.text: tathā rāgādisaṃvedanasyāpy avabhātārthotpādyatvaṃ nopapadyate, svātmotpādane sāmarthyavyatirekāt / tathā yogipratyakṣasya pratīyamānārthajanyatā na sambhavati vyatītānāgatayor ajanakatvāt / janakatve vātītānāgatatā hīyate /
body.translated_text: Likewise, the awareness of passion and other emotions also lacks the characteristic of being produced by the apprehended object, because of the absence of capacity in producing itself. Similarly, the perception of the <s>yogin</s> cannot have the characteristic of being produced by the apprehended object, because past and future objects are not producers. Or if they are producers, their past-ness and future-ness would be lost.

children.text: tathā rāgādisaṃvedanasyāpy avabhātārthotpādyatvaṃ nopapadyate, svātmotpādane sāmarthyavyatirekāt / tathā yogipratyakṣasya pratīyamānārthajanyatā na sambhavati vyatītānāgatayor ajanakatvāt / janakatve vātītānāgatatā hīyate /

body.text: 3.24 atha pratīyamānārthaṃ prati pravartakatvam avisaṃvādārthas, tad viparyayajñānasyāpi pravartakatvaṃ vidyate / viparītotpannodakabuddhiḥ pravartate, na ca tasyāvisaṃvādo 'sti / satyodakajñāne 'pi jāte na pravartate kenāpi hetunā, tad api visaṃvādi syāt /
body.translated_text: If non-deceptiveness means prompting activity toward the apprehended object, then even erroneous cognition has the capacity to prompt activity. One who produces the cognition of water in a mirage is prompted to act, yet that cognition is not non-deceptive. Even when true water-cognition arises, one may not act due to some reason — then that too would be deceptive.

children.text: 3.24 atha pratīyamānārthaṃ prati pravartakatvam avisaṃvādārthas, tad viparyayajñānasyāpi pravartakatvaṃ vidyate / viparītotpannodakabuddhiḥ pravartate, na ca tasyāvisaṃvādo 'sti / satyodakajñāne 'pi jāte na pravartate kenāpi hetunā, tad api visaṃvādi syāt /

body.text: 3.25 athārthaprāpakatvam avisaṃvādas, tatra kim arthamātraprāpakatvam āho 'vabhātārthaprāpakatvaṃ tajjātīyodakaprāpakatvaṃ vā svotpādakārthaprāpakatvaṃ vātha svotpādakakārakāṇāṃ dhruvabhāvitvam avisaṃvādaḥ?
body.translated_text: If non-deceptiveness means leading to the attainment of the object — does it mean leading to the attainment of any object whatsoever, or leading to the attainment of the apprehended object, or leading to the attainment of water of the same type, or leading to the attainment of the object that produced [the cognition], or does non-deceptiveness mean the guaranteed future existence of its own causal factors?

children.text: 3.25 athārthaprāpakatvam avisaṃvādas, tatra kim arthamātraprāpakatvam āho 'vabhātārthaprāpakatvaṃ tajjātīyodakaprāpakatvaṃ vā svotpādakārthaprāpakatvaṃ vātha svotpādakakārakāṇāṃ dhruvabhāvitvam avisaṃvādaḥ?

body.text: yady arthamātraprāpakatvaṃ, keśoṇḍukendudvayasaṃvedanasyāpy avisaṃvāditvam āpadyate / athāvabhātārthaprāpakatvaṃ, tadānumānajñānasyāvisaṃvāditvaṃ na labhyate 'vabhātārthāprāpakatvāt / anumānajñāne hi sāmānyākāro 'vabhāti, na cāsau prāpyate svayam asattvāt /
body.translated_text: If it means leading to the attainment of any object whatsoever, then even the awareness of hair-nets, double moons, and such would absurdly be non-deceptive. If it means leading to the attainment of the apprehended object, then inferential cognition would not be non-deceptive, because it does not lead to the attainment of the apprehended object. For in inferential cognition, the universal-form appears, yet that is not attained, since it does not exist in itself.

children.text: yady arthamātraprāpakatvaṃ, keśoṇḍukendudvayasaṃvedanasyāpy avisaṃvāditvam āpadyate / athāvabhātārthaprāpakatvaṃ, tadānumānajñānasyāvisaṃvāditvaṃ na labhyate 'vabhātārthāprāpakatvāt / anumānajñāne hi sāmānyākāro 'vabhāti, na cāsau prāpyate svayam asattvāt /

body.text: tathā yogijñānasyātītānāgatārthe samutpannasyārthaprāpakatvaṃ na vidyate / tathā rāgādisaṃvedane 'pi jāte nāvabhātarāgādiprāptir asti / tathā pratyakṣe pi vijñāne nāvabhātārthaprāptir asti kṣaṇikatvenāstamitatvāt / atha tajjātīyodakaprāpakatvenāvisaṃvāditvam ucyate, tad ayuktam udakatvajāter abhāvāt / athānudakatvavyāvṛttir jātir ity ucyate, sodakavyaktibhyo 'vyatiriktā vyatiriktā vā / yady avyatiriktā tadā vyaktir eva na jātiḥ / atha vyatiriktā sā vastubhūtāvastubhūtā vā / yadi vastubhūtā tadābhyupetahāniḥ / athāvastubhūtā tadgatiḥ katham?
body.translated_text: Similarly, the yogic cognition that has arisen regarding past and future objects does not have the capacity to make one reach the object. Similarly, even when the experience of passion and the like has arisen, there is no attainment of the perceived passion. Similarly, even in perceptual cognition, there is no attainment of the perceived object, since it has ceased at the next moment due to being momentary. Now if non-deceptiveness (<s>avisaṃvāditva</s>) is defined as the capacity to make one reach water of the same class, that is not justified, because of the non-existence of the universal 'water-ness.' If it is said that the universal is the exclusion from non-water-ness — is that exclusion non-different or different from water-particulars? If non-different, then it is just the particular, not the universal. If different, is it a real entity or a non-entity? If a real entity, then there is a loss of one's own thesis. If a non-entity, then how can it function?

children.text: tathā yogijñānasyātītānāgatārthe samutpannasyārthaprāpakatvaṃ na vidyate / tathā rāgādisaṃvedane 'pi jāte nāvabhātarāgādiprāptir asti / tathā pratyakṣe pi vijñāne nāvabhātārthaprāptir asti kṣaṇikatvenāstamitatvāt / atha tajjātīyodakaprāpakatvenāvisaṃvāditvam ucyate, tad ayuktam udakatvajāter abhāvāt / athānudakatvavyāvṛttir jātir ity ucyate, sodakavyaktibhyo 'vyatiriktā vyatiriktā vā / yady avyatiriktā tadā vyaktir eva na jātiḥ / atha vyatiriktā sā vastubhūtāvastubhūtā vā / yadi vastubhūtā tadābhyupetahāniḥ / athāvastubhūtā tadgatiḥ katham?

body.text: na codakavyaktīnāṃ nānātvam upapadyate / yathā ca nopapadyate tathā niveditaṃ naiyāyikapratyakṣalakṣaṇādhikāre /
body.translated_text: Nor is the plurality of water-particulars tenable. How it is not tenable has been explained in the section on the <s>Naiyāyika</s> definition of perception.

children.text: na codakavyaktīnāṃ nānātvam upapadyate / yathā ca nopapadyate tathā niveditaṃ naiyāyikapratyakṣalakṣaṇādhikāre /

body.text: atha svotpādakārthaprāpakatvam avisaṃvādakatvaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, nayanālokamanaskārādeḥ pratyastamitatvāt /
body.translated_text: If non-deceptiveness means the capacity to make one reach the object that produced it, that is not justified, because the eye, light, mental attention, and other causal factors have already ceased.

children.text: atha svotpādakārthaprāpakatvam avisaṃvādakatvaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, nayanālokamanaskārādeḥ pratyastamitatvāt /

body.text: atha svotpādakakārakāṇāṃ dhruvabhāvitvam avisaṃvādas, tadabhāve tadabhāvaprasaṅgāt / yady evaṃ keśoṇḍukavijñānasyāpi dhruvabhāvikāraṇatvenāvisaṃvādo 'sty anyathākasmikatvaprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: If non-deceptiveness is the certainty that the causal factors of its own production invariably exist — in their absence, the absence of that cognition would follow. If so, then even the cognition of hair-nets would be non-deceptive, since its causes are certain; otherwise, the absurd consequence of being uncaused would follow.

children.text: atha svotpādakakārakāṇāṃ dhruvabhāvitvam avisaṃvādas, tadabhāve tadabhāvaprasaṅgāt / yady evaṃ keśoṇḍukavijñānasyāpi dhruvabhāvikāraṇatvenāvisaṃvādo 'sty anyathākasmikatvaprasaṅgāt /

body.text: evaṃ cāvyavasthite yad uktaṃ na hy ābhyām arthaṃ paricchidya pravartamāno 'rthakriyāyāṃ visaṃvādyateti tad bālavilasitam /
body.translated_text: Since this is thus unsettled, what was said — 'one who acts after ascertaining an object through these two is not deceived in causal efficacy' — that is mere child's play.

children.text: evaṃ cāvyavasthite yad uktaṃ na hy ābhyām arthaṃ paricchidya pravartamāno 'rthakriyāyāṃ visaṃvādyata iti tad bālavilasitam /

body.text: 3.3 tathā mānameyasaṅkhyāpi saugatamate nopapadyate / tad eva katham? kathyate dva eva pramāṇe, na mānāntaram asti / tad dvitvaṃ kiṃ vyaktibhedenākārabhedena viṣayabhedena vā?
body.translated_text: [3.3] Similarly, the enumeration of the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and objects of valid knowledge (<s>prameya</s>) is also not tenable in the <s>Saugata</s> (Buddhist) position. How exactly? It is said: 'there are only two <s>pramāṇas</s>, there is no other means.' Is that duality by difference of particular instances, by difference of form, or by difference of object?

children.text: 3.3 tathā mānameyasaṅkhyāpi saugatamate nopapadyate / tad eva katham? kathyate -dva eva pramāṇe, na mānāntaram asti / tad dvitvaṃ kiṃ vyaktibhedenākārabhedena viṣayabhedena vā?

body.text: 3.31 yadi vyaktibhedena, tadāparisaṅkhyeyatvaṃ jñānavyaktīnām ānantyād, dvitvānupapattiḥ / na ca jñānānāṃ bhedo 'sty ajñānād dhi jñānaṃ jñānātmatayā bhidyate, jñānāntarāt tu kathaṃ nivartate? kiṃ jñānātmatayākārāntareṇa vā? yadi jñānākāratayā bhidyate, tadānyeṣām ajñānātmakatvaprasaṅgo rasāder iva / athākārāntareṇa vyāvartate, tadājñānātmatā tasyotpadyate rasāder iva /
body.translated_text: [3.31] If by difference of particular instances, then there would be innumerability, since the particular instances of cognition are infinite — the duality would not be established. Nor is there any difference among cognitions; for cognition is distinguished from non-cognition by its nature as cognition, but how is it distinguished from another cognition? By its nature as cognition or by another form? If it is distinguished by its nature as cognition, then the consequence follows that other things are not of the nature of cognition, just as with taste and the like. If it is distinguished by another form, then the nature of non-cognition would arise in it, just as with taste and the like.

children.text: 3.31 yadi vyaktibhedena, tadāparisaṅkhyeyatvaṃ jñānavyaktīnām ānantyād, dvitvānupapattiḥ / na ca jñānānāṃ bhedo 'sty-- ajñānād dhi jñānaṃ jñānātmatayā bhidyate, jñānāntarāt tu kathaṃ nivartate? kiṃ jñānātmatayākārāntareṇa vā? yadi jñānākāratayā bhidyate, tadānyeṣām ajñānātmakatvaprasaṅgo rasāder iva / athākārāntareṇa vyāvartate, tadājñānātmatā tasyotpadyate rasāder iva /

body.text: 3.32 athākārabhedena mānayor bhedaḥ, so 'py anupapannaiva / jñānākāravyatirekeṇa pratyakṣānumānayor nākārāntaram asti / tadupagame vā jñānākāravirahaḥ syāt / na cākārasamūhātmakaṃ jñānaṃ tasyābhinnātmakatvāt /
body.translated_text: [3.32] If the distinction of the two means of knowledge is by difference of form, that too is simply untenable. Apart from the cognition-form, there is no other form in perception and inference. If such another form were admitted, there would be an absence of the cognition-form. Nor is cognition an aggregate of forms, since its nature is undifferentiated.

children.text: 3.32 athākārabhedena mānayor bhedaḥ, so 'py anupapanna eva / jñānākāravyatirekeṇa pratyakṣānumānayor nākārāntaram asti / tadupagame vā jñānākāravirahaḥ syāt / na cākārasamūhātmakaṃ jñānaṃ tasyābhinnātmakatvāt /

body.text: 3.33 atha viṣayabhedena dvaividhyam upapādyate,
body.translated_text: [3.33] If the duality is established by difference of object,

children.text: 3.33 atha viṣayabhedena dvaividhyam upapādyate,

body.text: 3.331 tadānumānajñānasya viṣayārtho vaktavyaḥ kim agnyādisvalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ vidyamānasāmānyaviṣayam apāramārthikasāmānyaviṣayaṃ vā nirviṣayaṃ vā svāṃśaviṣayaṃ vā?
body.translated_text: [3.331] Then the object of inferential cognition must be stated: Is it the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) such as fire, an existent universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), a non-ultimate universal, objectless, or having its own aspect as object?

children.text: 3.331 tadānumānajñānasya viṣayārtho vaktavyaḥ kim agnyādisvalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ vidyamānasāmānyaviṣayam apāramārthikasāmānyaviṣayaṃ vā nirviṣayaṃ vā svāṃśaviṣayaṃ vā?

body.text: yadyagnyādisvalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ, tadā pratyakṣānumānayor bhedānupapattir abhinnaviṣayatvāt / athānumānike jñāne 'gnimātraṃ pratīyate, pratyakṣe tu tārṇādiviśeṣātmatayā pratīyate / yady evaṃ svalakṣaṇaviṣayatvaṃ nātivartate 'numānasya, yadi nāma vahner eva prapañcatā / atha satsāmānyaviṣayatvaṃ, tathāpi pratyakṣānumānayor na bhedo 'sti sāmānyasya svalakṣaṇarūpatvāt / na ca satsāmānyasya vijñānaviṣayatopapadyate nityatvena janakatvākārārpakatvānupapatteḥ / na ca satsāmānyaviṣayatve bhrāntatopapadyate / bhrāntir apy arthasambandhataḥ prameti na vaktavyam /
body.translated_text: If it has a particular such as fire as its object, then the distinction between perception and inference would not be established, since they would have the same object. If in inferential cognition only 'fire in general' is perceived, while in perception it is perceived with particular characteristics such as straw-burning — even so, inference does not transcend having a particular as its object, if fire itself is merely elaborated upon. If it has an existent universal as its object, even then there is no difference between perception and inference, because the universal is of the nature of a particular. Nor is it tenable that a real universal is an object of cognition, because being eternal, the impossibility of being a producer or of imparting its form to cognition follows. Nor in the case of having a real universal as its object is erroneousness tenable. Error too, being related to an object, should not be said to be a <s>pramā</s> (valid cognition).

children.text: yadyagnyādisvalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ, tadā pratyakṣānumānayor bhedānupapattir abhinnaviṣayatvāt / athānumānike jñāne 'gnimātraṃ pratīyate, pratyakṣe tu tārṇādiviśeṣātmatayā pratīyate / yady evaṃ svalakṣaṇaviṣayatvaṃ nātivartate 'numānasya, yadi nāma vahner eva prapañcatā / atha satsāmānyaviṣayatvaṃ, tathāpi pratyakṣānumānayor na bhedo 'sti sāmānyasya svalakṣaṇarūpatvāt / na ca satsāmānyasya vijñānaviṣayatopapadyate nityatvena janakatvākārārpakatvānupapatteḥ / na ca satsāmānyaviṣayatve bhrāntatopapadyate / bhrāntir apy arthasambandhataḥ prameti na vaktavyam /

body.text: athāsatsāmānyaviṣayaṃ, na tarhi tasya bhrāntatāsataḥ svena rūpeṇa vidyamānatvāt / na cāsad viṣayabhāvaṃ pratipadyate janakatvākārārpakatvavyatirekāt / avyatireke vā vastutvaprasaṅgaḥ / tatprasaktau ca pratyakṣānumānayor bhedānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: If it has a non-existent universal as object, then its erroneousness is not tenable, since what is non-existent exists in its own form. Nor can a non-existent thing assume the role of an object, since it lacks the capacity for producing and imparting its form. Or if it does not lack these, the consequence of being a real entity follows. And in that consequence, the distinction between perception and inference would not be established.

children.text: athāsatsāmānyaviṣayaṃ, na tarhi tasya bhrāntatāsataḥ svena rūpeṇa vidyamānatvāt / na cāsad viṣayabhāvaṃ pratipadyate janakatvākārārpakatvavyatirekāt / avyatireke vā vastutvaprasaṅgaḥ / tatprasaktau ca pratyakṣānumānayor bhedānupapattiḥ /

body.text: atha nirviṣayaṃ, na tarhi mānayor bhedo 'sty, anumānajñānasya viṣayāsambhavāt / nāpi bhrāntatā nirviṣayatvād eva / na ca jñānasya svasattāmātreṇa bhrāntatābhrāntatā copapadyate, kiṃ tu paropadhānavaśāt /
body.translated_text: If objectless, then there is no distinction between the two means of knowledge, since inferential cognition has no object. Nor is there erroneousness, precisely because it is objectless. And the erroneousness or non-erroneousness of cognition is not established merely by its own existence, but rather by the influence of something external.

children.text: atha nirviṣayaṃ, na tarhi mānayor bhedo 'sty, anumānajñānasya viṣayāsambhavāt / nāpi bhrāntatā nirviṣayatvād eva / na ca jñānasya svasattāmātreṇa bhrāntatābhrāntatā copapadyate, kiṃ tu paropadhānavaśāt /

body.text: atha svāṃśaviṣayaṃ, tathāpi pratyakṣānumānayor na nānātvam, ubhayoḥ svalakṣaṇaviṣayatvāt / na cānumānajñānasya bhrāntatā svāṃśasyāvañcanāt /
body.translated_text: If it has its own aspect as object, even so there is no plurality of perception and inference, since both have a particular as their object. Nor is inferential cognition erroneous, since its own aspect is not deceptive.

children.text: atha svāṃśaviṣayaṃ, tathāpi pratyakṣānumānayor na nānātvam, ubhayoḥ svalakṣaṇaviṣayatvāt / na cānumānajñānasya bhrāntatā svāṃśasyāvañcanāt /

body.text: 3.332 tathā pratyakṣasyāpi viṣayo vaktavyaḥ  kiṃ rūpādisvalakṣaṇaviṣayam ātmaviṣayam ubhayaviṣayaṃ vā?
body.translated_text: [3.332] Similarly, the object of perception must also be stated: Is it having only the particular such as color as its object, having the self as its object, or having both as its object?

children.text: 3.332 tathā pratyakṣasyāpi viṣayo vaktavyaḥ -- kiṃ rūpādisvalakṣaṇaviṣayam ātmaviṣayam ubhayaviṣayaṃ vā?

body.text: tad yadi rūpādimātrālocakaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ tadanavagatāvetadgatyabhāvāt /
body.translated_text: If it illuminates only color and the like, that is not justified, because without cognizing that cognition itself, there would be no means of ascertaining its course.

children.text: tad yadi rūpādimātrālocakaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ tadanavagatāvetadgatyabhāvāt /

body.text: atha jñānamātrakāyāvagāhakaṃ, tad api nopapadyate, viṣayabhāvasya janakatvākārārpakatvena vyavasthiteḥ / na ca svātmani janakatvam ākārārpakatvaṃ copapadyate / viṣayiṇam apekṣya viṣayo bhavati, yathā kāraṇam apekṣya kāryaṃ kāryaṃ cāpekṣya kāraṇaṃ tathehāpi /
body.translated_text: If it grasps merely the nature of cognition, that too is not tenable, because the status of being an object is established through being a producer and imparting one's form. And neither productivity nor form-imparting with respect to oneself is tenable. An object exists in dependence upon a cognizer, just as an effect exists in dependence upon a cause and a cause in dependence upon an effect — so too here.

children.text: atha jñānamātrakāyāvagāhakaṃ, tad api nopapadyate, viṣayabhāvasya janakatvākārārpakatvena vyavasthiteḥ / na ca svātmani janakatvam ākārārpakatvaṃ copapadyate / viṣayiṇam apekṣya viṣayo bhavati, yathā kāraṇam apekṣya kāryaṃ kāryaṃ cāpekṣya kāraṇaṃ tathehāpi /

body.text: yadi ca pratyakṣajñānenātmamātram ātmasātkriyate, tadānumāne 'py etad asti, pratyakṣānumānayor bhedānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: If by perceptual cognition only the self is appropriated, then this is present in inference too — hence the distinction between perception and inference would not be established.

children.text: yadi ca pratyakṣajñānenātmamātram ātmasātkriyate, tadānumāne 'py etad asti, pratyakṣānumānayor bhedānupapattiḥ /

body.text: athobhayaṃ viṣayīkriyate, tad apy ayuktam, ekopalambhasya dvitīyākāraparihāreṇa vyavasthitatvāt / yadi ca rūpagṛhītir eva jñānagṛhītis, tadā rūpasya jñānarūpatā, jñānasya vā rūparūpatā, rūpagṛhīter vā rūpāvyavasthāpakatvam / na caikasyākāradvayaṃ paśyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: If both are made objects, that too is not justified, because a single apprehension is established by excluding a second form. And if the grasping of form is itself the grasping of cognition, then either form would be of the nature of cognition, or cognition would be of the nature of form, or the grasping of form would not establish form. Nor do we observe two forms in a single cognition.

children.text: athobhayaṃ viṣayīkriyate, tad apy ayuktam, ekopalambhasya dvitīyākāraparihāreṇa vyavasthitatvāt / yadi ca rūpagṛhītir eva jñānagṛhītis, tadā rūpasya jñānarūpatā, jñānasya vā rūparūpatā, rūpagṛhīter vā rūpāvyavasthāpakatvam / na caikasyākāradvayaṃ paśyāmaḥ /

body.text: 3.3a na ca dvitvāvadhāraṇam ihopapadyate / pratyakṣaṃ jñānam ātmānaṃ gṛhṇad upajāyate, nānumānaṃ viṣayayati / tathānumānam apy ātmānam ātmasātkurvad upajāyate, na pratyakṣaṃ jñānam avadyotayati / evaṃ dvitvasaṅkhyāvyavahārānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: [3.3a] Nor is the ascertainment of duality tenable here. Perceptual cognition arises while grasping itself, and does not make inference an object. Similarly, inference also arises while appropriating itself, and does not illuminate perceptual cognition. Thus the practical usage of the number 'two' is not established.

children.text: 3.3a na ca dvitvāvadhāraṇam ihopapadyate / pratyakṣaṃ jñānam ātmānaṃ gṛhṇad upajāyate, nānumānaṃ viṣayayati / tathānumānam apy ātmānam ātmasātkurvad upajāyate, na pratyakṣaṃ jñānam avadyotayati / evaṃ dvitvasaṅkhyāvyavahārānupapattiḥ /

body.text: atha vikalpena dvayāvadhāraṇam iti cet, tad ayuktam, asāv apy ātmasaṃvedanaparyavasitatvān na dvayaṃ gṛhṇāti / grahaṇe vābhyupetahānam / tadanupapattau ca dva eveti jaḍaceṣṭitam /
body.translated_text: If it is objected that the ascertainment of the two is by conceptual thought (<s>vikalpa</s>) — that is not justified, because that thought too, being confined to self-awareness, does not grasp the two. Or if it does grasp them, there is a loss of one's own thesis. In the failure of establishing this, the statement 'there are only two' is foolish behavior.

children.text: atha vikalpena dvayāvadhāraṇam iti cet, tad ayuktam, asāv apy ātmasaṃvedanaparyavasitatvān na dvayaṃ gṛhṇāti / grahaṇe vābhyupetahānam / tadanupapattau ca dva eveti jaḍaceṣṭitam /

body.text: Chapter 4: Examintation of the Buddhist definition of pereception
4.1 tathā pratyakṣaṃ kalpanāpoḍham abhrāntam iti na vaktavyaṃ kalpanāpoḍhapadasyāpohyārthāsambhavāt /
body.translated_text: [4.1] Similarly, it should not be said that 'perception is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>) and non-erring,' because there is no possible object to be excluded by the term 'free from conceptual construction.'

children.text: 4.1 tathā pratyakṣaṃ kalpanāpoḍham abhrāntam iti na vaktavyaṃ kalpanāpoḍhapadasyāpohyārthāsambhavāt /

body.text: nanu kalpanaivāpohyā /
body.translated_text: Objection: It is precisely conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) that is to be excluded.

children.text: nanu kalpanaivāpohyā /

body.text: keyaṃkalpanā  kiṃ guṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣaṇotpāditaṃ vijñānaṃ kalpanāho smṛtyutpādakaṃ vijñānaṃ kalpanā smṛtirūpaṃ vā smṛtyutpādyaṃ vābhilāpasaṃsarganirbhāso vābhilāpavatī pratītir vā kalpanāspaṣṭākārā vātāttvikārthagṛhītirūpā vā svayaṃ vātāttvikī trirūpāl liṅgato 'rthadṛg vātītānāgatārthanirbhāsā vā?
body.translated_text: What is this conceptual construction? Is it (1) cognition produced by qualifiers such as quality, motion, universal, etc.; (2) cognition that produces memory; (3) of the form of memory; (4) produced by memory; (5) manifesting verbal association; (6) cognition involving words; (7) having an indistinct form; (8) grasping a non-real object; (9) itself non-real; or (10) cognition of an object through a triple-characterized logical mark apprehending past and future objects?

children.text: keyaṃkalpanā -- kiṃ guṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣaṇotpāditaṃ vijñānaṃ kalpanāho smṛtyutpādakaṃ vijñānaṃ kalpanā smṛtirūpaṃ vā smṛtyutpādyaṃ vābhilāpasaṃsarganirbhāso vābhilāpavatī pratītir vā kalpanāspaṣṭākārā vātāttvikārthagṛhītirūpā vā svayaṃ vātāttvikī trirūpāl liṅgato 'rthadṛg vātītānāgatārthanirbhāsā vā?

body.text: 4.11 tad yadi guṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣaṇotpāditaṃ vijñānaṃ kalpanā, tat kim avidyamānaguṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣanotpādyatvena kalpanota vidyamānotpādyatvena?
body.translated_text: [4.11] If conceptual construction is cognition produced by qualifiers such as quality, motion, universal, etc. — is it conceptual construction because it is produced by non-existent qualifiers of quality, motion, universal, etc., or because it is produced by existent ones?

children.text: 4.11 tad yadi guṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣaṇotpāditaṃ vijñānaṃ kalpanā, tat kim avidyamānaguṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣanotpādyatvena kalpanota vidyamānotpādyatvena?

body.text: tad yady avidyamānaguṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣaṇotpādyatvena kalpanātvaṃ, tad ayuktam avidyamānasya janakatvābhāvād evākalpanātvam / atha vidyamānaguṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣaṇotpādyatvena kalpanā, tat kiṃ saviṣayaṃ kalpanājñānaṃ nirviṣayaṃ vā? tad yadi saviṣayaṃ sat kalpanājñānaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, guṇacalanajātyādijanyatve 'pi na kalpanātvam arthasāmarthyasamudbhavatvasyānativṛtteḥ / atha nirviṣayaṃ sat kalpanā, tadā nirviṣayatvam eva kalpanātve kāraṇaṃ, na guṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣaṇajanyatvam / yadi ca tan nirviṣayaṃ, tadā na kalpanājñānaṃ nāpy akalpanājñānaṃ, jñānamātratā syāt / jñānātmatayā ca kalpanātve sarvaṃ jñānaṃ kalpanājñānaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: If it is conceptual construction because it is produced by non-existent qualifiers of quality, motion, universal, etc., that is not justified — precisely because what is non-existent lacks productivity, it would be non-conceptual. If conceptual construction is because it is produced by existent qualifiers of quality, motion, universal, etc., then is the conceptual-construction-cognition with an object or without an object? If the conceptual-construction-cognition has an object, that is not justified — because even though produced by quality, motion, universal, etc., it would not be conceptual construction, since its origination from the power of real things is not transcended. If it is conceptual construction because it is without an object, then objectlessness itself is the reason for being conceptual construction, not being produced by qualifiers of quality, motion, universal, etc. And if it is objectless, then it is neither conceptual-construction-cognition nor non-conceptual-construction-cognition — it would be mere cognition. And if being of the nature of cognition makes it conceptual construction, all cognition would be conceptual-construction-cognition.

children.text: tad yady avidyamānaguṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣaṇotpādyatvena kalpanātvaṃ, tad ayuktam avidyamānasya janakatvābhāvād evākalpanātvam / atha vidyamānaguṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣaṇotpādyatvena kalpanā, tat kiṃ saviṣayaṃ kalpanājñānaṃ nirviṣayaṃ vā? tad yadi saviṣayaṃ sat kalpanājñānaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, guṇacalanajātyādijanyatve 'pi na kalpanātvam arthasāmarthyasamudbhavatvasyānativṛtteḥ / atha nirviṣayaṃ sat kalpanā, tadā nirviṣayatvam eva kalpanātve kāraṇaṃ, na guṇacalanajātyādiviśeṣaṇajanyatvam / yadi ca tan nirviṣayaṃ, tadā na kalpanājñānaṃ nāpy akalpanājñānaṃ, jñānamātratā syāt / jñānātmatayā ca kalpanātve sarvaṃ jñānaṃ kalpanājñānaṃ syāt /

body.text: 4.12 atha smṛtyutpādakaṃ jñānaṃ kalpanā, tad ayuktaṃ, rūpādidarśanād api smṛtir utpadyate na ca kalpanātvaṃ, yatsannidhāne yo dṛṣṭas taddṛṣṭes taddhvanau smṛtir iti vacanāt /
body.translated_text: [4.12] If conceptual construction is cognition that produces memory, that is not justified, because memory arises even from seeing color and the like, yet that is not conceptual construction — as stated in the dictum: 'upon seeing in whose presence someone was seen, from the sight of that person, memory of the sound arises.'

children.text: 4.12 atha smṛtyutpādakaṃ jñānaṃ kalpanā, tad ayuktaṃ, rūpādidarśanād api smṛtir utpadyate na ca kalpanātvaṃ, yatsannidhāne yo dṛṣṭas taddṛṣṭes taddhvanau smṛtir iti vacanāt /

body.text: 4.13 atha smṛtirūpatvena kalpanā, tatrāpi kiṃ gṛhītagrāhitvena nirviṣayatvenāpūrvārthagṛhītirūpatvena vā? tad yadi gṛhītārthagrāhitvena kalpanātvaṃ, tadā prathamānubhavasyāpi kalpanātvam āpadyate gṛhītārthagrāhitvāviśeṣād ity uktaṃ purastāt / atha nirviṣayatvena, tadā na kalpanākāratā nāpy akalpanākāratā jñānākāravyatirekeṇa / athāpūrvārthagṛhītitvena kalpanātvaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, na smṛter apūrvārthagṛhītitvam asti / tadabhāvān na kalpanātvam / yadi cāpūrvārthagṛhītitvena kalpanātvaṃ, rūpādijñānānāṃ kalpanātvam āpadyate /
body.translated_text: 4.13 Now if <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction) is defined as being of the form of memory — in that case too, is it so by virtue of grasping what has been grasped, by virtue of being objectless, or by virtue of being of the form of grasping a novel object? If <s>kalpanā</s> is defined by grasping what has been grasped, then even the first experience would absurdly become <s>kalpanā</s>, since there is no difference in grasping what has been grasped — as was stated earlier. If by virtue of being objectless, then there would be neither conceptual-construction-form nor non-conceptual-construction-form, apart from the form of cognition itself. If <s>kalpanā</s> is defined by being of the form of grasping a novel object, that is unjustified — memory does not have the character of grasping a novel object. Due to its absence, there is no conceptual-construction-nature. And if <s>kalpanā</s> were defined by grasping a novel object, then cognitions of form and the like would absurdly become <s>kalpanā</s>.

children.text: 4.13 atha smṛtirūpatvena kalpanā, tatrāpi kiṃ gṛhītagrāhitvena nirviṣayatvenāpūrvārthagṛhītirūpatvena vā? tad yadi gṛhītārthagrāhitvena kalpanātvaṃ, tadā prathamānubhavasyāpi kalpanātvam āpadyate gṛhītārthagrāhitvāviśeṣād ity uktaṃ purastāt / atha nirviṣayatvena, tadā na kalpanākāratā nāpy akalpanākāratā jñānākāravyatirekeṇa / athāpūrvārthagṛhītitvena kalpanātvaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, na smṛter apūrvārthagṛhītitvam asti / tadabhāvān na kalpanātvam / yadi cāpūrvārthagṛhītitvena kalpanātvaṃ, rūpādijñānānāṃ kalpanātvam āpadyate /

body.text: 4.14 atha smṛtyutpādyatvena kalpanātvaṃ, tadā rūpādijñānasyāpi nirvikalpakatvenābhimatasya smṛtyutpādyatvam asti, tad astu kalpanājñānam / atha na bhavati tat kalpanājñānaṃ smṛtyā bodhasvabhāvatayotpāditaṃ, kalpanājñānaṃ tu smaraṇākāratayotpādyate / tad idaṃ madvikalpāndolitabuddher nirupapattikābhidhānam / na hy ekasya svabhāvadvayam upapaśyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 4.14 Now if <s>kalpanā</s> is defined by being produced by memory, then even cognition of form and the like, which is accepted as <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual), is produced by memory — so let it too be <s>kalpanā</s>-cognition. If it is objected that it is not <s>kalpanā</s>-cognition because it is produced by memory in its nature as awareness, while <s>kalpanā</s>-cognition is produced in its nature as recollection — this is an unjustified statement from one whose intellect is swayed by one's own conceptual constructions. For we do not observe a single thing having a dual nature.

children.text: 4.14 atha smṛtyutpādyatvena kalpanātvaṃ, tadā rūpādijñānasyāpi nirvikalpakatvenābhimatasya smṛtyutpādyatvam asti, tad astu kalpanājñānam / atha na bhavati tat kalpanājñānaṃ smṛtyā bodhasvabhāvatayotpāditaṃ, kalpanājñānaṃ tu smaraṇākāratayotpādyate / tad idaṃ madvikalpāndolitabuddher nirupapattikābhidhānam / na hy ekasya svabhāvadvayam upapaśyāmaḥ /

body.text: 4.15 athābhilāpasaṃsargapratibhāsā pratītiḥ kalpanā, sa saṃsargaḥ pāramārthiko 'pāramārthiko vā / yadi pāramārthiko, na tadā tasya kalpanātvaṃ rūpādijñānasyeva / athāpāramārthikaḥ, kathaṃ tadābhaṃ vijñānaṃ nairātmyaprasaṅgāt? na cātāttvike viṣayārthaḥ kaścil labhyate janakatvākārārpakatvasahotpādasattāmātravyatirekāt / yadi cātāttvikārthagṛhītirūpaṃ, tadā viparyayajñānam / tac cāvyabhicāripadenāpoditaṃ, na kalpanāpoḍhapadam upādeyam /
body.translated_text: 4.15 Now if <s>kalpanā</s> is a cognition manifesting verbal association (<s>abhilāpasaṃsarga</s>), is that association ultimate or non-ultimate? If ultimate, then it would not be <s>kalpanā</s>, just like cognition of form and the like. If non-ultimate, how can that appearance be cognition, given the consequence of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness)? And in the case of a non-ultimate object, no purpose whatsoever is obtained, since apart from productivity, form-imparting, co-arising, and mere existence there is nothing else. And if it is of the form of grasping a non-ultimate object, then it would be erroneous cognition. That has been refuted by the term '<s>avyabhicāri</s>' (non-erring) — the term '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>' (free from conceptual construction) need not be adopted.

children.text: 4.15 athābhilāpasaṃsargapratibhāsā pratītiḥ kalpanā, sa saṃsargaḥ pāramārthiko 'pāramārthiko vā / yadi pāramārthiko, na tadā tasya kalpanātvaṃ rūpādijñānasyeva / athāpāramārthikaḥ, kathaṃ tadābhaṃ vijñānaṃ nairātmyaprasaṅgāt? na cātāttvike viṣayārthaḥ kaścil labhyate janakatvākārārpakatvasahotpādasattāmātravyatirekāt / yadi cātāttvikārthagṛhītirūpaṃ, tadā viparyayajñānam / tac cāvyabhicāripadenāpoditaṃ, na kalpanāpoḍhapadam upādeyam /

body.text: 4.16 athābhilāpavātī pratītiḥ kalpanā, kim abhilāpātmikāho 'bhilāpotpādyābhilāpagṛhītir vā? tad yady abhilāpātmikā, pratītiḥ katham? pratītiś ced abhilāpātmiketi na vaktavyaṃ, viruddhākārayos tādātmyavyatirekāt / athābhilāpotpādyā, tadā śabdajñānānāṃ kalpanātvam āpadyate / teṣāṃ ca kalpanātve śabdavyavasthānupapattiḥ syāt / athābhilāpagṛhītitvena kalpanātvaṃ, tadā sarvāsām abhilāpagṛhītīnāṃ kalpanātvam āpadyate / tatkalpanātve śabdavyavasthānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: 4.16 Now if <s>kalpanā</s> is a cognition involving words (<s>abhilāpavat</s>) — is it of the nature of words, produced by words, or a grasping of words? If it is of the nature of words, how can it be a cognition? If it is a cognition, it should not be said to be of the nature of words, because there is a distinction between contradictory forms. If it is produced by words, then verbal cognitions would absurdly become <s>kalpanā</s>. And if they become <s>kalpanā</s>, the convention regarding verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) would be untenable. If <s>kalpanā</s> is defined by grasping words, then all graspings of words would absurdly become <s>kalpanā</s>. If they become <s>kalpanā</s>, the convention regarding verbal testimony would be untenable.

children.text: 4.16 athābhilāpavātī pratītiḥ kalpanā, kim abhilāpātmikāho 'bhilāpotpādyābhilāpagṛhītir vā? tad yady abhilāpātmikā, pratītiḥ katham? pratītiś ced abhilāpātmiketi na vaktavyaṃ, viruddhākārayos tādātmyavyatirekāt / athābhilāpotpādyā, tadā śabdajñānānāṃ kalpanātvam āpadyate / teṣāṃ ca kalpanātve śabdavyavasthānupapattiḥ syāt / athābhilāpagṛhītitvena kalpanātvaṃ, tadā sarvāsām abhilāpagṛhītīnāṃ kalpanātvam āpadyate / tatkalpanātve śabdavyavasthānupapattiḥ /

body.text:
4.17 athāspaṣṭākārā pratītiḥ kalpanā, aspaṣṭatā kā? kim avijñānātmakatvam āho svalakṣaṇājanyatvam atha pratīyamānārthājanyatvaṃ pratīyamānāsatyatā vā svalakaṇāpratibhāsitā vā? tad yady avijñānātmakatvam aspaṣṭatā, tad ayuktaṃ, pratītir ihāspaṣṭākārā gīyate, sā katham avijñānātmikā bhavitum arhati? atha svalakṣaṇājanyatāspaṣṭatā, tadā jñānākasmikatvaprasaṅgaḥ / atha pratīyamānārthājanyatvaṃ, tadā rāgādisaṃvedanasyāspaṣṭatā prāpnoti, rāgādīnāṃ svātmasaṃvedanotpādakatvāyogāt / svātmotpādakatvaṃ vastūnāṃ na dṛṣṭapūrvam / tathā keśoṇḍukavijñānasya pratīyamānakeśoṇḍukotpādyatvaṃ na vidyate / tad api spaṣṭābham upajāyate, na tv aspaṣṭābhaṃ, na vikalpānubaddhasya spaṣṭārthapratibhāsiteti vacanāt / atha svalakṣaṇāpratibhāsitvam
aspaṣṭatā, tadā nirvikalpābhimatakeśoṇḍukavijñānasyāspaṣṭatā prāpnoti, tatra svalakṣaṇasyāpratibhāsanāt,
spaṣṭābhaṃ ca tad gīyate / na ca tāthāgate darśane tathābhūtaṃ jñānam asti yat svalakṣaṇāpratibhāsi, sarvasmin jñāne jñānakāyapratibhāsanāt / atha pratīyamānāsatyātāspaṣṭatā, tadā keśoṇḍukendudvayavijñānasyāspaṣṭatā prāpnoti / na ca pratīyamānasyāsatyatā vijñānakāyasya pratīyamānatvāt / na ca tasya visaṃvādo 'sti /
body.translated_text: 4.17 Now if <s>kalpanā</s> is a cognition with indistinct form (<s>aspaṣṭākāra</s>), what is indistinctness? Is it (1) not being of the nature of cognition, (2) not being produced by a particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), (3) not being produced by the apprehended object, (4) the unreality of the apprehended object, or (5) the non-appearance of the particular? If indistinctness is not being of the nature of cognition, that is unjustified — what is declared here as having an indistinct form is a cognition; how can it be not of the nature of cognition? If indistinctness is not being produced by a particular, then the consequence of being uncaused follows for cognition. If indistinctness is not being produced by the apprehended object, then the awareness of passion and the like would be indistinct, because passion and the like lack the capacity to produce self-awareness. The productivity of things with respect to themselves has never been observed. Similarly, the cognition of hair-nets does not have the characteristic of being produced by the apprehended hair-net. That cognition too arises with a distinct appearance, not with an indistinct one — as stated in the dictum: 'what is connected with conceptual construction does not have the appearance of a distinct object.' If indistinctness is the non-appearance of the particular, then the <s>nirvikalpaka</s> cognition of hair-nets, which is accepted as non-conceptual, would be indistinct, because in it the particular does not appear, yet it is declared as having a distinct appearance. Nor in the <s>Tāthāgata</s> (Buddhist) system does there exist such a cognition that does not manifest a particular, because in all cognition the cognition-body appears. If indistinctness is the unreality of the apprehended, then the cognition of hair-nets and double moons would be indistinct. Nor is the unreality of the apprehended established for the cognition-body, since it is apprehended. Nor is there deceptiveness regarding it.

body.translated_text: 4.1(10) If it is objected that <s>kalpanā</s> is the cognition of an object through a triple-characterized logical mark — that too, is it <s>kalpanā</s> by virtue of being produced by the mark, or by virtue of being objectless? If <s>kalpanā</s> is defined by being produced by the logical mark, then even the <s>nirvikalpaka</s> cognition that apprehends the mark would absurdly become <s>kalpanā</s>. Nor is inferential cognition directly produced by the logical mark without mediation. If <s>kalpanā</s> is defined by being objectless, that too is not justified, because inferential cognition has its own aspect as object. If it is said that no object exists apart from its own aspect, and therefore it is designated as <s>kalpanā</s> due to objectlessness — then even the cognition of hair-nets would absurdly become <s>kalpanā</s>.

/ piśācaparamāṇumaheśvarakalpārthotpāditaṃ kāryaṃ nehopalabhyate / atha
jñānam eva tasya liṅgaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, tena saha tasya sambandhānavagateś cinmātratayaiva na tv anyo 'rthaḥ / na ca cid ātmānaṃ janayati / samanantarajñānaṃ tasya hetur iti cet, tad ayuktaṃ, tadavagatau na mānam asti / parasantānajñānārthakalpaṃ tad api na svasaṃvedyaṃ tatkāryajñānasya, tato bhinnatvāt parasantānajñānārthavat / nāpyanumāṭena, tadāyattatāyānavagateḥ / cinmātratayaivātmānam avagāhayati, nānyāyattatayā, tato 'nyasya piśāceśvaratulyatvāt / yadi ca samanantaravijñānotpādyatvena spaṣṭatā, tadānumānajñānasyāpi samanantarajñānotpādyatvena nirvikalpakatvam anuṣaktam /
body.translated_text: 4.1(10)a1 If it is being produced by a particular — is it being produced by the particular that appears in cognition, or being produced by a particular different from that? If it is being produced by the particular that appears in cognition, what appears in cognition? Is it the object, the cognition, or both? If the object — that is unjustified, because in an unestablished cognition, it does not appear. If the cognition — then it does not produce itself, due to the impossibility of action upon oneself. If both appear — that is unjustified, because a single apprehension is established by excluding a second form. And if both appear, then it would absurdly follow that cognition is produced by cognition just as by the object. That too is unjustified due to the impossibility of action upon oneself. If it is being produced by a particular that does not appear — how is that ascertained? Not by perception, precisely because it does not appear. Nor by inference, because neither a <s>svabhāva</s> (nature) nor a <s>kārya</s> (effect) logical mark is apprehended. A <s>svabhāva</s>-inference is not possible because, when the identity and that thing are not ascertained, the inference is not ascertained. Nor is a <s>kārya</s>-inference possible, because no effect belonging to it is apprehended — no effect produced by a hypothetical atom, <s>Maheśvara</s> (God), or spirit is apprehended here. If it is said that cognition itself is the logical mark for it — that is unjustified, because the relation between them is not ascertained; it is mere cognition and no other object. And cognition does not produce itself. If it is objected that the immediately preceding cognition is its cause — that is unjustified, because there is no means of knowledge for ascertaining that. The cognition of another's mental continuum, like the object of another's mental continuum, is not self-cognizable by that effect-cognition, because it is different from it, just like the cognition and object of another's continuum. Nor by inference, because dependence upon it is not ascertained. It illuminates itself merely as cognition, not as dependent upon another, because that other is like a spirit or God. And if distinctness is being produced by the immediately preceding cognition, then inferential cognition too, being produced by an immediately preceding cognition, would absurdly be <s>nirvikalpaka</s>.

body.translated_text: 4.1(10)a2 If distinctness is the appearance of a particular (<s>svalakṣaṇapratibhāsitā</s>) — what appears therein? Is it the object, the cognition, or both? If the object — that is unjustified, because in an unestablished apprehension, the apprehension of that is absent. If the cognition — that appears in inference too; let that also be <s>nirvikalpaka</s>. If it becomes <s>nirvikalpaka</s>, then the term '<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>' (free from conceptual construction) must now be sought and pursued anew. If both appear — that is unjustified, because it is accepted that a single apprehension is established by excluding a second form.

/ na ca jñānamātratayā tasya savikalpakatvam iṣyate sarvajñānānāṃ savikalpakatvaprasaṅgāt / yadi
ca nirviṣayatvenātītānāgatārthavijñānasya savikalpakatvam abhyupeyate, nirvikalpakābhimatakeśoṇḍukavijñānasyāpi savikalpakatvam āpadyate / na cātītānāgatavijñānasya nirviṣayatvam asti svāṃśaparyavasitatvāt / nāpi svāṃśavyatirikto 'rtho 'nyo 'sty ekopalambhenāpohitatvāt / na ca svāṃśasya vañcanopapadyate / tadabhāvāt sarvaṃ vijñānaṃ savikalpakaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ vā vaktavyaṃ bhedānupapatteḥ /
body.translated_text: 4.1(11) Now, if <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction) has the form of grasping past and future objects, then does an object appear therein, or its absence, or nothing at all? If a past object appears, then it is not <s>kalpanā</s>, just like a present cognition of blue. Nor is the pastness of the object established by virtue of its being cognized, like blue water and so forth. For there is no such thing as pastness of what is being cognized. And if pastness is ascribed even to what is being cognized, then everything apprehended by cognition would be past, and consequently there would be an absence of all present conventional usage. Now, if its absence appears, that too has no pastness, since it exists in its own form. Nor is the status of <s>kalpanā</s> established for the cognition having that as its object, since it arises by the power of a real object. Or if there is no such power, the object of the cognition must be reconsidered. Now, if it is objectless, then it is not designated as cognition of past and future objects, being devoid of any relation to past and future objects. And when it is objectless, it is neither <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate) nor <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate), but is established merely as having the nature of cognition. And its being <s>savikalpaka</s> is not accepted merely by virtue of being cognition, since the absurd consequence would follow that all cognitions are <s>savikalpaka</s>. And if the <s>savikalpaka</s> nature of cognition of past and future objects is accepted on the grounds of its being objectless, then even the cognition of hair-nets and the like, which is regarded as <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate), would also turn out to be <s>savikalpaka</s>. Nor is the cognition of past and future objects truly objectless, since it terminates in its own aspect. Nor is there any object other than its own aspect, since it is excluded by the principle of unified apprehension. And there can be no deception regarding its own aspect. In the absence of that distinction, all cognition must be declared either <s>savikalpaka</s> or <s>nirvikalpaka</s>, since no basis for differentiation is established.

jagat syāt / avijñānātmake ca jagati mānameyavyavahārābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / tatprasaktau ca
kasyedaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ prastūyate? athopādānabhūtena rūpeṇa rūpam utpādyate, nimittātmakena tu jñānam iti cet, tad idaṃ mahānubhavasya darśanam / na hy abāliśaivaṃ vaktum utsaheta / na hy ekasyānekākāratā nāma / na cānekanāmakaraṇe meyādyanyatvam asti / anyatve vā na tarhīdaṃ vaktavyaṃ  svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇendriyajñānena manovijñānaṃ niṣpādyate / tad evam indriyajñānasya pratīyamānārthasamudbhavatvābhāvaḥ / dṛṣṭāntaś ca sādhanavikalo  na rūpādisvalakṣaṇasya rūparūpāvabhātārthodbhavatvam asti / athāpratīyamānasvalakṣa.ṇodbhavatvaṃ me vivakṣitaṃ, tadātītānāgatānumānavikalpānām apratīyamānārthodbhavatvena nirvikalpakatvam āpadyate /
body.translated_text: 4.1a As for the further statement that perception is <s>kalpanāpoḍha</s> (free from conceptual construction) because it arises by the power of the object, like the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of form and so forth — is what is intended here that it arises from the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> as cognized, or merely that it arises from an object in general? If what is intended is that it arises from the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> as cognized, then the self-awareness of passion and the like, and <s>yogipratyakṣa</s> (yogic perception), cannot obtain this property of arising from a cognized <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. If, on the other hand, this is stated with reference to sense-generated perception — that it arises by the power of the object — even there, [the argument fails] since [the opponent] is committed to the rejection of external objects. Or let there be an external object; even so, does it produce [cognition] as a material cause or as an efficient cause? If it produces as an efficient cause, then the form of what is produced by it does not attain the nature of form, just as cognition produced by an efficient-cause form [does not take on that form]. If it produces as a material cause, then by this reasoning the cognition does attain the nature of form, just as a form produced from form [retains that nature]. In that case, the entire world would be non-conscious in nature. And if the world is non-conscious, the absurd consequence follows that there would be no conventional practice of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) and <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge). And if that consequence follows, for whom is this definition being proposed? Now, if one says that form produces form as a material cause, while it produces cognition as an efficient cause — this is the view of a great genius indeed! For no one but a fool would venture to say such a thing. For a single entity does not have multiple natures. And merely giving different names does not make something other than the measurable and so forth. Or if there is otherness, then one should not say that <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental cognition) is produced by sense-cognition along with the immediately subsequent object of that sense as a cooperating condition. Thus, sense-cognition lacks the property of arising from a cognized object. And the example is deficient in the proof — the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> of form and the like does not possess the property of arising from an object that appears as having the nature of form. If, on the other hand, what is intended is arising from a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> that is not cognized, then past and future objects, inference, and <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) would turn out to be <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate), since they too arise from objects not cognized.

children.text:
4.1a yad apy uktaṃ kalpanāpoḍhaṃ pratyakṣam arthasāmarthyena samudbhavād rūpādisvalakṣaṇavad iti tatra kiṃ pratīyamānasvalakṣaṇodbhavatvaṃ vivakṣitam āho 'rthamātrodbhavatvam? tad yadi pratīyamānasvalakṣaṇodbhavatvaṃ vivakṣitaṃ, tadā rāgādisaṃvedanasya yogipratyakṣasya ca pratīyamānasvalakṣaṇodbhavatvaṃ na labhyate / athendriyajapratyakṣavivakṣayedam apadiśyate 'rthasāmarthyena samudbhūtatvād iti sādhanaṃ, tatrāpi ... sya bāhyārthanirākaraṇaparatvāt / astu vā bāhyo 'rthas, tathāpi kiṃ tena nimittātmakenotpādyatā aha upādānātmakena? tad yadi nimittabhūtenotpādyate, tadā tadutpāditarūpasya rūparūpatā na prāpnoti nimittabhūtarūpotpāditajñānavat / athopādānātmakenotpādyate, tadānayā rītyā rūparūpatāpadyate jñānasya rūpotpāditarūpasyeva / tataḥ sarvam avijñānātmakaṃ
jagat syāt / avijñānātmake ca jagati mānameyavyavahārābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / tatprasaktau ca
kasyedaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ prastūyate? athopādānabhūtena rūpeṇa rūpam utpādyate, nimittātmakena tu jñānam iti cet, tad idaṃ mahānubhavasya darśanam / na hy abāliśa evaṃ vaktum utsaheta / na hy ekasyānekākāratā nāma / na cānekanāmakaraṇe meyādyanyatvam asti / anyatve vā na tarhīdaṃ vaktavyaṃ -- svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇendriyajñānena manovijñānaṃ niṣpādyate / tad evam indriyajñānasya pratīyamānārthasamudbhavatvābhāvaḥ / dṛṣṭāntaś ca sādhanavikalo -- na rūpādisvalakṣaṇasya rūparūpāvabhātārthodbhavatvam asti / athāpratīyamānasvalakṣa.ṇodbhavatvaṃ me vivakṣitaṃ, tadātītānāgatānumānavikalpānām apratīyamānārthodbhavatvena nirvikalpakatvam āpadyate /

body.text: 4.1b yad apy anyad uktam ekopalambhasāmarthyād vikalpikāyāḥ samudbhavedam upalabhedaṃ nopalabheti kilaikabhūtalopalambhe sati vikalpikā buddhir utpadyatedam upalabhedaṃ nopalabhyatetyādikaitad api na yuktam / yathā rūpasvalakṣaṇasya savikalpakavijñānajanakatvaṃ nāsty avikalpakatvāt, tathā vijñānasvalakṣaṇam api na savikalpakaviJñānotpādakatvam ativartate 'vicārakatvāviśeṣāt / athāvicārakatvāviśeṣe 'pi nirvikalpakavijñānasya savikalpakaviJñānodayadānasāmarthyaṃ jegīyate, tadā rūpādisvalakṣaṇasyāpy etad astu / tataś ca pratyakṣānumānayor bhedānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: 4.1b As for the further statement that by the power of unified apprehension, a conceptual cognition arises — 'this is apprehended, this is not apprehended' — that is, when there is apprehension of a single entity, a conceptual cognition arises such as 'this is apprehended, this is not apprehended' — this too is not correct. Just as the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of form does not have the capacity to generate <s>savikalpaka</s> (determinate) cognition because it is <s>avikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual), so too the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> of cognition does not transcend the incapacity to produce <s>savikalpaka</s> cognition, there being no difference in their non-deliberative nature. If, despite no difference in non-deliberative nature, the power of <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (indeterminate) cognition to give rise to <s>savikalpaka</s> cognition is asserted, then let this capacity belong to the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> of form and so forth as well. In that case, no distinction between <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference) can be established.

children.text: 4.1b yad apy anyad uktam ekopalambhasāmarthyād vikalpikāyāḥ samudbhava idam upalabha idaṃ nopalabha iti kilaikabhūtalopalambhe sati vikalpikā buddhir utpadyata idam upalabha idaṃ nopalabhyata ityādika aitad api na yuktam / yathā rūpasvalakṣaṇasya savikalpakavijñānajanakatvaṃ nāsty avikalpakatvāt, tathā vijñānasvalakṣaṇam api na savikalpakaviJñānotpādakatvam ativartate 'vicārakatvāviśeṣāt / athāvicārakatvāviśeṣe 'pi nirvikalpakavijñānasya savikalpakaviJñānodayadānasāmarthyaṃ jegīyate, tadā rūpādisvalakṣaṇasyāpy etad astu / tataś ca pratyakṣānumānayor bhedānupapattiḥ /

body.text: 4.1c yad apy anyad uktaṃ pratyakṣasādhanaivendriyadhiyaḥ kalpanāvirahaḥ /
body.translated_text: 4.1c As for the further statement that the freedom from <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction) of sense-cognition is established by the very means that establish perception —

children.text: 4.1c yad apy anyad uktaṃ pratyakṣasādhana evendriyadhiyaḥ kalpanāvirahaḥ /

body.text: atha ko 'yaṃ kalpanāviraho nāma? kiṃ Jñānakāyatādātmyavyavasthitadehas tadviparīto vā? tad yadi jñānatādātmyena vyavasthitas, tadā pratyakṣasādhanaḥ kalpanāviraheti kim uktaṃ bhavati? pratyakṣasādhano vijñānākāraḥ pratyakṣadhiyaḥ / na kevalaṃ pratyakṣakalpanāvirahaḥ pratyakṣasādhano, 'numānadhiyo 'pi pratyakṣasādhanaiva, jñānākārasyānumānajñāne 'pi bhāvāt / athānumānajñānasyāpy ātmasaṃvittau kalpanārahitatvaṃ, bāhyārthāpekṣayā kalpanātmakatvam iti cet,
body.translated_text: Now, what is this freedom from <s>kalpanā</s>? Is it established as identical in nature with the body of cognition, or is it the opposite of that? If it is established as identical with cognition, then what does the statement mean that freedom from <s>kalpanā</s> is established by the means of perception? It would mean that the form of cognition is what establishes perceptual cognition. Not only is freedom from <s>kalpanā</s> in perception established by the means of perception, but the cognition of <s>anumāna</s> (inference) too is established by the means of perception, since the form of cognition is present in inferential cognition as well. If one says that inferential cognition too is free from <s>kalpanā</s> with respect to self-awareness, but is of the nature of <s>kalpanā</s> with respect to external objects —

body.text: tad etan mugdhābhidhānaṃ dunoti mānasam / kathaṃ syur vividhākārās tadekasya vastunaḥ?
body.translated_text: this bewildered statement pains the mind. How could there be manifold forms belonging to one and the same entity?

children.text: tad etan mugdhābhidhānaṃ dunoti mānasam / kathaṃ syur vividhākārās tadekasya vastunaḥ?

body.text: atha bhedena vyavasthitas, tadgatiḥ katham? na svasaṃvedyo 'sau jñānākāravyatirekāt / nāpi janakatvākārārpakatvena gṛhyate virahasya sāmarthyavyatirekāt / evaṃ ca sati yad uktaṃ pratyakṣasādhanaivendriyadhiyaḥ kalpanāviraheti tad bālavalgitam /
body.translated_text: Now, if [freedom from <s>kalpanā</s>] is established as distinct [from cognition], how is it apprehended? It is not self-cognized, since it is different from the form of cognition. Nor is it grasped through the capacity of producing or imparting a form, since absence [of <s>kalpanā</s>] has no causal power. This being so, the statement that freedom from <s>kalpanā</s> of sense-cognition is established by the very means that establish perception — that is mere childish prattle.

children.text: atha bhedena vyavasthitas, tadgatiḥ katham? na svasaṃvedyo 'sau jñānākāravyatirekāt / nāpi janakatvākārārpakatvena gṛhyate virahasya sāmarthyavyatirekāt / evaṃ ca sati yad uktaṃ pratyakṣasādhana evendriyadhiyaḥ kalpanāviraha iti tad bālavalgitam /

body.text: 4.1d atha gaur ityādijñānaṃ kalpanā, katham asya kalpanātvam?
body.translated_text: 4.1d Now, if the cognition 'this is a cow' and the like is <s>kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction), how is its status as <s>kalpanā</s> established?

children.text: 4.1d atha gaur ityādijñānaṃ kalpanā, katham asya kalpanātvam?

body.text: arthenājanitatvād yadi gavāder arthasya gaur ityādijñānotpādanasāmarthyaṃ syāt, tadā prathamākṣasannipātavelāyām api kuryāt tadātmano 'viśeṣāt / tad uktaṃ
body.translated_text: If it is because it is not produced by the object — if the object such as a cow and so forth had the capacity to produce the cognition 'this is a cow,' then it should produce it even at the first moment of sensory contact, there being no difference in its own nature. As has been said:

children.text: arthenājanitatvād yadi gavāder arthasya gaur ityādijñānotpādanasāmarthyaṃ syāt, tadā prathamākṣasannipātavelāyām api kuryāt tadātmano 'viśeṣāt / tad uktaṃ

body.text: yaḥ prāg ajanako buddher upayogāviśeṣataḥ/ sa paścād api tena syād arthāpāye 'pi netradhīḥ//
body.translated_text: That which previously did not generate cognition, due to there being no difference in its engagement, would remain the same even afterwards; and even in the absence of the object, there would be visual cognition.

children.text: yaḥ prāg ajanako buddher upayogāviśeṣataḥ/ sa paścād api tena syād arthāpāye 'pi netradhīḥ//

body.text: atha śabdasmaraṇam apekṣyotpādayati, tad evāstu taddehānantaraphalatvād gaur ityādijñānasya / tad uktam
body.translated_text: If one says that it produces [the cognition 'this is a cow'] in dependence on the recollection of the word — then let that alone be [the cause], since the cognition 'this is a cow' has as its result what immediately follows that [recollection]. As has been said:

children.text: atha śabdasmaraṇam apekṣyotpādayati, tad evāstu taddehānantaraphalatvād gaur ityādijñānasya / tad uktam

body.text: arthopayoge 'pi punaḥ smārtaṃ śabdānuyojanam/ akṣadhīr yady apekṣeta so 'rtho vyavahito bhavet//
body.translated_text: Even when the object is present, if sense-cognition requires the associative connection of a remembered word, then that object would be obstructed [as a direct cause].

children.text: arthopayoge 'pi punaḥ smārtaṃ śabdānuyojanam/ akṣadhīr yady apekṣeta so 'rtho vyavahito bhavet//

body.text:
tad etad ayuktam / prāthamikam api jñānaṃ gaur iti jñānaṃ, gopiṇḍāvagāhini vijñāne gaur iti jñānasañjñā / tataś ca prathamākṣasannipātajam api bhavati / evaṃ ca pūrvāparavijñānayor ekaviṣayatvobhayor gaur iti jñānasañjñāviṣayatvam / nanv ekasya kramabhāvivijñānajanakatvaṃ kim ekena svarūpeṇa svarūpāntareṇa vā? ekenaiva svabhāvena janayatīti brūmaḥ / nanv ekakālīnatā pūrvāparavijñānayor ekasvabhāvāyattatve saty āpadyate / yady evam ekanīlotpāditanayanālokavijñānānām ekadeśasambandhitvam ekākārataikavyaktitvam āpadyataikanīlotpādyatvāviśeṣāt / athaivambhūtaṃ tat tasya svarūpaṃ yac citrakāryakaraṇātmakam / yady evaṃ mamake 'pi pakṣe kramabhāvyanekakāryakaraṇātmakam eva svarūpaṃ svahetusāmarthyaniyamitasyotpatteḥ / athavā yathātvadīye pakṣe manojñānaṃ svalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ
na ca prathamākṣasannipātajam, api tv indriyajñānena
svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇotpādyate, tathā gaur ityādikam api jñānaṃ prathamākṣasannipātajena vijñānena svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇā smaraṇādyupahitena cotpādyateti nirviṣayatvābhāvo viṣayāntarasya svakāraṇasāmarthyānurodhena gaur ityādijñānajananayogyasyotpatteḥ / smaraṇam api samartham utpannaṃ sad gaur ity utpādayati / evaṃ sati yad uktaṃ yaḥ prāg ajanako buddher ityādi, tad svaparamatam anālocyaiva jegīyate /
body.translated_text: This is not correct. Even the initial cognition is a cognition 'this is a cow'; when a cognition engages with a particular cow, it receives the designation 'cognition that this is a cow.' Therefore it arises even from the first moment of sensory contact. Thus, both the earlier and later cognitions, having the same object, are both designated as cognition 'this is a cow.' Now, does a single entity generate cognitions that arise in sequence by one nature or by another nature? We say: it generates by one and the same nature. But then, if the earlier and later cognitions depend on one and the same nature, the absurd consequence of their being simultaneous would follow. If so, then the visual cognitions produced by a single blue object, being related to the same locus, having the same form, and being of one individual — these would [absurdly] all be simultaneous, there being no difference in their being produced by one blue. But if the nature of that object is such that it is capable of producing diverse effects — if so, then in my position too, the nature is precisely that of producing multiple effects arising in sequence, since what arises is determined by the power of its own cause. Alternatively, just as in your position <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental cognition) has a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) as its object yet does not arise from the first moment of sensory contact, but is produced by sense-cognition along with the immediately subsequent object as a cooperating condition, so too the cognition 'this is a cow' and the like is produced by the cognition born of the first sensory contact, with the immediately subsequent object as a cooperating condition, and supplemented by recollection and the like — hence it is not objectless, since a different object, fit to generate the cognition 'this is a cow,' arises in conformity with the power of its own cause. Recollection too, being capable, once arisen produces [the cognition] 'this is a cow.' This being so, the statement 'that which previously did not generate cognition' and so forth is asserted without even considering one's own doctrine.
