body.text: 4.1e na ca jñānākaravyatirekeṇa vikalpākāro 'nyo 'sti / kalpanākāro hi jñānatādātmyena vyavasthitaḥ / tataś ca kalpanāpoḍhaṃ pratyakṣaṃ kim uktaṃ bhavati? jñānāpoḍhaṃ pratyakṣam / yo yatsvabhāvopanibaddhaḥ, sa nivartamānas tam ādāya nivartate / tataś cājñānātmakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ prasaktam /
body.translated_text: And there is no other form of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpākāra</s>) apart from the form of cognition. For the form of conceptual construction is established as identical with cognition. And therefore, what is meant by saying perception is 'free from conceptual construction' (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>)? It means perception is free from cognition. Whatever is bound to a particular nature, when it ceases, ceases taking that [nature] along with it. And therefore, the consequence follows that perception is devoid of cognition for the <s>Bhikṣus</s> (Buddhists).

children.text: 4.1e na ca jñānākaravyatirekeṇa vikalpākāro 'nyo 'sti / kalpanākāro hi jñānatādātmyena vyavasthitaḥ / tataś ca kalpanāpoḍhaṃ pratyakṣaṃ kim uktaṃ bhavati? jñānāpoḍhaṃ pratyakṣam / yo yatsvabhāvopanibaddhaḥ, sa nivartamānas tam ādāya nivartate / tataś cājñānātmakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ prasaktam /

body.text: 4.2 tathāvyabhicāripadam api nopādeyam apohyajñānāsambhavāt / nanu mārtaṇḍapādasaṅghātotpāditaṃ vijñānam apohyam asti  kathaṃ tad apohyam?  atathyodakaviṣayatvāt / yady atathyodakaviṣayatvaṃ, kathaṃ tad apanīyate 'tathyodakākārasya svena rūpeṇa vidyamānatvān madhurodakadīrghodakākāravat? atha tatra madhurodakaṃ vidyate, svena rūpeṇa pratīyamānatvāt, tad ihāpy udakaṃ pratīyatodakaṃ gṛhṇāmīti vyavahāradarśanāt / satyaṃ, pratibhāty, atathyaṃ tu pratibhāti /
body.translated_text: Similarly, the qualification 'non-erring' (<s>avyabhicāri</s>) also should not be accepted, because erroneous cognition (<s>apohyajñāna</s>) is impossible. Objection: But the cognition produced by the aggregate of the sun's rays and the feet [of a traveler] is erroneous — how is it erroneous? Because it has unreal water as its object. If it has unreal water as its object, how is it to be removed, since the form of real water exists in its own nature, just like the form of sweet water or distant water? Now if sweet water exists there, because it is experienced in its own form, then here too water is experienced — 'I perceive water' — as seen from ordinary practice. True, it appears, but what appears is unreal.

children.text: 4.2 tathāvyabhicāripadam api nopādeyam apohyajñānāsambhavāt / nanu mārtaṇḍapādasaṅghātotpāditaṃ vijñānam apohyam asti - kathaṃ tad apohyam? - atathyodakaviṣayatvāt / yady atathyodakaviṣayatvaṃ, kathaṃ tad apanīyate 'tathyodakākārasya svena rūpeṇa vidyamānatvān madhurodakadīrghodakākāravat? atha tatra madhurodakaṃ vidyate, svena rūpeṇa pratīyamānatvāt, tad ihāpy udakaṃ pratīyata udakaṃ gṛhṇāmīti vyavahāradarśanāt / satyaṃ, pratibhāty, atathyaṃ tu pratibhāti /

body.text: 4.21 atathyatā kā? kiṃ pratīyamānasyābhāvo 'tha pratīyamānaivābhāvaḥ?
body.translated_text: What is this unreality? Is it the non-existence of what appears, or is what appears itself non-existence?

children.text: 4.21 atathyatā kā? kiṃ pratīyamānasyābhāvo 'tha pratīyamāna evābhāvaḥ?

body.text: 4.211 yadi pratīyamānasyābhāvaḥ, so 'tra nāvābhāty, udakākāraivāvabhāti /
body.translated_text: If it is the non-existence of what appears, that [non-existence] does not appear there — only the water-form appears.

children.text: 4.211 yadi pratīyamānasyābhāvaḥ, so 'tra nāvābhāty, udakākāra evāvabhāti /

body.text: 4.212 atha pratīyamānaivābhāvaḥ so 'py anupapannaiva / na hi bhāvākāre pratīyamāne 'bhāvakalpanā yuktā / anyathā rasākāre pratīyamāne rūpākāraḥ parikalpayitavyaḥ / tataś cālūnaviśīrṇaṃ jagat syāt / yadi cābhāvaḥ pratibhāti, kathaṃ tad udakajñānaṃ mithyājñānaṃ cocyate 'bhāvaviṣayasya svena rūpeṇa vidyamānatvāt?
body.translated_text: If what appears is itself non-existence, that too is simply untenable. For when the form of an existent appears, it is not proper to imagine it as non-existence. Otherwise, when the form of taste appears, the form of color would have to be imagined. And thus the world would be torn asunder and destroyed. And if non-existence appears, how can that water-cognition be called erroneous cognition, since the object — non-existence — exists in its own form?

children.text: 4.212 atha pratīyamāna evābhāvaḥ so 'py anupapanna eva / na hi bhāvākāre pratīyamāne 'bhāvakalpanā yuktā / anyathā rasākāre pratīyamāne rūpākāraḥ parikalpayitavyaḥ / tataś cālūnaviśīrṇaṃ jagat syāt / yadi cābhāvaḥ pratibhāti, kathaṃ tad udakajñānaṃ mithyājñānaṃ cocyate 'bhāvaviṣayasya svena rūpeṇa vidyamānatvāt?

body.text: 4.22 tad etad udakajñānam udakaṃ viṣayayaty udakābhāvam ātmānaṃ na kiñcid vā /
body.translated_text: This water-cognition either has water as its object, or non-existence of water, or itself, or nothing at all.

children.text: 4.22 tad etad udakajñānam udakaṃ viṣayayaty udakābhāvam ātmānaṃ na kiñcid vā /

body.text: 4.221 tad yady udakaṃ viṣayayati, tadā na tasya mithyātvaṃ madhurodakasaṃvedanasyeva / tatra tathyodakaṃ pratibhāti / kiṃ yat pratibhāti tat tathyodakam, āho yat tathyaṃ tat pratibhāti? tad yadi yat pratibhāti tat tathyam, ihāpy udakaṃ pratibhāti, prāptā tasyāpi tathyatā /
body.translated_text: If it has water as its object, then it is not erroneous, just like the experience of sweet water. In that case, real water appears. Now, is what appears real water, or does what is real appear? If what appears is real, then here too water appears, and its reality follows.

children.text: 4.221 tad yady udakaṃ viṣayayati, tadā na tasya mithyātvaṃ madhurodakasaṃvedanasyeva / tatra tathyodakaṃ pratibhāti / kiṃ yat pratibhāti tat tathyodakam, āho yat tathyaṃ tat pratibhāti? tad yadi yat pratibhāti tat tathyam, ihāpy udakaṃ pratibhāti, prāptā tasyāpi tathyatā /

body.text:
atha yat tathyaṃ tat pratibhāti, tasya tathyatā kathaṃ jñāyate? kiṃ pratītyānyathā vā? yadi pratītyā, ihāpi pratītir utpadyate / astu tathyatā / atha pratītim antareṇa tathyatopapādyate, tadā susthitāni vastūni / sarvavādasiddhiḥ syāt / atha pratīyate yadi nāma bādhyate / pratīyate bādhyate ceti citram / pratīyamānatvaṃ ca janakatvākārārpakatvena vyāptam / yac ca na janayati nākāram arpayati tan nāvabhāti yathā rūpajñāne rasaḥ / pratīyate cātrodakaṃ, janakatvākārārpakatvopapattiḥ / tadupapattau ca na bādhopapattir, janakatvākārārpakatvasya sattvanibandhanatvāt /
4.222 athābhāvaṃ viṣayayati, na tarhy udakajñānarūpatābhāvagṛhītirūpatvāt / nāpi tasya mithyātvam abhāvaviṣayasyopapatteḥ / na ca saugatamate 'bhāve kaścid viṣayārthopapadyate janakatvākārārpakatvavyatirekāt. udakākāro hi pratītyutkalitaḥ / tadabhāvaś cāprātītikehopapādyate mugdhabauddhaiḥ /
body.translated_text:
If what is real appears — how is its reality known? By experience or otherwise? If by experience, here too experience arises — let its reality be established. If reality is established without experience, then things are well-established, and all doctrines would be proven. If it is experienced but then sublated — that it is experienced and also sublated is remarkable! And being experienced is pervaded by being a producer and by imparting one's form. And what does not produce and does not impart its form does not appear, just as taste does not appear in the cognition of color. And water is experienced here, so the capacity for producing and imparting form is established. And when that capacity is established, sublation is not established, because the capacity for producing and imparting form is grounded in real existence.
If it has non-existence as its object, then it is not of the nature of water-cognition, because it grasps non-existence, not water. Nor is it erroneous, because having non-existence as its object is established. Nor in the <s>Saugata</s> (Buddhist) view does any objective reality obtain in non-existence, because of the absence of the capacity for producing and imparting one's form. For the water-form is manifested through experience. And its non-existence is established here without experience by the confused Buddhists.

children.text:
atha yat tathyaṃ tat pratibhāti, tasya tathyatā kathaṃ jñāyate? kiṃ pratītyānyathā vā? yadi pratītyā, ihāpi pratītir utpadyate / astu tathyatā / atha pratītim antareṇa tathyatopapādyate, tadā susthitāni vastūni / sarvavādasiddhiḥ syāt / atha pratīyate yadi nāma bādhyate / pratīyate bādhyate ceti citram / pratīyamānatvaṃ ca janakatvākārārpakatvena vyāptam / yac ca na janayati nākāram arpayati tan nāvabhāti yathā rūpajñāne rasaḥ / pratīyate cātrodakaṃ, janakatvākārārpakatvopapattiḥ / tadupapattau ca na bādhopapattir, janakatvākārārpakatvasya sattvanibandhanatvāt /
4.222 athābhāvaṃ viṣayayati, na tarhy udakajñānarūpatābhāvagṛhītirūpatvāt / nāpi tasya mithyātvam abhāvaviṣayasyopapatteḥ / na ca saugatamate 'bhāve kaścid viṣayārtha upapadyate janakatvākārārpakatvavyatirekāt. udakākāro hi pratītyutkalitaḥ / tadabhāvaś cāprātītika ihopapādyate mugdhabauddhaiḥ /

body.text: 4.223 athātmaviṣayaṃ, tathāpi vyabhicāritā nopapadyate, svāṃśasyāvañcanāt / na hi jñānam ātmānaṃ visaṃvadati / nāpi tad udakajñānatvena vyapadeśyaṃ rāgādisaṃvedanavat / na hi nīlābhaṃ saṃvedanaṃ rasavijñānātmakatvena vyapadiśyamānaṃ dṛṣtam /
body.translated_text: If it has itself as object, even so erroneousness is not established, because one's own aspect is not deceptive. For cognition does not deceive itself. Nor can it be designated as water-cognition, like the experience of passion and the like. For we do not observe a cognition appearing as blue being designated as a taste-cognition.

children.text: 4.223 athātmaviṣayaṃ, tathāpi vyabhicāritā nopapadyate, svāṃśasyāvañcanāt / na hi jñānam ātmānaṃ visaṃvadati / nāpi tad udakajñānatvena vyapadeśyaṃ rāgādisaṃvedanavat / na hi nīlābhaṃ saṃvedanaṃ rasavijñānātmakatvena vyapadiśyamānaṃ dṛṣtam /

body.text: 4.224 atha nirviṣayaṃ, na tarhi tad udakajñānam, udakajñānatayā tu pratibhāti, tena jānīma na nirviṣayam / yadi ca nirviṣayaṃ, kathaṃ tan mithyājñānam? jñānamātrānurodhena na mithyājñānaṃ nāpi samyagjñānam / na ca bhavatāṃ pakṣe jñānaṃ nirālambanam asti svāṃśaparyavasitatvāt /
body.translated_text: If it is objectless, then it is not water-cognition — but it appears as water-cognition, and by that we know it is not objectless. And if it is objectless, how is it erroneous cognition? By the mere fact of being cognition, it is neither erroneous nor valid. Nor in your position is cognition without a support (<s>nirālambana</s>), because it terminates in its own aspect.

children.text: 4.224 atha nirviṣayaṃ, na tarhi tad udakajñānam, udakajñānatayā tu pratibhāti, tena jānīma na nirviṣayam / yadi ca nirviṣayaṃ, kathaṃ tan mithyājñānam? jñānamātrānurodhena na mithyājñānaṃ nāpi samyagjñānam / na ca bhavatāṃ pakṣe jñānaṃ nirālambanam asti svāṃśaparyavasitatvāt /

body.text: 4.23 vijñānasya vyabhicāritā kiṃ svasattāmātrānurodhenāho parasattānurodhena?
body.translated_text: Is the erroneousness (<s>vyabhicāritā</s>) of cognition by virtue of its own existence alone, or by virtue of the existence of something external?

children.text: 4.23 vijñānasya vyabhicāritā kiṃ svasattāmātrānurodhenāho parasattānurodhena?

body.text: 4.231 tad yadi svasattānurodhena, tadā sarvavijñānānāṃ vyabhicāritā prāpnoti jñānarūpatāyāḥ sarvatra bhāvāt / na kiñcid vijñānam avyabhicāri syāt /
body.translated_text: If by virtue of its own existence, then all cognitions would be erroneous, since the nature of being cognition is present everywhere. No cognition would be non-erroneous.

children.text: 4.231 tad yadi svasattānurodhena, tadā sarvavijñānānāṃ vyabhicāritā prāpnoti jñānarūpatāyāḥ sarvatra bhāvāt / na kiñcid vijñānam avyabhicāri syāt /

body.text: 4.232 atha parasattānurodhena vyabhicāritocyate, kim anupakārakaparasattānurodhenāhopakārakaparasattānurodhena? tad yady anupakārakaparasattānurodhena vyabhicāritā, tadā sarvasaṃvittīnāṃ vyabhicāritā prāpnotyanupakārakaparasattāviśeṣāt / athopakārakaparasattānurodhena vyabhicāritābhidhīyate, kiṃ karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattānurodhenāho karmatāpannopakārakaparasattānurodhena? tad yadi karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattānuvedhena, tadā sarvāsāṃ saṃvittīnāṃ mithyātvam āpadyate karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattāviśeṣāt / atha karmakārakopakārakaparasattānuvedhena mithyātvaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, na tasya mithyātvaṃ satyodakajñānasyeva karmakārakeṇopakriyamāṇatvāt /
body.translated_text: If erroneousness is said to be by virtue of the existence of something external — is it by virtue of the existence of something external that is non-contributory, or by virtue of the existence of something external that is contributory? If erroneousness is by virtue of the existence of something non-contributory external, then all cognitions would be erroneous, since there is no difference regarding the existence of non-contributory external things. If erroneousness is said to be by virtue of the existence of something contributory external — is it by virtue of the existence of something external that contributes as an instrument, or by virtue of the existence of something external that contributes as an object? If by virtue of the existence of something external that contributes as an instrument, then all cognitions would be erroneous, since there is no difference regarding the existence of something external that contributes as an instrument. If erroneousness is by virtue of the existence of something external that contributes as an object, that is not justified — because that cognition is not erroneous, since it is assisted by the object-factor, just like the cognition of real water.

children.text: 4.232 atha parasattānurodhena vyabhicāritocyate, kim anupakārakaparasattānurodhenāha upakārakaparasattānurodhena? tad yady anupakārakaparasattānurodhena vyabhicāritā, tadā sarvasaṃvittīnāṃ vyabhicāritā prāpnotyanupakārakaparasattāviśeṣāt / athopakārakaparasattānurodhena vyabhicāritābhidhīyate, kiṃ karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattānurodhenāho karmatāpannopakārakaparasattānurodhena? tad yadi karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattānuvedhena, tadā sarvāsāṃ saṃvittīnāṃ mithyātvam āpadyate karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattāviśeṣāt / atha karmakārakopakārakaparasattānuvedhena mithyātvaṃ, tad ayuktaṃ, na tasya mithyātvaṃ satyodakajñānasyeva karmakārakeṇopakriyamāṇatvāt /

body.text: 4.24 tathā samyagjñānatvam api ka ham? kiṃ jñānasattāmātrānurodhenāho parasattānurodhena?
body.translated_text: Similarly, how is valid cognition (<s>samyagjñānatva</s>) [established]? Is it by virtue of the mere existence of cognition, or by virtue of the existence of something external?

children.text: 4.24 tathā samyagjñānatvam api ka ham? kiṃ jñānasattāmātrānurodhenāho parasattānurodhena?

body.text: 4.241 tad yadi jñānasattāmātrānurodhena samyaktvaṃ, tadā sarvasaṃvittīnāṃ samyaktvaṃ prāpnoti jñānākārasyopapatteḥ /
body.translated_text: If validity is by virtue of the mere existence of cognition, then all cognitions would be valid, because the cognition-form is established in all cases.

children.text: 4.241 tad yadi jñānasattāmātrānurodhena samyaktvaṃ, tadā sarvasaṃvittīnāṃ samyaktvaṃ prāpnoti jñānākārasyopapatteḥ /

body.text: 4.242 atha parasattānurodhena samyaktvaṃ, tadā kim anupakārakaparasattānurodhena kiṃ vopakārakaparasattānurodhena? tad yady anupakārakaparasattānurodhena samyaktvaṃ, tadā sarvāsāṃ saṃvittīnāṃ samyaktvam āpadyate 'nupakārakaparasattāviśeṣāt / athopakārakaparasattānurodhena kiṃ karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattānuvedhenāho karmatāpannopakārakaparasattānuvedhena? tad yadi karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattānuvedhena, tadā sarvāsāṃ saṃvittīnāṃ samyaktvam āpadyate karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattāviśeṣāt / atha karmatāpannopakārakaparasattānuvedhena samyaktvam abhidhīyate, tadā rāgādisaṃvedanasya samyaktvaṃ na prāpnoty, atītānāgatārthaviṣayatve yogijñānasya ca /
body.translated_text: If validity is by virtue of the existence of something external — is it by virtue of the existence of something non-contributory external, or by virtue of the existence of something contributory external? If validity is by virtue of the existence of something non-contributory external, then all cognitions would be valid, since there is no difference regarding the existence of non-contributory external things. If by virtue of the existence of something contributory external — is it by virtue of the existence of something external that contributes as an instrument, or by virtue of the existence of something external that contributes as an object? If by virtue of the existence of something external that contributes as an instrument, then all cognitions would be valid, since there is no difference regarding the existence of something external that contributes as an instrument. If validity is said to be by virtue of the existence of something external that contributes as an object, then the experience of passion and the like would not be valid, and the cognition of the <s>yogin</s> regarding past and future objects would also not be valid.

children.text: 4.242 atha parasattānurodhena samyaktvaṃ, tadā kim anupakārakaparasattānurodhena kiṃ vopakārakaparasattānurodhena? tad yady anupakārakaparasattānurodhena samyaktvaṃ, tadā sarvāsāṃ saṃvittīnāṃ samyaktvam āpadyate 'nupakārakaparasattāviśeṣāt / athopakārakaparasattānurodhena kiṃ karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattānuvedhenāho karmatāpannopakārakaparasattānuvedhena? tad yadi karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattānuvedhena, tadā sarvāsāṃ saṃvittīnāṃ samyaktvam āpadyate karaṇabhūtaparopakārakasattāviśeṣāt / atha karmatāpannopakārakaparasattānuvedhena samyaktvam abhidhīyate, tadā rāgādisaṃvedanasya samyaktvaṃ na prāpnoty, atītānāgatārthaviṣayatve yogijñānasya ca /

body.text: 4.25 yat tad vyabhicāri jñānaṃ, tat kiṃ vyabhicāribhūtenopādānajñānena janyatāho 'vyabhicāribhūtenopādānajñānena janyate?
body.translated_text: That erroneous cognition — is it produced by material-cause cognition that is itself erroneous, or is it produced by material-cause cognition that is non-erroneous?

children.text: 4.25 yat tad vyabhicāri jñānaṃ, tat kiṃ vyabhicāribhūtenopādānajñānena janyatā aho 'vyabhicāribhūtenopādānajñānena janyate?

body.text: 4.251 tad yadi vyabhicāribhūtenopādānajñānena janyate, tad api vyabhicāribhūtena, prāptā vyabhicāriparamparā / saṅgrāhyam avyabhicāri na labhyate /
body.translated_text: If it is produced by material-cause cognition that is erroneous, that too is produced by something erroneous — and an infinite regress of erroneousness follows. A non-erroneous [cognition] to be apprehended is never obtained.

children.text: 4.251 tad yadi vyabhicāribhūtenopādānajñānena janyate, tad api vyabhicāribhūtena, prāptā vyabhicāriparamparā / saṅgrāhyam avyabhicāri na labhyate /

body.text: 4.252 athāvyabhicāribhūtenopādānajñānena janyate, tad upādānakāraṇam anukurvad vopajāyate 'nanukurvad vā / tad yady upādānakāraṇānukāreṇotpādyate, tadā kim āpnoti? avyabhicārisvarūpānukāreṇotpādyate / katham? avyabhicārasya jñānatādātmyena vyavasthiteḥ / na caikadeśānukāritvam asty upādānakāraṇasya niravayavatvāt / evaṃ sarvaṃ vijñānam avyabhicāri prasaktam, apohyajñānānupapattiḥ / na ca vyabhicārāvyabhicārau jñānād vyatiriktau staḥ / yathā rasākāro rūpākāro vā jñānākārād bhinno, na tathā vyabhicārāvyabhicārau jñānād vyatiriktau / tataś ca vyabhicārākāro 'tra nirākriyate kim uktaṃ bhavati? jñānākāro 'tra nirākriyate / tataś cājñānātmakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ prasaktaṃ saugatānām /
body.translated_text: If it is produced by material-cause cognition that is non-erroneous — does it arise conforming to its material cause or not conforming to it? If it is produced conforming to its material cause, then what does it attain? It is produced conforming to the nature of being non-erroneous. How? Because the non-erroneous nature is established as identical with cognition. Nor is there partial conformity to the material cause, since it is without parts. Thus all cognition would be non-erroneous, and erroneous cognition (<s>apohyajñāna</s>) would be impossible. Nor are erroneousness and non-erroneousness distinct from cognition. Unlike the form of taste or the form of color being different from the form of cognition, erroneousness and non-erroneousness are not distinct from cognition. Therefore, when the erroneous form is removed here, what is being said? The cognition-form is being removed. And thus the consequence follows that perception is devoid of cognition for the <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists).

children.text: 4.252 athāvyabhicāribhūtenopādānajñānena janyate, tad upādānakāraṇam anukurvad vopajāyate 'nanukurvad vā / tad yady upādānakāraṇānukāreṇotpādyate, tadā kim āpnoti? avyabhicārisvarūpānukāreṇotpādyate / katham? avyabhicārasya jñānatādātmyena vyavasthiteḥ / na caikadeśānukāritvam asty upādānakāraṇasya niravayavatvāt / evaṃ sarvaṃ vijñānam avyabhicāri prasaktam, apohyajñānānupapattiḥ / na ca vyabhicārāvyabhicārau jñānād vyatiriktau staḥ / yathā rasākāro rūpākāro vā jñānākārād bhinno, na tathā vyabhicārāvyabhicārau jñānād vyatiriktau / tataś ca vyabhicārākāro 'tra nirākriyate kim uktaṃ bhavati? jñānākāro 'tra nirākriyate / tataś cājñānātmakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ prasaktaṃ saugatānām /

body.text: 4.25āpi ca yathā rūpeṇopādānabhūtena janyate rūpaṃ, tathā jñānam apy upādānabhūtenaiva janyate / yaiva tasya rūpotpādanātmā, saiva tasya jñānotpādane 'pi / na hi tasya jñānotpādanātmānyatvam /
body.translated_text: Moreover, just as form is produced by form as its material cause, so too cognition is produced by that very material cause. The very nature of that cause in producing form is the same in producing cognition. For its nature as a producer of cognition is not different.

children.text: 4.25a api ca yathā rūpeṇopādānabhūtena janyate rūpaṃ, tathā jñānam apy upādānabhūtenaiva janyate / ya eva tasya rūpotpādanā atmā, sa eva tasya jñānotpādane 'pi / na hi tasya jñānotpādanā atmānyatvam /

body.text: atha nimittabhūtena jñānam utpādyatopādānabhūtena rūpam iti cet, tat katham ekasyānekākārayogitopapadyate? na ca sañjñānyatve meyādyanyatvam upapadyate / rūpavad vijñānasyāpi rūparūpatā prāpnoti / tatprāptau ca na paraloky ātmā / tadabhāvān na paralokaḥ / idam eva cetasi samāropyāha bhagavān bṛhaspatiḥ paralokino 'bhāvāt paralokābhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: If cognition is produced by an efficient cause while form is produced by a material cause — then how is it established that a single thing has the capacity for multiple forms? And when the designation differs, the difference of the object of knowledge and the like is not established. Cognition too would attain the nature of form, just like form. And in that case, the self does not exist in the next world. Due to its non-existence, there is no next world. Having placed this very thought in the mind, the venerable <s>Bṛhaspati</s> says: 'Due to the non-existence of one who goes to the next world, the next world does not exist.'

children.text: atha nimittabhūtena jñānam utpādyata upādānabhūtena rūpam iti cet, tat katham ekasyānekākārayogitopapadyate? na ca sañjñānyatve meyādyanyatvam upapadyate / rūpavad vijñānasyāpi rūparūpatā prāpnoti / tatprāptau ca na paraloky ātmā / tadabhāvān na paralokaḥ / idam eva cetasi samāropyāha bhagavān bṛhaspatiḥ paralokino 'bhāvāt paralokābhāvaḥ /

body.text: atha rūpopādānajanyatve 'pi jñānarūpataiva, rūpasyāpi jñānarūpatā prāptā rūpopādānajanyatvāj jñānavat / atha jñānaṃ jñānenopādānabhūtena janyate, rūpam api tenaiva janyate / na hi tasya rūpotpādanātmānyatvam / evaṃ ca
body.translated_text: Even if cognition is produced with form as its material cause, it is still of the nature of cognition. Form too would attain the nature of cognition, since it is produced with form as its material cause, just like cognition. If cognition is produced by cognition as its material cause, form too is produced by that very same cause. For the nature of that cause is not different in producing form. And thus:

children.text: atha rūpopādānajanyatve 'pi jñānarūpataiva, rūpasyāpi jñānarūpatā prāptā rūpopādānajanyatvāj jñānavat / atha jñānaṃ jñānenopādānabhūtena janyate, rūpam api tenaiva janyate / na hi tasya rūpotpādanā atmānyatvam / evaṃ ca

body.text: tadatadrūpiṇo bhāvās tadatadrūpahetujāḥ/ tad rūpādi kim ajñānaṃ vijñānābhinnahetujam//
body.translated_text: Things are of such and such a nature, born from causes of such and such nature; then is form and the like non-cognition, being born from a cause indistinguishable from cognition?

children.text: tadatadrūpiṇo bhāvās tadatadrūpahetujāḥ/ tad rūpādi kim ajñānaṃ vijñānābhinnahetujam//

body.text: atha rūpopādānajanyatve 'pi vijñānasya na rūpātmatā, tathā jñānopādānajanyatve 'pi vijñānasya na jñānarūpatāṭataś ca nairātmyaprasaṅgaḥ / atha jñānopādānajanyatve jñānākāraparikalpanā, tathā rūpopādānajanyatve rūpākārātālokopādānajanyatve cālokākāratā prāpnoti / tataś cākārakadambātmakaṃ jñānaṃ prasaktam / aniṣṭaṃ caitad advayarūpatvenābhyupagamāt /
body.translated_text: If cognition, though produced with form as its material cause, is not of the nature of form, then similarly, even though produced with cognition as its material cause, cognition would not be of the nature of cognition — and the consequence of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) follows. If, because it is produced with cognition as its material cause, the cognition-form is attributed, then similarly, because it is produced with form as its material cause, the form-nature should be attributed; and because it is produced with light as its material cause, the light-nature should follow. And thus the consequence arises that cognition is an aggregate of multiple forms. And this is not desired, because it is accepted as having a non-dual nature.

children.text: atha rūpopādānajanyatve 'pi vijñānasya na rūpātmatā, tathā jñānopādānajanyatve 'pi vijñānasya na jñānarūpatāṭataś ca nairātmyaprasaṅgaḥ / atha jñānopādānajanyatve jñānākāraparikalpanā, tathā rūpopādānajanyatve rūpākārātālokopādānajanyatve cālokākāratā prāpnoti / tataś cākārakadambātmakaṃ jñānaṃ prasaktam / aniṣṭaṃ caitad advayarūpatvenābhyupagamāt /

body.text: 4.25b yat tad rūpotpādyaṃ vijñānaṃ, tat kim ekadeśena rūpotpādyatvena sthitaṃ sarvātmanā votpādyatvena paryavasitam? tad yady ekadeśena sthitaṃ, tad ayuktam, akhaṇḍasyaikadeśavirahāt / atha sarvātmanā rūpotpādyatvena paryavasitaṃ, tadā vijnānotpādyaṃ na prāpnoti, yathaikakārakasamūhotpādyatvena paryavasitasya kāryasya saṅghātāntarotpādyatvaṃ na dṛṣtam / tataś ca vijñānasaṅghātānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: [4.25b] That cognition which is produced by form — is it established as produced by form with respect to one part, or is it determined as produced with respect to its entire nature? If established with respect to one part, that is not justified, because what is undivided has no separate parts. If it is determined as produced by form with respect to its entire nature, then it cannot also be produced by cognition, just as an effect determined as produced by a single set of causal factors is not observed to be also produced by another aggregate. And thus the aggregate nature of cognition is not established.

children.text: 4.25b yat tad rūpotpādyaṃ vijñānaṃ, tat kim ekadeśena rūpotpādyatvena sthitaṃ sarvātmanā votpādyatvena paryavasitam? tad yady ekadeśena sthitaṃ, tad ayuktam, akhaṇḍasyaikadeśavirahāt / atha sarvātmanā rūpotpādyatvena paryavasitaṃ, tadā vijnānotpādyaṃ na prāpnoti, yathaikakārakasamūhotpādyatvena paryavasitasya kāryasya saṅghātāntarotpādyatvaṃ na dṛṣtam / tataś ca vijñānasaṅghātānupapattiḥ /

body.text: 4.25c tathā rūpam api jñānam ekadeśena kuryāt sarvātmanā karaṇaparyavasitaṃ vā / tad yady ekadeśena karoti, tad ayuktam, akhaṇḍasyaikadeśāyogāt /
body.translated_text: [4.25c] Similarly, would form produce cognition with respect to one part, or is its causal activity determined with respect to its entire nature? If it produces with respect to one part, that is not justified, because what is undivided cannot have separate parts.

children.text: 4.25c tathā rūpam api jñānam ekadeśena kuryāt sarvātmanā karaṇaparyavasitaṃ vā / tad yady ekadeśena karoti, tad ayuktam, akhaṇḍasyaikadeśāyogāt /

body.text: atha sarvātmanā karoti, tadā rūpaṃ sarvātmanā vijñānakaraṇe paryavasitaṃ na rūpāntarakaraṇe pravartate / yathaikakārakasāmagry ekakāryotpādanaparyavasitā kāryāntarasavitrī na bhavati, tathā rūpam api rūpāntarotpādakaṃ na bhavati / tataś ca rūpāntarasyākasmikatvam / tadākasmikatve kāryānumānaṃ vilupyate saugatānām / athānekakāryotpādakatvena paryavasitaṃ rūpasvarūpaṃ, tadā ghaṭasaṅkhyāsāmānyāder apy anekādhikaraṇāśritātmakaṃ rūpaṃ, vṛttivikalpadoṣānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: If it produces with respect to its entire nature, then form, being fully engaged in producing cognition, does not proceed to produce another form. Just as a set of causal factors fully engaged in producing one effect cannot be productive of another effect, so too form cannot be productive of another form. And therefore the next form would be causeless. If the next form were causeless, the causal inference of the <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists) would be undermined. If the nature of form is determined as productive of multiple effects, then even the form of pot, number, universal, and the like would rest in multiple substrates — and the defect of occurrence-deviation (<s>vṛttivikalpa</s>) would not arise.

children.text: atha sarvātmanā karoti, tadā rūpaṃ sarvātmanā vijñānakaraṇe paryavasitaṃ na rūpāntarakaraṇe pravartate / yathaikakārakasāmagry ekakāryotpādanaparyavasitā kāryāntarasavitrī na bhavati, tathā rūpam api rūpāntarotpādakaṃ na bhavati / tataś ca rūpāntarasyākasmikatvam / tadākasmikatve kāryānumānaṃ vilupyate saugatānām / athānekakāryotpādakatvena paryavasitaṃ rūpasvarūpaṃ, tadā ghaṭasaṅkhyāsāmānyāder apy anekādhikaraṇāśritātmakaṃ rūpaṃ, vṛttivikalpadoṣānupapattiḥ /

body.text:
d.1 ito 'pi vṛttivikalpadoṣānupapattir  vṛttivikalpadoṣeṇa vṛtter eva nirākaraṇaṃ kṛtaṃ, na ghaṭasaṅkhyāsāmānyādes, tato 'nyatvāt / na hy anyasyābhāve 'nyasyābhāvo 'sty asambandhāt / na hy anudakaḥ kamaṇḍalur ity ukte kamaṇḍalor abhāvaḥ pratīyate, kapālānāṃ tadudakasya vā, api tu kamaṇḍalunā sākam udakasya viśleṣamātraṃ pratīyate / nanu naiyāyikair vṛttimad ghaṭasāmānyam abhyupeyate / tadabhāve kathaṃ tasya saṃsthitiḥ? yady evaṃ rūparasavijñānānām api vṛttir abhyupeyate naiyāyikais, tadabhāve 'pi sadbhāvo 'bhyupagamyate teṣāṃ bhavadbhiḥ / atha tāni pratibhānti vṛttyabhāve 'pi, tena teṣām abhyupagamaḥ kriyate / yady evaṃ ghaṭasaṅkhyāsāmānyāder api svarūpaṃ pratibhāty abhinnānugatātmatayā / na cānubhūyamānasya nihnavo yuktaḥ sarvāpalāpaprasaṅgāt
/ anupalabdhau vā saiva samarthā, ataṃ vṛttivikalpadoṣeṇa / yady upalabhyate, tadā vṛttivikalpadoṣo na vaktavyaḥ / atha
nopalabhyate, tathāpi na vaktavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: [d.1] The defect of occurrence-deviation also fails for another reason: the defect of occurrence-deviation refutes only the occurrence of the universal, not the pot, number, universal, and the like, since they are different from it. For the non-existence of one thing does not entail the non-existence of another, due to lack of connection. When one says 'the water-pot has no water,' the non-existence of the water-pot is not understood, nor that of the potsherds or the water — rather, merely the separation of the water from the water-pot is understood. Objection: The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> accept that the pot-universal has occurrence in multiple substrates. In its absence, how can it subsist? If so, the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> also accept occurrence for form, taste, cognition, and the like — yet you also accept their existence even in the absence of such occurrence. If they are experienced even in the absence of occurrence, their acceptance is made on that basis. If so, the nature of pot, number, universal, and the like also appears as having an identical pervading nature. And it is not proper to deny what is experienced, lest everything be denied. Or if non-apprehension is the argument, that alone is sufficient — enough with the defect of occurrence-deviation. If it is apprehended, then the defect of occurrence-deviation should not be stated. If it is not apprehended, even then it should not be stated.

nopalabhyate, tathāpi na vaktavyaḥ /

body.text: d.2 yad apy uktaṃ  deśabhedenāgrahaṇād ghaṭasāmānyānupapattis tad apy ayuktam / na deśabhedena vastūnāṃ bhedo, 'pi tv ākārabhedenābhinnānugatātmatayā tayoḥ svarūpam anubhūyate / na deśabhedāgrahaṇena svāvayavādhikaraṇena saha tayos tādātmyaṃ sidhyaty asattvaṃ vā / yady ākārabhedena grahaṇaṃ, tadā deśabhedenāgrahaṇasyāprayojakatvam, ākārabhedagrahaṇena svarūpānyatvasya prabodhitatvāt / athākārānyatvena nāvabodho 'sti, saivāstv asadvyavahārasamarthatvāt / kiṃ deśabhedāgrahaṇena? svahetor eva niyatadeśakālaniyamitasyotpatter na deśāntarādau grahaṇam / anyathā rūpāder asattvaṃ syād itaretaradeśalagnasyāgrahaṇāt /
body.translated_text: [d.2] As for the claim that pot-universality is not established because it is not grasped through spatial difference — that too is not justified. Things are not differentiated by spatial difference, but rather their nature is experienced as having an identical pervading form through difference of configuration. Nor is identity with its own constituent substrates, or non-existence, established through non-apprehension via spatial difference. If grasping is through difference of configuration, then non-apprehension through spatial difference is irrelevant, since the difference of nature is awakened by grasping the difference of configuration. If there is no awareness through difference of configuration, let that be so, since it is capable of establishing the convention of non-existence. What use is non-apprehension through spatial difference? For due to the arising of what is determined by a fixed place and time from its own cause alone, there is no apprehension in another place, etc. Otherwise, form and the like would be non-existent, due to non-apprehension of what is located in other places.

body.text: d.3 yad apy uktaṃ nāsti ghaṭasāmānyaṃ tadagrahe 'grahāt / kim anena kriyate? kim avayavādhikaraṇāvyatirekapratipādanam āho 'sattvapratipādanam? tad yady avyatirekapratipādanaṃ kriyate, kasyātra pakṣīkaraṇam? kiṃ ghaṭasāmānyasyāho tadavayavādhikaraṇasya? tad yadi ghaṭasāmānyasya pakṣīkaraṇaṃ, tat kim avagatasyānavagatasya vā? tad yady anavagatasya, tad ayuktam / na hy anavagate dharmiṇi hetor utthānam asti / na cāśrayavaikalye gamakatvam / athāvagatasya, tadā tenaiva bhinnākārāvagamenāvyatirekapratyāyakasādhanaṃ bādhyate / atha tadavayavādhikaraṇasya pakṣīkaraṇaṃ, tatrāpi kiṃ svasmāt svarūpād avyatirekaḥ sādhyatāho parasmād iti?
body.translated_text: [d.3] As for the claim 'pot-universality does not exist because it is not apprehended when the constituent parts are not apprehended' — what is accomplished by this? Is it establishing non-difference from the constituent substrates, or establishing non-existence? If non-difference is being established — what is made the subject here? The pot-universal, or its constituent substrates? If the pot-universal is the subject — is it known or unknown? If unknown, that is not justified, for there is no arising of an inferential mark regarding an unknown subject. Nor is there probative force when the substrate is deficient. If known, then that very grasping of its different configuration refutes the means of proof that would establish non-difference. If the constituent substrates are made the subject — is non-difference from their own nature being proved, or from something else?

children.text: d.3 yad apy uktaṃ nāsti ghaṭasāmānyaṃ tadagrahe 'grahāt / kim anena kriyate? kim avayavādhikaraṇāvyatirekapratipādanam āho 'sattvapratipādanam? tad yady avyatirekapratipādanaṃ kriyate, kasyātra pakṣīkaraṇam? kiṃ ghaṭasāmānyasyāho tadavayavādhikaraṇasya? tad yadi ghaṭasāmānyasya pakṣīkaraṇaṃ, tat kim avagatasyānavagatasya vā? tad yady anavagatasya, tad ayuktam / na hy anavagate dharmiṇi hetor utthānam asti / na cāśrayavaikalye gamakatvam / athāvagatasya, tadā tenaiva bhinnākārāvagamenāvyatirekapratyāyakasādhanaṃ bādhyate / atha tadavayavādhikaraṇasya pakṣīkaraṇaṃ, tatrāpi kiṃ svasmāt svarūpād avyatirekaḥ sādhyatā aho parasmād iti?

body.text: yadi svasmāt svarūpād avyatirekaḥ sādhyate, siddhasādhyatayā sambodhayitavyāḥ / atha parasmād avyatirekaḥ sādhyate, sa parātmā pratipanno 'pratipanno vā? yadi pratipannaḥ, sa kiṃ bhinnākāratayāvagato 'bhinnākāratayā vā?
body.translated_text: If non-difference from their own nature is being proved, you should be informed that this is proving what is already established. If non-difference from something else is being proved — is that other entity accepted or not accepted? If accepted, is it cognized as having a different configuration or as having an identical configuration?

children.text: yadi svasmāt svarūpād avyatirekaḥ sādhyate, siddhasādhyatayā sambodhayitavyāḥ / atha parasmād avyatirekaḥ sādhyate, sa parātmā pratipanno 'pratipanno vā? yadi pratipannaḥ, sa kiṃ bhinnākāratayāvagato 'bhinnākāratayā vā?

body.text:
tad yadi bhinnākāratayopalabdhas, tadānenaiva bhinnākārāvagamenābhedapratyāyakaṃ sādhanaṃ bādhyate / athābhinnākāratayāvagato, na tarhi parātmā / idānīṃ svasmāt svarūpād avyatirekaḥ sādhyateti siddhasādhyatayā sambodhayitavyāḥ / athānavagato, na tarhy ekatvaṃ rathaturagaviṣāṇayor iva / athābhāvaḥ sādhyas, tatrāpi kasya pakṣīkaraṇam? kiṃ ghaṭasāmānyasyāho tad avayavādhikaraṇasya? tad yadi ghaṭasāmānyasya pakṣīkaraṇaṃ, tat kim avagatasyānavagatasya vā? yady avagatasya, tadā tenaiva sadbhāvāvagamenābhāvahetor bādhyamānatvād agamakatvam / atha nāvagataṃ, kathaṃ tasya pakṣīkaraṇaṃ svayam anavagatasya pakṣīkaraṇāyogāt? athāvayavādhikaraṇasya pakṣīkaraṇaṃ ghaṭasāmānyaṃ nāstīti pratijñā tadagrahe 'grahād ity asya hetos tadabhāvena saha sambandho nāsti /
tādātmyatadutpattisambandhābhāve sati kathaṃ gamakatvam? tadagrahe 'grahād ity asya ko 'rthaḥ? kim
avayavādhikaraṇagrahaṇam eva ghaṭasāmānyasya grahaṇam āho 'vayavādhikaraṇagrahaṇānantaraṃ ghaṭasāmānyasya grahaṇaṃ kiṃ vā ghaṭasāmānyasyāgrahaṇam eva vivakṣitam? tad yady avayavādhikaraṇagrahaṇam eva ghaṭasāmānyasya grahaṇaṃ vivakṣitaṃ, tadā nānenāvyatireko 'nyatarāsattvaṃ vā pratipādyate / yathā nīlataddhiyor ekopalambhe 'pi nānyatarābhāvo 'vyatireko vā, tathā nīlalohitayor ekopalambhe 'pi nānyatarābhāvo 'vyatireko vā / athāvayavādhikaraṇagrahaṇānantaraṃ ghaṭasāmānyagrahaṇaṃ vivakṣitaṃ, tadā nānenāvyatirekaḥ sādhyate 'nyatarāsattvaṃ vā / yathā rūpagrahaṇānantaraṃ rasasaṃvedanaṃ na tayor ekatāṃ gamayaty 'nyatarāsattvaṃ vā / athāgrahaṇam eva vivakṣitaṃ ghaṭasāmānyasya, tadā tadagrahe 'grahād ity etan na vaktavyam / agrahād ity etāvad astu / na
hy anyasyāgrahe tadanupalambhasiddhis tatsvabhāvavinivṛttinibandhanatvāt tadanupalambhasya / na cāyaṃ
vyatirekārtho labhyate tadagrahe 'grahād ity asya hetor ghaṭasāmānyasyāgrahaṇam eva, api tv avayavādhikaraṇagrahaṇānantaraṃ ghaṭasāmānyasya grahaṇaṃ labhyate / tataś ca viparītasādhanād viruddho bhavati /
body.translated_text:
Now, if [the other entity] is cognized as having a different configuration, then by this very cognition of different configuration, the means of proof that would establish non-difference is refuted. If it is cognized as having an identical configuration, then it is not another entity. Now non-difference from one's own nature is being proved — you should be informed that this is proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhya</s>). If it is not cognized, then there is no unity between the two, just as between a chariot and a horse's horn. If non-existence is what is being proved — then of what is the subject-locus (<s>pakṣa</s>) made? Is it of the pot-universal (<s>ghaṭasāmānya</s>), or of the substratum of its parts? If the pot-universal is made the subject-locus — is it of what is known or unknown? If of what is known, then by that very cognition of its existence, the reason for non-existence is refuted due to being sublated, hence it is non-probative. If it is not known, how can it be made the subject-locus, since what is itself unknown cannot serve as a subject-locus? If the substratum of the parts is made the subject-locus, and the proposition is 'the pot-universal does not exist,' then this reason — 'because it is not grasped when that is not grasped' — has no connection with that non-existence.
In the absence of the relation of <s>tādātmya</s> (identity) and <s>tadutpatti</s> (origination), how can there be probative force? What is the meaning of 'because it is not grasped when that is not grasped'? Does it mean that the grasping of the substratum of parts is itself the grasping of the pot-universal, or that after grasping the substratum of parts the pot-universal is grasped, or that the non-grasping of the pot-universal is what is intended? If the grasping of the substratum of parts is itself the grasping of the pot-universal that is intended, then by this, neither non-difference nor the non-existence of either is established. Just as in the co-apprehension of blue and its substrate, there is neither the non-existence of either nor non-difference, so too in the co-apprehension of blue and red, there is neither the non-existence of either nor non-difference. If after the grasping of the substratum of parts, the grasping of the pot-universal is intended, then by this, neither non-difference is established nor the non-existence of either. Just as the sensing of taste after the grasping of form does not prove their identity or the non-existence of either. If the non-grasping of the pot-universal is what is intended, then the statement 'because of non-grasping when that is not grasped' should not be made; 'because of non-grasping' alone suffices. For the non-apprehension proof of one thing is not established through the non-grasping of another, since non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) has the cessation of the thing's own nature as its basis. Nor is the meaning of mutual exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>) obtained from this reason 'because of non-grasping when that is not grasped' — that is, the non-grasping of the pot-universal — but rather, the grasping of the pot-universal after grasping the substratum of parts is obtained. And thus, from proving the opposite, it becomes contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>).

body.text:
d.4 yad apy abhyadhāyy ekapiṇḍagrahaṇakālopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdher nāsti sāmānyam / kaivam āha  nopalabdhaṃ sāmānyam? api tūpalabdham eva / katham jñāyate? dvitīyādipiṇḍadarśane sati pūrve piṇḍe smṛtidarśanād, anena sadṛśo 'sāv evam anusmarati / athavaikapiṇḍagrahaṇakāle tad upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ na bhavati tena nopalabhyate / upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptir ihānekasahakāripiṇḍopanipātaḥ / yadi copalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ, kathaṃ nopalabhyate? atha nopalabhyate, na tarhy.upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptam / upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptir iha pratyayāntarasākalyaṃ svabhāvaviśeṣaś ca / etac ced vidyate katham anupalabdhiḥ? evambhūtasyāpy anupalambhe parikalpyamāne sarvavastūnām anupalambhaprasaṅgaḥ / upalabdhau vānyat kāraṇam anveṣṭavyam / atha pratyayāntarasākalyamātraṃ
vivakṣitaṃ, na tatsvabhāvaviśeṣaḥ / yady evam adṛśyasyaivānupalabdhir, na dṛśyānupalabdhir asti / yadi
cānyakārakasākalyam upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptir abhidhīyate, tadāpy upalabdhyā bhavitavyaṃ nānupalabdhyā / itarakārakasākalyaṃ hy upalambhajananasāmarthyam / tac ced vidyate, katham anupalabdhiḥ? tasmād anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyaivānupalabdhir, nopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya /
body.translated_text: [d.4] As for the further claim that 'the universal does not exist because of the non-apprehension of what meets the conditions for apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>) at the time of grasping a single lump' — who says that the universal is not apprehended? Rather, it is indeed apprehended. How is this known? Because upon seeing a second lump and so on, memory regarding the first lump is observed — 'that one was similar to this one,' thus one recollects. Or alternatively, at the time of grasping a single lump, it does not meet the conditions for apprehension, and therefore it is not apprehended. The meeting of conditions for apprehension here means the presence of multiple cooperating lumps. If it meets the conditions for apprehension, how can it not be apprehended? If it is not apprehended, then it does not meet the conditions for apprehension. The meeting of conditions for apprehension here means the totality of other causal factors and the specific nature. If this is present, how can there be non-apprehension? If non-apprehension is imagined even for such a thing, the absurd consequence of non-apprehension of all things follows. Or another cause for apprehension must be sought. If only the totality of other causal factors is intended, not its specific nature — if so, then there is only non-apprehension of what is imperceptible, not non-apprehension of the perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalabdhi</s>). If the totality of other causal factors is what is called meeting the conditions for apprehension, then there should be apprehension, not non-apprehension. For the totality of other causal factors is the capacity for producing apprehension. If that is present, how can there be non-apprehension? Therefore, there is non-apprehension only of what meets the conditions for non-apprehension, not of what meets the conditions for apprehension.

body.text: d.5 yad apy uvāca  kṣīrodakavad vivekenāgrahaṇān nāsti sāmānyaṃ  tad apy ayuktam / viveko hy ākārānyatvaṃ vyaktīnām ananugamarūpatā, sāmānyaṃ tv anugatākāram anayoḥ sārūpyaṃ taiḥ saha sārūpyam as yeti viviktākārāvagamadarśanāt / tathā kṣīrodakayor api viviktam eva grahaṇam / tatra kṣīrodakayor ekabhājananikṣepe sati, kiṃ kevalaṃ kṣīraṃ pratibhāty āhodakam ubhayaṃ vā? tad yadi kṣīram eva pratibhāti, kathaṃ tad udakākārān na viviktaṃ bhavati? athodakaṃ kevalaṃ pratibhāti, tad api kathaṃ kṣīrān na viviktaṃ bhavati? athobhayaṃ pratibhāti, tadobhayor itaretarākāraviViktayor grahaṇaṃ tādātmyavyatirekāt /
body.translated_text: [d.5] As for the further claim that 'the universal does not exist because it is not grasped as separate, like milk and water' — that too is unjustified. For differentiation means the otherness of configuration among individuals — the non-pervading form, while the universal is the pervading configuration. The similarity between these two — that 'this has similarity with those' — is observed from the cognition of distinct configurations. Similarly, even with milk and water, the grasping is indeed distinct. When milk and water are placed in a single vessel, does only milk appear, or only water, or both? If only milk appears, how is it not differentiated from the form of water? If only water appears, how is it not differentiated from milk? If both appear, then there is grasping of both as differentiated from each other's configuration, due to the exclusion of identity.

body.text: d.6 yad apy anyad uktam ekatra dṛṣṭo bhedo hi kvacin nānyatra dṛśyate/ na tasmād bhinnam asty anyat sāmānyaṃ buddhyabhedataḥ// ity etad apy ayuktam / ekatra dṛṣṭasya bhedasyānyatra darśanam asty eva / yathā ghaṭavastrāder ekāvayavoparidṛṣṭasyāvayavāntaralagnasyopalambhas, tathā sāmānyam api bhinnam asty anugatākārasya buddhibhedenādhyavasīyamānatvāt /
body.translated_text: [d.6] As for the further statement: 'A difference seen in one place is not seen elsewhere; therefore, there is no other separate universal, due to non-difference in cognition' — this too is unjustified. The seeing elsewhere of a difference seen in one place is indeed possible. Just as a part adhering to another component, seen upon one component of pot, cloth, and the like, is apprehended, so too the universal is indeed different, because the pervading configuration is determined by difference of cognition.

body.text:
d.7 yad apy anyad uktaṃ nityasya krametarābhyām arthakriyākaraṇasāmarthyaṃ nāstīty asat sāmānyaṃ, tad etad ayuktam / ubhayathāpy arthakriyāsampādanam upapadyate yugapat krameṇa ca / nanu kramakartṛtvam abhinnasya nopapadyate, kāryasyaikakālīnatā prāpnoti / etac cāsamīcīnam / yathā bhavatāṃ pakṣaikaṃ nīlasvalakṣaṇam anekākārakāryaṃ niyatadeśasambandhi janayati nayanālokamanaskārādirūpaṃ, na ca kāryāṇām ekākārataikadeśasambandhitā vā vidyataikasvabhāvasamudbhavatve 'pi, tathehāpy evambhūtaṃ / tat sāmānyaṃ yat krametarābhyāṃ kāryotpādātmakam / nanu yadi krameṇa kāryaṃ karoti, tadā tad eva janakaṃ tad eva cājanakam / satyaṃ, tad eva janakaṃ tad eva cājanakam / nanu janakājanakayor bhedaprasaṅgaḥ / na prasaṅgo 'sti / yathā tvadīye pakṣaikaṃ nīlasvalakṣaṇaṃ svakāryāpekṣayā
janakaṃ, svakāraṇātmāpekṣayā tv ajanakaṃ, na tasya svarūpabhedo 'sti / atha
svakāraṇam ātmānaṃ ca janayati, tad ayuktam / tad ātmānaṃ kurvad utpannaṃ vā kuryād anutpannaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: [d.7] As for the further statement that 'because an eternal entity has no capacity to perform <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) either sequentially or otherwise, the universal is non-existent' — that is unjustified. The accomplishment of causal efficacy is possible in both ways — simultaneously and sequentially. Objection: Sequential agency for what is undifferentiated is not possible; the simultaneity of the effect would follow. This is not correct. Just as in your own position, a single blue <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), connected with a fixed location, produces effects of many kinds — in the form of eye, light, mental attention, and the like — yet the effects do not have uniformity or connection with a single location, even though they arise from a single nature, so too here it is the same. That universal is one whose nature is producing effects both sequentially and otherwise. Objection: If it produces effects sequentially, then it is both a producer and a non-producer. True, it is both a producer and a non-producer. Objection: The absurd consequence of difference between the producer and non-producer follows. There is no such consequence. Just as in your own position, a single blue <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) is a producer with respect to its own effect, but a non-producer with respect to its own causal nature, yet there is no difference in its own nature. If it produces its own cause and itself, that is unjustified — in producing itself, would it produce what is already arisen or what has not arisen?

tad yady utpannaṃ karoti, tad ayuktaṃ, kṛtasya karaṇāyogāt / athānutpannaṃ karoty asataḥ kaḥ kārakārthaḥ? tathā svakāraṇam api na janayatītaretarāśrayatvadoṣaprasaṅgāt / atas tad eva kārakaṃ tad eva cākārakam iti tathā sāmānyam api janakam ajanakaṃ ca / na cārthakriyākartṛtvābhāve 'sattvaṃ sidhyati / yathā vahner ayogolakāṅgārāvasthāyāṃ dhūmotpādakatvābhāve 'pi na nivartate vahnirūpatā, svahetor eva tathābhūtasyotpatter vahnisvabhāvasya dhūmājanakātmakasya ca, tathānyad api kāryaṃ svahetunotpāditaṃ yad vastusvabhāvaṃ kāryājanakātmakaṃ ca / tathā sāmānyam api vastubhūtaṃ na ca kāryam utpādayati / nanu yadi kāryaṃ notpādayati, tad astīti kathaṃ vetsi? tadupalabdhyā / nanu tadanutpādyā kathaṃ tadgṛhītir bhavati? svahetusāmarthyaniyamitāyās tadgṛhītyātmatayotpatteḥ / na ca
tadutpādyatvena tadgṛhītitvaṃ, cakṣurāder api saṃvedyatvaprasaṅgāt / na ca
viṣayākārayogitvena tadgṛhītitvaṃ vijñānātmatāvyatirekeṇa viṣayākārasamāveśāyogāt / yo 'sāv ākāro viṣayārpitaḥ, sa kiṃ jñānākārād bhinno 'bhinno vā? yadi bhinnaḥ, sa tāttviko 'tāttviko vā / yadi tāttvikas, tadgatiḥ katham? kiṃ svasaṃvedyatvenāho janakatvākārārpakatvena? tad yadi svasaṃvedyatvena, tad ayuktam, avijñānātmatayā svasaṃvedyatvāyogāt / atha janakatvākārārpakatvena, tadā prāptākāraparamparā / athātāttvikas, tadgatir nopapadyate svasaṃvedyatvajanakatvavyatirekāt / athāvyatiriktaḥ, sa tāttviko 'tāttviko vā / yadi tāttvikaḥ, sa jaḍātmā tadviparīto vā / yadi jaḍātmā, na tarhi citā saha tādātmyam / cidacitos tādātmyānupapattiḥ / atha tadviparītas, tadā jñānamātratā syāt / jñānarūpatā ca sarvajñānasādhāraṇā pratikarmavyavasthānupapattiḥ / athātāttvikas, tadā jñānasyāpy
atāttvikatvaṃ prāpnoti / yadi ca vijñānatādātmyenākārotpattir bhavati, vijñānaṃ
sarvakārakaniṣpādyatvena sādhāraṇaṃ pratikarmavyavasthānupapattiḥ / evaṃ ca sati yad uktam
body.translated_text: If it produces what is already produced, that is not justified, because what is already accomplished cannot be accomplished again. If it produces what is not yet produced — what causal purpose can there be with respect to what is non-existent? Similarly, it does not produce its own cause either, because the defect of mutual dependence would follow. Therefore, that very thing is both a causal agent and a non-agent — and similarly, the universal too is both a producer and a non-producer. Nor is non-existence established merely by the absence of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>). Just as in the case of fire in the state of an iron ball or charcoal, even though the capacity to produce smoke is absent, the nature of fire does not cease — because something of that nature arises from its own cause, having the nature of fire and also having the nature of not producing smoke — so too other effects produced by their own causes have the nature of real things and also the nature of not producing [further] effects. Similarly, the universal too is a real entity and yet does not produce an effect. Objection: If it does not produce an effect, how do you know it exists? By its apprehension. Objection: If it does not produce that [apprehension], how can there be apprehension of it? Because the apprehension arises as having the nature of grasping it, determined by the capacity of its own cause. Nor is the grasping of it due to being produced by it, for otherwise even the eye and the like would absurdly be objects of experience. Nor is the grasping of it due to possessing the object-form, because apart from the nature of cognition, the incorporation of an object-form is impossible. That form which is imparted by the object — is it different from the cognition-form or not different? If different, is it real or unreal? If real, how is it cognized? By self-awareness, or by productivity and form-imparting? If by self-awareness, that is not justified, because what is not of the nature of cognition cannot be self-aware. If by productivity and form-imparting, then an infinite regress of forms follows. If unreal, its cognition is not established, because of the absence of self-awareness and productivity. If not different, is it real or unreal? If real, is it of an insentient nature or the opposite? If of an insentient nature, then it has no identity with consciousness. The identity of the sentient and the insentient is impossible. If of the opposite nature, then it would be mere cognition. And the cognition-nature being common to all cognitions, the assignment of specific functions would be impossible. If unreal, then the unreality of cognition too would follow. And if the form arises as identical with cognition, then cognition, being commonly produced by all causal factors, would make the assignment of specific functions impossible. And this being the case, what was stated —

viṣayākārayogitvena tadgṛhītitvaṃ vijñānātmatāvyatirekeṇa viṣayākārasamāveśāyogāt / yo 'sāv ākāro viṣayārpitaḥ, sa kiṃ jñānākārād bhinno 'bhinno vā? yadi bhinnaḥ, sa tāttviko 'tāttviko vā / yadi tāttvikas, tadgatiḥ katham? kiṃ svasaṃvedyatvenāho janakatvākārārpakatvena? tad yadi svasaṃvedyatvena, tad ayuktam, avijñānātmatayā svasaṃvedyatvāyogāt / atha janakatvākārārpakatvena, tadā prāptākāraparamparā / athātāttvikas, tadgatir nopapadyate svasaṃvedyatvajanakatvavyatirekāt / athāvyatiriktaḥ, sa tāttviko 'tāttviko vā / yadi tāttvikaḥ, sa jaḍātmā tadviparīto vā / yadi jaḍātmā, na tarhi citā saha tādātmyam / cidacitos tādātmyānupapattiḥ / atha tadviparītas, tadā jñānamātratā syāt / jñānarūpatā ca sarvajñānasādhāraṇā pratikarmavyavasthānupapattiḥ / athātāttvikas, tadā jñānasyāpy
atāttvikatvaṃ prāpnoti / yadi ca vijñānatādātmyenākārotpattir bhavati, vijñānaṃ
sarvakārakaniṣpādyatvena sādhāraṇaṃ pratikarmavyavasthānupapattiḥ / evaṃ ca sati yad uktam

d.8 tad evaṃ vṛttivikalpādidūṣaṇaṃ sāmānyādau na sambhavati  yathaikaṃ rūpam anekakāryotpādakatvena sādhāraṇaṃ, tathaikaṃ sāmānyam anekādhārasādhāraṇam / athaikaṃ rūpaṃ nānekaṃ kāryaṃ janayaty, api tv ekam eva, tatrāpi kiṃ rūpam eva kevalam utpādayaty uta jñānam eva? tad yadi rūpam eva kevalam utpādayati, tadā rūpasyāgrahaṇaṃ prāpnoti vijñānājananāt / atha jñānam eva kevalam utpādayati, tathāpi mānasaṃ pratyakṣaṃ na prāpnoti / svaviṣayānantaraviṣayasahakāriṇendriyajñānena yaj janyate, tan mānasaṃ pratyakṣam / na ca svaviṣayānantarabhāvī viṣayo'sti rūpāntarājananāt6ṭasmād ekam eva rūpaṃ vijñānanīlādikāryasādhāraṇaṃ pratipattavyam / cakṣūrūpālokādīni kāraṇāni vijñānam utpādayanti, tāni kim ekasvabhāvayuktāny āho niyatasvabhāvayuktāni?
tad yady ekasvabhāvatayotpādayanti, tadā kārakaikatvaṃ prāpnoty abhinnasvabhāvayogitvāt /
body.translated_text:
[d.8] Thus, the refutation through occurrence-deviation (<s>vṛttivikalpa</s>) and the like does not apply to universals and the rest. Just as a single form is common to the production of multiple effects, so too a single universal is common to multiple substrates. Now if a single form does not produce multiple effects but only one, then does it produce only form, or only cognition? If it produces only form, then form would not be apprehended, because cognition is not produced. If it produces only cognition, then even so, mental perception (<s>mānasa pratyakṣa</s>) would not be obtained. Mental perception is that which is produced by a sense-cognition assisted by the immediately subsequent object of its own object-domain. But there is no immediately subsequent object, because no further form is produced. Therefore, a single form must be understood as common to the production of effects such as cognition, blue, and the like. The causal factors — the eye, form, light, and the like — that produce cognition: do they possess a single nature, or do they possess distinct natures?
If they produce with a single nature, then the consequence of oneness of the causal factors follows, because they possess an undifferentiated nature.

atha niyatasvabhāvayuktāni jñānarūpaṃ kāryaṃ janayanti, tadā vijñānasyābhedarūpatā nivartate niyatasvabhāvakārakajanyatvād rūpaśabdādivat / atha vividhād api kāraṇād akhaṇḍitarūpaṃ kāryaṃ bhavati / evaṃ ca kāryabhedād bhinnakāraṇānumānaṃ nivartate / ekasvabhāvād api vijñānād anekaṃ nayanālokādikāryam utpadyate / anekasmād apy ekaṃ bhavati / evaṃ ca sati niyatakāryadarśane niyatakāraṇānumānaṃ nivartate / athaikasmād eva kāraṇād ekaṃ kāryaṃ bhavati na bahūnāṃ saṅkalitānām ekaphalotpādakatvam / tataś ca niyatakāryadarśane niyatakāraṇānumānaṃ kena nivāryate? tad etad asamīcīnam / yady ekaṃ kāraṇam ekaṃ kāryaṃ janayati tadābhyupagamavirodhaś  caturbhyaś cittacaittā bhavanti bodhād bodharūpatā viṣayād viṣayākāratetyādi / ekam eva janayati, kiṃ samānajātīyatvenāho
tadākāratvena kiṃ vā pūrvāparakālabhāvitvena? tad yadi
samānajātīyatvena janakatvaṃ, tadā samānajātīyaṃ paścād utpannam api janayet / atha tadākārānukāritvena janakaṃ, tatrāpy etad eva dūṣaṇam / atha pūrvāparakālabhāvitvena janakaṃ, na tarhīdaṃ vaktavyam ekam eva janakaṃ cakṣūrūpālokamanaskārāṇāṃ pūrvakālabhāvitvāviśeṣāt / evaṃ cānekopādānotpādyatvenākārakadambakasvarūpaṃ vijñānaṃ prasaktam / rūpādyākāraparihāre vā vijñānākārasyāpy anupapattiḥ / tadanupapattau nairātmyaprasaṅgaḥ / kiṃ ca jñānaṃ kāryaikasvabhāvaṃ kāraṇaikasvabhāvam ubhayasvabhāvaṃ vā / tad yadi kāraṇaikasvabhāvaṃ, tadā kāryarūpatā na sambhavati / tadabhāve na vastutvaṃ saṃskṛtānāṃ vastutvābhyupagamāt / nāpi kāraṇarūpatopapadyate 'nādhīyamānātiśayatvena janakatvāyogāt / athakāryaikasvabhāvaṃ, tathāpi na sadātmakam
arthakriyākaraṇe vastutvavirahāt / athobhayātmakam / ekam anekātmakaṃ bhavati / kena
tvaṃ vipralambhitaḥ? na hy ekasyānekanāmakaraṇe nānātopapadyate / na cānekanāmakaraṇam upapadyate nimittasyāvicitratvāt / evaṃ vijñānasyāsambhave sati santānānupapattir abhrāntabhrāntadvaitasyānupapattiś ca /
body.translated_text: If they possess distinct natures and produce the effect that is cognition-form, then the undifferentiated nature of cognition would cease, because it is produced by causal factors with distinct natures, just like form, sound, and the like. Now if from diverse causes too, an effect of unbroken nature arises — then the inference of distinct causes from the difference of effects would cease. From cognition too, which has a single nature, multiple effects such as the eye, light, and the like would arise. And from multiple causes too, a single effect would arise. And this being so, the inference of specific causes from observing specific effects would cease. Now if from a single cause only a single effect arises, and the aggregate of multiple [factors] does not have the capacity to produce a single result — then what prevents the inference of specific causes from observing specific effects? This too is improper. If a single cause produces a single effect, then there would be a contradiction with one's own position — 'from the four [conditions] arise <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caittas</s> (mental factors); from awakening comes the nature of awakening; from the object comes the object-form' — and so on. It produces only one effect — is that by virtue of being of the same class, by virtue of having its form, or by virtue of being temporally prior and posterior? If productivity is by virtue of being of the same class, then even something of the same class arising later would produce [it]. If it is productive by virtue of conforming to its form, the same refutation applies. If it is productive by virtue of being temporally prior and posterior, then it should not be said that only one thing is the producer, because there is no difference in temporal priority among the eye, form, light, and mental attention. And thus the consequence follows that cognition, being produced by multiple material causes, has the nature of an aggregate of forms. Or if the form of color and the like is removed, the form of cognition too would be impossible. And in its impossibility, the consequence of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) follows. Furthermore, is cognition of a single nature as effect, of a single nature as cause, or of both natures? If of a single nature as cause, then the effect-nature is not possible. In its absence, there is no real existence, because real existence is accepted only for conditioned things. Nor is the cause-nature established, because what does not acquire any additional capacity cannot be a producer. If of a single nature as effect, even so it is not of the nature of a real entity, because of the absence of real existence in the absence of causal efficacy. If of both natures — a single thing having multiple natures — by whom have you been deceived? For the multiplicity of a single thing is not established merely by giving it multiple names. Nor is giving multiple names justified, because the basis is not variegated. Thus, when the existence of cognition is impossible, the impossibility of the continuum (<s>santāna</s>) follows, and the impossibility of the duality of erroneous and non-erroneous also follows.

body.text: e.1 ito 'pi santānasyāsiddhir  vijñānasyaikatvāt / tadekatvaṃ cākārāntarasyānupapatteḥ / upapattau vā jñānākāravirahaprasaṅgaḥ / tatprasaktau ca santānānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: [e.1] For this further reason too, the continuum is not established: because cognition is unitary. And its unitariness is because no other form is possible. Or if another form were possible, the consequence of the absence of the cognition-form would follow. And in that consequence, the impossibility of the continuum follows.

children.text: e.1 ito 'pi santānasyāsiddhir -- vijñānasyaikatvāt / tadekatvaṃ cākārāntarasyānupapatteḥ / upapattau vā jñānākāravirahaprasaṅgaḥ / tatprasaktau ca santānānupapattiḥ /

body.text: e.2 ito 'pi vijñānasantānānupapattir  vijñānam asaddharmāt sadātmatayā nivartate, svarūpāntarāt tu kathaṃ vyāvartate? kiṃ sadātmatayāhākārāntareṇa? tad yadi sadātmatayā vyāvartate, tadā rūpāder asadākāratā prāpnoti vājiviṣāṇayor iva / athākārāntareṇa nivartate, tadā jñānasyāsatsvabhāvatā prāpnoti turagaviṣāṇavad ity atha vijñānākāratayā nivartate rūpādibhyo vijñānaṃ, sā vijñānākāratā satsvabhāvāsatsvabhāvā vā tad yadi satsvabhāvā, tadā jñānākāratayā nivartateti kim uktaṃ bhavati? sadātmatayā nivartate vijñānasadākārayor avyatirekāt / tataś ca rūpāder asadākāratā prāpnoti turagaviṣāṇavad iti pūrvoditam eva dūṣaṇam āpadyate / athāsatsvabhāvā, tadā kharaviṣāṇavad vijñānarūpatāṃ parityajati / tyāge vijñānasantānānupapattiḥ / tadanupapattau caityavandanādikriyānarthakyam /
body.translated_text: [e.2] For this further reason too, the cognition-continuum (<s>vijñānasantāna</s>) is impossible: cognition is distinguished from non-existence by virtue of being a real entity, but how is it distinguished from its own other form? Is it by virtue of being a real entity, or by virtue of another form? If it is distinguished by virtue of being a real entity, then form and the like would absurdly have the nature of non-existence, like a hare's horn. If it is distinguished by another form, then cognition would absurdly have the nature of non-existence, like a horse's horn. Now if cognition is distinguished from form and the like by virtue of having the cognition-form — is that cognition-form of the nature of a real entity or of a non-real entity? If of the nature of a real entity, then what is meant by saying 'it is distinguished by the cognition-form'? It means it is distinguished by virtue of being a real entity, because cognition and the real-entity-form are non-different. And thus the previously stated refutation applies — that form and the like would absurdly have the nature of non-existence, like a horse's horn. If of the nature of a non-real entity, then like a donkey's horn, it abandons its cognition-nature. And upon that abandonment, the cognition-continuum is impossible. And in its impossibility, the activities of worshipping <s>caityas</s> (sacred shrines) and the like become purposeless.

children.text: e.2 ito 'pi vijñānasantānānupapattir -- vijñānam asaddharmāt sadātmatayā nivartate, svarūpāntarāt tu kathaṃ vyāvartate? kiṃ sadātmatayāhā akārāntareṇa? tad yadi sadātmatayā vyāvartate, tadā rūpāder asadākāratā prāpnoti vājiviṣāṇayor iva / athākārāntareṇa nivartate, tadā jñānasyāsatsvabhāvatā prāpnoti turagaviṣāṇavad ity atha vijñānākāratayā nivartate rūpādibhyo vijñānaṃ, sā vijñānākāratā satsvabhāvāsatsvabhāvā vā tad yadi satsvabhāvā, tadā jñānākāratayā nivartata iti kim uktaṃ bhavati? sadātmatayā nivartate vijñānasadākārayor avyatirekāt / tataś ca rūpāder asadākāratā prāpnoti turagaviṣāṇavad iti pūrvoditam eva dūṣaṇam āpadyate / athāsatsvabhāvā, tadā kharaviṣāṇavad vijñānarūpatāṃ parityajati / tyāge vijñānasantānānupapattiḥ / tadanupapattau caityavandanādikriyānarthakyam /

body.text:
e.3 ito 'pi vijñānasantānānupapattis  tadutpādakavijñānasya pūrvāparasahotpannavijñānaṃ prati svarūpāviśeṣāt / yad eva pūrvasahotpannavijñānāpekṣayā svarūpaṃ tad evāparavijñānāpekṣayāpi svarūpaṃ vijñānasya niravayavatvena / tataś ca yathā pūrvasahotpannavijñānasya hetur na bhavaty, evam aparavijñānasyāpi hetur na bhavati tatsvarūpavyatiriktavyāpārātiśayasyānupalabdheḥ / atha pūrvakālabhāvaivātiśayas tena tasya hetutvam upapādyate / yady evaṃ yathā devadattajñānapūrvakālabhāvi devadattajñānaṃ devadattajñānakāraṇaṃ, tathā sarvapuruṣajñānānāṃ devadattajñānapūrvakālotpannānāṃ devadattajñānaṃ prati hetutvaṃ prasaktam / tatprasaktāvanekadvīpadeśāntaritapuruṣānubhūtārthānusmaraṇaṃ syāt / tathā svajanabhujaṅgamādāv ananubhūte 'py arthe 'nusmaraṇaṃ syāt / tathā
tathāgatāvadātajñānajanyatve devadattādijñānānām avadātatā syāt /
tataś ca sarve sarvajñāḥ syuḥ / atha naivāvadātatā devadattādijñānānāṃ tathāgatāvadātajñānopādānajanyatve 'pi devadattādijñānenāpi janitatvāt, tajjanyatvenaivatathāgatajñānasyāpy avadātarūpatā na prāpnoti / tataś cāsāv apy avītarāgaḥ syād asarvajñaś ca /
body.translated_text: e.3 From this too the consciousness-continuum (<s>vijñānasantāna</s>) is untenable: because the producing consciousness has no difference in its own nature with respect to the cognition co-produced with the earlier and the later. Whatever is its own nature with respect to the cognition co-produced with the earlier is also its own nature with respect to the later cognition, since consciousness is without parts. Therefore, just as it is not the cause of the cognition co-produced with the earlier, so too it is not the cause of the later cognition, because no operative distinction apart from its own nature is apprehended. If it is said that mere temporal priority is the distinguishing factor by which its causality is established — if so, then just as <s>Devadatta</s>'s cognition that is temporally prior to <s>Devadatta</s>'s cognition is the cause of <s>Devadatta</s>'s cognition, so too the causality of all persons' cognitions that arose prior to <s>Devadatta</s>'s cognition with respect to <s>Devadatta</s>'s cognition would absurdly follow. From that consequence, one would remember objects experienced by persons separated by many continents and lands. Likewise, one would have recollection even of objects never experienced, such as one's own relatives, serpents, and so forth. Similarly, if the cognitions of <s>Devadatta</s> and the like are produced by the purified cognition of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, then <s>Devadatta</s>'s cognitions and the like would be purified. And thus everyone would be omniscient. If there is no purity in the cognitions of <s>Devadatta</s> and the like even though they are produced by the purified cognition of the <s>Tathāgata</s> as their material cause, because they are also produced by <s>Devadatta</s>'s cognition and the like, then by that same reasoning the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s cognition too would not attain purity. And thus he too would be one who has not overcome passion and would not be omniscient.

e.3 ito 'pi vijñānasantānānupapattis -- tadutpādakavijñānasya pūrvāparasahotpannavijñānaṃ prati svarūpāviśeṣāt / yad eva pūrvasahotpannavijñānāpekṣayā svarūpaṃ tad evāparavijñānāpekṣayāpi svarūpaṃ vijñānasya niravayavatvena / tataś ca yathā pūrvasahotpannavijñānasya hetur na bhavaty, evam aparavijñānasyāpi hetur na bhavati tatsvarūpavyatiriktavyāpārātiśayasyānupalabdheḥ / atha pūrvakālabhāva evātiśayas tena tasya hetutvam upapādyate / yady evaṃ yathā devadattajñānapūrvakālabhāvi devadattajñānaṃ devadattajñānakāraṇaṃ, tathā sarvapuruṣajñānānāṃ devadattajñānapūrvakālotpannānāṃ devadattajñānaṃ prati hetutvaṃ prasaktam / tatprasaktāvanekadvīpadeśāntaritapuruṣānubhūtārthānusmaraṇaṃ syāt / tathā svajanabhujaṅgamādāv ananubhūte 'py arthe 'nusmaraṇaṃ syāt / tathā
tathāgatāvadātajñānajanyatve devadattādijñānānām avadātatā syāt /
tataś ca sarve sarvajñāḥ syuḥ / atha naivāvadātatā devadattādijñānānāṃ tathāgatāvadātajñānopādānajanyatve 'pi devadattādijñānenāpi janitatvāt, tajjanyatvenaivatathāgatajñānasyāpy avadātarūpatā na prāpnoti / tataś cāsāv apy avītarāgaḥ syād asarvajñaś ca /

e.4 itaś ca santānānupapattir vijñānayoḥ sahotpāde hetuphalabhāvānupapatteḥ / yadaiva kāraṇajñānaṃ vinaśyati, tadaiva kāryajñānaṃ jāyateti vaḥ siddhāntaḥ / kāraṇajñānasya ca vināśas tadutpādaiva / tataś ca kāraṇajñānavināśakāle kāryajñānaṃ bhavati kim uktaṃ bhavati? kāraṇajñānotpādakālaiva bhavati / tataś ca sahotpannayor hetuphalabhāvānupapattir ekakālodgatayor goviṣāṇayor iva / kāraṇajñānasya cānutpannasyotpattivad anutpannasya vināśaprasaṅgaḥ / tataś ca kṣaṇam api nopalabhyeta / upalabdhau vā satatopalambhaprasaṅgas tadātmabhūtavināśasyopalambhavighātākartṛtvāt / vighātakartṛtve vaikakṣaṇopalambhasyāpy anupapattiprasaṅgaḥ / athaikakṣaṇopalabhyasvabhāvakaṃ sañjātaṃ tena na satatopalabdhir anupalabdhir vā / yady evaṃ dvādaśāṣṭakṣaṇopalabhyasvabhāvakaṃ
sañjātaṃ kiṃ na kalpyate? kiṃ cotpādavināśayor abhede sati kāryakāraṇayoḥ samaṃ vināśaḥ
syāt /
body.translated_text: e.4 The consciousness-continuum is also untenable for this reason: when two cognitions arise simultaneously, the cause-effect relation is untenable. Your established doctrine is that the effect-cognition arises at the very moment the cause-cognition perishes. And the destruction of the cause-cognition is its very arising. Therefore, when the effect-cognition exists at the time of the destruction of the cause-cognition — what has been said? — it exists at the very time of the arising of the cause-cognition. And thus, for two things arising simultaneously, the cause-effect relation is untenable, just as with the two horns of a cow arising at the same time. And just as the cause-cognition, being unarisen, has an arising, so too the consequence follows that the unarisen undergoes destruction. And thus it would not be apprehended even for a single moment. Or if it is apprehended, the consequence of perpetual apprehension follows, because the destruction that is identical with its nature cannot obstruct apprehension. If it does obstruct, then the consequence follows that even single-moment apprehension is untenable. If it is said that it arises having the nature of being apprehensible for a single moment, and therefore there is neither perpetual apprehension nor non-apprehension — if so, why not conceive of it as arising having the nature of being apprehensible for twelve or eight moments? And when arising and destruction are not different, the destruction of the cause and effect would be simultaneous.

e.5 yad apy anyad uktaṃ  mātur udaraniṣkramaṇānantaraṃ yad ādyaṃ jñānaṃ taj jñānāntarapūrvakaṃ jñānatvād dvitīyajñānavat / nāsiddhatvād dṛṣṭāntasya / dvitīyādijñānasyāpi yathā jñānapūrvakatvaṃ nāvagāhayituṃ pāryate, tathā prāg evāveditam / kiṃ ca yadi jñānatvāj jñānapūrvakatvānumānaṃ, na kilāvabodhātmakakāraṇam antareṇa bodhātmakaṃ kāryam upapadyate / etac cāvadyam / abodhātmakād api nīlālokalocanādikāraṇād upajāyate / tathā garbhādau yad ādyaṃ vijñānaṃ, tad bhūtasaṅghātād eva bhaviṣYati, na jñānāntaraṃ parikalpanīyam / yasyānantaraṃ yad bhavati, tat tasya kāraṇaṃ, nāparidṛṣṭasāmarthyam / vijñānābhāve vijñānajanyākāratā nivṛttā, na tu jñānākāratā / yathendriyavyāpāram antareṇopajāyamāne manovijñānendriyajanyākāratā
nivartate, na tu jñānākāratā / yadi ca sadṛśāt sadṛśasyotpattir niyamyate, tadā dhūmena
dahanānumānaṃ na prāpnoti, dahanasya dhūmasārūpyam antareṇopādānakāraṇatvāyogāt / atha rūparūpatā sārūpyam ubhayor iti cet, tad ihāpi svalakṣaṇarūpatā sārūpyaṃ bhūtavijñānayor, alaṃ paralokavijñānakalpanayā / atha vijñānarūpatā bhūtānāṃ na vidyate tena teṣām upādānakāraṇatvaṃ nāsti vijñānaṃ pratīti ced, ihāpi dhūmarūpatā nāsti dahanasya, nopādānakāraṇatvam / tadabhāve na dahanānumānam / tathānubhavajñānād anubhavajñānasyaiva niṣpattir abhyupeyopādānakāraṇānukāritvena kāryasya niṣpattyabhyupagamāt / na caikadeśānukāritvam asti tadbījasyāvicitratvāt / anubhavākārānanukār.itve ca jñānākāratāvirahaḥ syāt / anukaroti ca vijñānarūpatāṃ tena kathaṃ nānubhavātmakam? tadupapattau ca prāptānubhavaparamparety alaḥ smaraṇānupapattiḥ / tadanupapattau
cānumānajñānasyāpy anupapattiḥ / tataś ca sarvavyavahāravilopaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: e.5 As for what else was said — 'the first cognition immediately after emerging from the mother's womb must be preceded by another cognition, because it is a cognition, just like the second cognition' — this is not established because the example is unproven. That the second cognition and so forth are preceded by cognition also cannot be ascertained — as was explained before. Moreover, if precedence by cognition is inferred from being a cognition, the claim is that without a cause of the nature of awareness, an effect of the nature of awareness is not possible. This is faulty. For awareness arises even from causes not of the nature of awareness, such as blue, light, the eye, and the like. Similarly, the first consciousness in the embryo and so forth will arise from the aggregate of material elements alone — there is no need to postulate another cognition. Whatever immediately follows something is its cause, not something whose capacity is unobserved. In the absence of consciousness, the character of being produced by consciousness ceases, but not the character of being cognition — just as when mental cognition arises without the operation of the sense organ, the character of being produced by the sense organ ceases, but not the character of being cognition. And if it is insisted that the similar is produced only from the similar, then inference of fire from smoke would be impossible, because without resemblance to smoke, fire cannot be a material cause. If it is said that the resemblance of both consists in having the nature of form — then here too the resemblance of material elements and consciousness consists in having the nature of a particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>); enough with postulating consciousness from a previous life. If it is said that material elements do not possess the nature of consciousness, and therefore they cannot be the material cause of consciousness — here too, fire does not possess the nature of smoke, so it cannot be the material cause. In its absence, there is no inference of fire. Similarly, from experiential cognition only experiential cognition should arise, because you accept that an effect arises conforming to its material cause. And there is no partial conformity, because the seed is undifferentiated. And if it does not conform to the experiential character, then the character of being cognition would be lost. But it does conform to the consciousness-nature — so how is it not experiential in nature? And if that is established, then the experiential series is obtained — enough with the impossibility of memory. And if that is not established, then even inferential cognition is untenable. And thus the consequence of the collapse of all practical activity follows.
