body.text: (4.) evaṃ ca na santānasiddhir, nāpi savikalpakanirvikalpakajñānadvairāśyam asti, nāpi vyabhicārāvyabhicāradvaividhyam upapadyate saugate mate /
body.translated_text: (4.) Thus neither is the consciousness-continuum established, nor does the duality of <s>savikalpaka</s> (conceptual) and <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual) cognition exist, nor is the distinction between erring and non-erring tenable in the <s>Saugata</s> (Buddhist) position.

children.text: (4.) evaṃ ca na santānasiddhir, nāpi savikalpakanirvikalpakajñānadvairāśyam asti, nāpi vyabhicārāvyabhicāradvaividhyam upapadyate saugate mate /

body.text: Chapter 5: Examination of Mīmāṃsāsūtra 1.1.4
5. tathā satsamprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tat pratyakṣaṃ tad api pratyuktam / katham? etat sūtraṃ kadācil lakṣaṇaparaṃ kadācic ca kārakasaṅkhyāpratipādanaparaṃ kadācic cānuvādaparam /
body.translated_text: 5. Similarly, 'perception is the cognition born from the contact of the sense organs of the <s>puruṣa</s> (person) with the existent' — that too has been refuted. How? This <s>sūtra</s> is sometimes intended as a definition, sometimes intended to enumerate causal factors, and sometimes intended as a restatement.

children.text: 5. tathā satsamprayoge puruṣasyendriyāṇāṃ buddhijanma tat pratyakṣaṃ tad api pratyuktam / katham? etat sūtraṃ kadācil lakṣaṇaparaṃ kadācic ca kārakasaṅkhyāpratipādanaparaṃ kadācic cānuvādaparam /

body.text: 5.1(1) tad yadi lakṣaṇaparaṃ, tadāvabodhasyāvyabhicāritvaṃ nāvagantuṃ pāryate  nāduṣṭakāraṇajanyatvena nāpi pravṛttisāmarthyena nāpi bādhārahitatvena nānyathā vā / sarvaṃ pūrvoditam anusmṛtya vaktavyam /
body.translated_text: 5.1(1) If it is intended as a definition, then the non-deceptiveness of awareness cannot be ascertained — neither by virtue of being produced by non-defective causes, nor by virtue of capacity for prompting activity, nor by virtue of being free from sublation, nor in any other way. All this should be stated by recalling what was said earlier.

children.text: 5.1(1) tad yadi lakṣaṇaparaṃ, tadāvabodhasyāvyabhicāritvaṃ nāvagantuṃ pāryate -- nāduṣṭakāraṇajanyatvena nāpi pravṛttisāmarthyena nāpi bādhārahitatvena nānyathā vā / sarvaṃ pūrvoditam anusmṛtya vaktavyam /

body.text: 5.12 nāpīndriyārthasamprayogajatvaṃ vijñānasyāvabodhasya cārvāgbhāgavidāvagamyate tadatīndriyatvena tadāyat tatānaḍhigateḥ / nāpīndriyajanyatvam avagantuṃ pāryatendriyāṇām atīndriyatvād eva / athāvabodhānyathānupapattyā sannikarṣaparikalpanā kriyate / avabodhasyānyathānupapattir na bhavati / kānumā?
body.translated_text: 5.12 Nor can the origin of cognition or awareness from sense-organ-object contact be ascertained by one who knows only the external aspect, because the sense organs are beyond the senses and dependence upon them is not ascertained. Nor can the origin from the sense organs be ascertained, precisely because the sense organs are beyond the senses. If it is said that the postulation of contact is made because awareness is otherwise inexplicable — the otherwise-inexplicability of awareness does not hold. What inference is there?

children.text: 5.12 nāpīndriyārthasamprayogajatvaṃ vijñānasyāvabodhasya cārvāgbhāgavidāvagamyate tadatīndriyatvena tadāyat tatānaḍhigateḥ / nāpīndriyajanyatvam avagantuṃ pāryata indriyāṇām atīndriyatvād eva / athāvabodhānyathānupapattyā sannikarṣaparikalpanā kriyate / avabodhasyānyathānupapattir na bhavati / kānumā?

body.text: 5.2 atha kārakasaṅkhyārthaṃ, kiṃ tena parisaṅkhyānena prayojanam? ālokādīnām api kārakatvāt tāny api parisaṅkhyeyāni bhavanti /
body.translated_text: 5.2 If the <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of enumerating causal factors — what is accomplished by such enumeration? Since light and the like are also causal factors, they too should be enumerated.

children.text: 5.2 atha kārakasaṅkhyārthaṃ, kiṃ tena parisaṅkhyānena prayojanam? ālokādīnām api kārakatvāt tāny api parisaṅkhyeyāni bhavanti /

body.text: 5.3 athānuvādaparatā, prasiddhasyānuvādo nāprasiddhasya / na cādhyakṣaṃ kvacid viditam / nanu lake viditam / na viditam iti brūmo 'vyabhicāritayānavagateḥ / nāpi satsamprayogajatvaṃ viditam / tataś ca pratyakṣānadhigatiḥ / tadanavagatau cānuvādānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: 5.3 If it is a restatement, it is a restatement of what is well-known, not of what is unknown. But perception (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) has never been ascertained anywhere. Objection: It is known in the world. We say it is not known, because its non-deceptiveness has not been ascertained. Nor has its origin from sense-object contact been ascertained. Therefore, perception has not been ascertained. And when it has not been ascertained, restatement is impossible.

children.text: 5.3 athānuvādaparatā, prasiddhasyānuvādo nāprasiddhasya / na cādhyakṣaṃ kvacid viditam / nanu lake viditam / na viditam iti brūmo 'vyabhicāritayānavagateḥ / nāpi satsamprayogajatvaṃ viditam / tataś ca pratyakṣānadhigatiḥ / tadanavagatau cānuvādānupapattiḥ /

body.text: 5.3eto 'py anuvādānupapattiḥ prayojanābhāvāt / na hi prayojanaṃ vinānuvādaḥ pravartata, 'nūdya kvacit kiñcid vidhīyate pratiṣidhyate vā / nanv atrāpi dharmaṃ prati nimittatvaṃ pratiṣidhyate / tad uktaṃ dharmaṃ praty animittaṃ pratyakṣaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt samprayogajatvāc ca /
body.translated_text: 5.3e The restatement is impossible for yet another reason: the absence of purpose. For without a purpose, no restatement proceeds. 'Having restated something, something is prescribed or prohibited somewhere.' Objection: Here too, causality with respect to <s>dharma</s> is being prohibited. As stated: 'Perception is not a cause of <s>dharma</s>, because it apprehends what exists and because it arises from contact.'

children.text: 5.3a ito 'py anuvādānupapattiḥ prayojanābhāvāt / na hi prayojanaṃ vinānuvādaḥ pravartata, 'nūdya kvacit kiñcid vidhīyate pratiṣidhyate vā / nanv atrāpi dharmaṃ prati nimittatvaṃ pratiṣidhyate / tad uktaṃ -dharmaṃ praty animittaṃ pratyakṣaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt samprayogajatvāc ca /

body.text: tatra kim anyapadārthāvabhāsotpannaṃ pratyakṣaṃ dharmaṃ prati nimittatvena pratiṣidhyate kiṃ vā dharmāvabhāsotpannam anutpannaṃ vā? tad yady anyapadārthāvabhāsotpannapratyakṣavyāvṛttiḥ kriyate, tadāvipratipattyā sambodhayitavyā jaḍamatayaḥ /
body.translated_text: In this regard, is the perception that arises with the appearance of another object being excluded from being a cause of <s>dharma</s>, or is the perception that arises with the appearance of <s>dharma</s>, or one that has not arisen at all?

children.text: tatra kim anyapadārthāvabhāsotpannaṃ pratyakṣaṃ dharmaṃ prati nimittatvena pratiṣidhyate kiṃ vā dharmāvabhāsotpannam anutpannaṃ vā? tad yady anyapadārthāvabhāsotpannapratyakṣavyāvṛttiḥ kriyate, tadāvipratipattyā sambodhayitavyā jaḍamatayaḥ /

body.text: atha dharmāvabodhakotpannapratyakṣavyāvṛttiḥ kriyate, tadā virodhena pratyavastheyo bhavati / dharmāvabodhakotpannaṃ pratyakṣaṃ na ca dharmanimittam iti vyāhatam apadiśyate / anyathā cadanāvacanajanitavijñānasyāpi dharmāvabodhakatvenatpannasyātannimittatvaṃ syāt / athānutpannasya dharmāvabodhakatvaṃ nāsti, kenātra pratipadyate yan notpannaṃ tad dharmāvabodhakam ? nāpi kamaladalāvabodhakaṃ svayam asattvāt /
body.translated_text: If the exclusion is of perception that arises with the appearance of another object, then the dull-minded should be enlightened without contention.

children.text: atha dharmāvabodhakotpannapratyakṣavyāvṛttiḥ kriyate, tadā virodhena pratyavastheyo bhavati / dharmāvabodhakotpannaṃ pratyakṣaṃ na ca dharmanimittam iti vyāhatam apadiśyate / anyathā cadanāvacanajanitavijñānasyāpi dharmāvabodhakatvenatpannasyātannimittatvaṃ syāt / athānutpannasya dharmāvabodhakatvaṃ nāsti, kenātra pratipadyate yan notpannaṃ tad dharmāvabodhakam ? nāpi kamaladalāvabodhakaṃ svayam asattvāt /

body.text: yad apy uktaṃ satsamprayogajatvād iti, tad apy ayuktam / satsamprayogajatvaṃ yathā na bhavati tathā prāg evoktam /
body.translated_text: If the exclusion is of perception that arises as an illumination of <s>dharma</s>, then one must respond with a contradiction. To say 'perception arisen as an illumination of <s>dharma</s> is not a cause of <s>dharma</s>' is contradictory. Otherwise, even cognition produced by verbal utterance, having arisen as an illumination of <s>dharma</s>, would not be a cause of <s>dharma</s>. If it is said that what has not arisen has no illumination of <s>dharma</s> — by what does one ascertain here that what has not arisen does not illumine <s>dharma</s>? Nor does it illumine a lotus petal, since it itself does not exist.

children.text: yad apy uktaṃ satsamprayogajatvād iti, tad apy ayuktam / satsamprayogajatvaṃ yathā na bhavati tathā prāg evoktam /

body.text:
5.3b yad apy anyad uktaṃ vidyamānopalambhanatvāt kila pratyakṣaṃ vijñānaṃ vidyamānam avabodhayati / yady evaṃ na kevalaṃ pratyakṣam, api tu sarvapramāṇotpāditaṃ vijñānaṃ vidyamānāvabodhakam /
atha cadanājanitaṃ vijñānam avidyamānakartavyārthāvabodhakam /
body.translated_text:
[5.3b] As for the further statement that 'because it apprehends what exists, perception cognizes what exists' — if so, not only perception, but cognition produced by all means of valid knowledge apprehends what exists.
Now if cognition produced by Vedic injunction (<s>codanā</s>) apprehends an object to be done that is non-existent —

children.text:
5.3b yad apy anyad uktaṃ -vidyamānopalambhanatvāt kila pratyakṣaṃ vijñānaṃ vidyamānam avabodhayati / yady evaṃ na kevalaṃ pratyakṣam, api tu sarvapramāṇotpāditaṃ vijñānaṃ vidyamānāvabodhakam /
atha cadanājanitaṃ vijñānam avidyamānakartavyārthāvabodhakam /

body.text: yady avidyamānaṃ, katham avabodhyate? athāvabodhyate, katham avidyamānatā? avabodhyamānatvenaiva vidyamānatā pratyakṣapramāṇāvabodhitārthavad iti nāpy avabodhanam avabodhyam antareṇopajāyate pratyakṣāvabodhanavat / api ca codanāvacanajanitavijñānasya mithyātvam upapadyate 'vidyamānaviṣayatvāt keśoṇḍukajñānavat / keśoṇḍukavijñānasyāpi pratīyamānopakārakārthābhāve mithyātvam / tad ihāpi pratīyamānopakārakārtho nāsty eva, kathaṃ na mithyātvam? tadanvaye vā kartavyārthaviṣayatvaṃ pratihīyeta codanāvacasaḥ /
body.translated_text: if it is non-existent, how is it apprehended? If it is apprehended, how is it non-existent? By the very fact of being apprehended, its existence is established, just like an object apprehended by the means of valid knowledge of perception. And apprehension does not arise without something to be apprehended, just like perceptual apprehension. Moreover, the erroneousness of cognition produced by Vedic utterance (<s>codanā</s>) is established, because it has a non-existent object, just like the cognition of hair-nets. Even the cognition of hair-nets is erroneous because of the absence of a beneficial object corresponding to what appears. Here too, there is no beneficial object corresponding to what appears — how then is it not erroneous? Or if its [erroneousness] is accepted, the status of having an object to be done would be undermined for the Vedic utterance.

children.text: yady avidyamānaṃ, katham avabodhyate? athāvabodhyate, katham avidyamānatā? avabodhyamānatvenaiva vidyamānatā pratyakṣapramāṇāvabodhitārthavad iti nāpy avabodhanam avabodhyam antareṇopajāyate pratyakṣāvabodhanavat / api ca codanāvacanajanitavijñānasya mithyātvam upapadyate 'vidyamānaviṣayatvāt keśoṇḍukajñānavat / keśoṇḍukavijñānasyāpi pratīyamānopakārakārthābhāve mithyātvam / tad ihāpi pratīyamānopakārakārtho nāsty eva, kathaṃ na mithyātvam? tadanvaye vā kartavyārthaviṣayatvaṃ pratihīyeta codanāvacasaḥ /

body.text: kiṃ ca codanājanitaṃ vijñānaṃ kartavyatārthaviṣayaṃ vā tadabhāvaviṣayaṃ nirviṣayaṃ vā / tad yadi kartavyatārthaviṣayaṃ, tadā tasya vartamānataiva pratītyutkalitatvād vidyamānatoyādivat / toyāder apratīyamānatvaṃ svasattādhūmād agnau sati janakatvādinā nimittena / etac ced vidyate, katham avidyamānatā?
body.translated_text: Furthermore, cognition produced by Vedic injunction either has an object to be done as its object, or the absence thereof as its object, or is objectless. If it has an object to be done as its object, then that object's present existence is established, because it is manifested through experience, just like existing water and the like. The non-experience of water and the like [in certain cases] is due to some cause such as productivity, when fire exists [but is inferred] from the smoke that is its own existence. If this [object to be done] exists, how is it non-existent?

children.text: kiṃ ca codanājanitaṃ vijñānaṃ kartavyatārthaviṣayaṃ vā tadabhāvaviṣayaṃ nirviṣayaṃ vā / tad yadi kartavyatārthaviṣayaṃ, tadā tasya vartamānataiva pratītyutkalitatvād vidyamānatoyādivat / toyāder apratīyamānatvaṃ svasattādhūmād agnau sati janakatvādinā nimittena / etac ced vidyate, katham avidyamānatā?

body.text: atha tadabhāvaviṣayaṃ, tasyāpi svena rūpeṇa vidyamānatvān na kartavyatā /
body.translated_text: If it has the absence thereof as its object, even that [absence] exists in its own form — and therefore there is no obligation to act.

children.text: atha tadabhāvaviṣayaṃ, tasyāpi svena rūpeṇa vidyamānatvān na kartavyatā /

body.text: atha nirviṣayaṃ, na tarhi codanā kartavyāvabodhikā, api tu nirviṣayety evaṃ vaktavyam / evaṃ sthite yathā pratyakṣaṃ vidyamānopalambhakaṃ tathānyāny api pramāṇāni /
body.translated_text: If it is objectless, then the Vedic injunction should not be said to be a revealer of duty to be done, but rather should be said to be objectless. This being established, just as perception apprehends what exists, so too do the other means of valid knowledge.

children.text: atha nirviṣayaṃ, na tarhi codanā kartavyāvabodhikā, api tu nirviṣayety evaṃ vaktavyam / evaṃ sthite yathā pratyakṣaṃ vidyamānopalambhakaṃ tathānyāny api pramāṇāni /

body.text: 5.a buddhijanma pratyakṣaṃ, na ca buddhyavagame pramāṇam asti / pratyakṣāvaseyā sā na bhavati svayam anabhyupagamāt / anumānagamyāpi na bhavati tayā pratibaddhaliṅgānavagateḥ / athārthāpattyā pratīyate, kiṃ ghaṭārthānyathānupapattyāho tadupādānaparityāgānyathānupapattyā ghaṭāvabodhānyathānupapattyā vā?
body.translated_text: [5.a] The arising of cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), yet there is no means of valid knowledge for ascertaining cognition. It is not ascertained by perception itself, because it is not accepted [as self-revealing]. Nor is it ascertained by inference, because the inferential mark connected with it is not known. Now if it is known by <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — is it by the otherwise-inexplicability of the pot-object, or by the otherwise-inexplicability of the non-abandonment of its material cause, or by the otherwise-inexplicability of the apprehension of the pot?

children.text: 5.a buddhijanma pratyakṣaṃ, na ca buddhyavagame pramāṇam asti / pratyakṣāvaseyā sā na bhavati svayam anabhyupagamāt / anumānagamyāpi na bhavati tayā pratibaddhaliṅgānavagateḥ / athārthāpattyā pratīyate, kiṃ ghaṭārthānyathānupapattyāho tadupādānaparityāgānyathānupapattyā ghaṭāvabodhānyathānupapattyā vā?

body.text: tad yadi ghaṭārthānyathānupapattyā, tad ayuktam / na buddhikāryo ghaṭo, 'pi tu buddhir iha tatkāryā /
body.translated_text: If by the otherwise-inexplicability of the pot-object, that is not justified. The pot is not an effect of cognition; rather, cognition here is an effect of that [pot].

children.text: tad yadi ghaṭārthānyathānupapattyā, tad ayuktam / na buddhikāryo ghaṭo, 'pi tu buddhir iha tatkāryā /

body.text: atha ghaṭopādānaparityāgānyathānupapattyā buddhiparikalpanā kriyate, tad ayuktaṃ, buddhisvarūpasyānekakālāntarāvasthānāyogād arthāpatter nirviṣayatvam / kenāpi balavatā prerito buddhim antareṇa vā tadupaplavād vā ghaṭopādānaparityāgāya ghaṭate tena sandigdhārthāpattiḥ / na ca sambandhagrahaṇam antareṇa niyatāyāṃ buddhau pratipattir upapadyate / arthāpattitas tu tadanupapattāv indriyakalpanāpi durghaṭā / athāvabodhānyathānupapattyā buddhiparikalpanā kriyate, tasyāpi buddhyā saha sambandho nāsti, katham avabodhayati? avabodhe cāvagate pratyakṣāvagataiva buddhir nāvabodhagamyā / avabodhabuddhivijñānaśabdānāṃ paryāyatvād avabudhyate jñāyatety eko 'rthaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the postulation of cognition is made by the otherwise-inexplicability of the non-abandonment of the pot's material cause, that is not justified — because the nature of cognition cannot persist across many different times, hence the presumption has no object. Someone impelled by a powerful force, or due to the disruption of cognition, can manage to abandon the pot's material cause — therefore the presumption is doubtful. Nor is the determination of a specific cognition established without the grasping of a relation. And by <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), when that is not established, even the postulation of sense organs is difficult. If the postulation of cognition is made by the otherwise-inexplicability of apprehension — even that [apprehension] has no relation with cognition; how does it make one apprehend? And when apprehension is known, cognition is just what is ascertained by perception — it is not known through apprehension. For the words apprehension (<s>avabodha</s>), cognition (<s>buddhi</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) are synonymous — 'one apprehends' and 'one knows' have the same meaning.

children.text: atha ghaṭopādānaparityāgānyathānupapattyā buddhiparikalpanā kriyate, tad ayuktaṃ, buddhisvarūpasyānekakālāntarāvasthānāyogād arthāpatter nirviṣayatvam / kenāpi balavatā prerito buddhim antareṇa vā tadupaplavād vā ghaṭopādānaparityāgāya ghaṭate tena sandigdhārthāpattiḥ / na ca sambandhagrahaṇam antareṇa niyatāyāṃ buddhau pratipattir upapadyate / arthāpattitas tu tadanupapattāv indriyakalpanāpi durghaṭā / athāvabodhānyathānupapattyā buddhiparikalpanā kriyate, tasyāpi buddhyā saha sambandho nāsti, katham avabodhayati? avabodhe cāvagate pratyakṣāvagataiva buddhir nāvabodhagamyā / avabodhabuddhivijñānaśabdānāṃ paryāyatvād avabudhyate jñāyata ity eko 'rthaḥ /

body.text: 6. tathā śrotrādivṛttir avikalpikā, etad api pratyuktam /
body.translated_text: [6.] Similarly, 'the functioning of the ear and other sense organs is non-conceptual' — this too has been refuted.

children.text: 6. tathā śrotrādivṛttir avikalpikā, etad api pratyuktam /

body.text: 6.1 śrotrādikaraṇānāṃ śabdādiviṣayākāratayā vipariṇāmo vṛttiśabdenābhidhīyate / sā cānekaprakārā bhavati samyagjñānarūpā viparyayajñānasandeharūpā ca / tad uktaṃ tamo moho mahāmohas tāmisro 'ndhatāmisretyādi /
body.translated_text: [6.1] The transformation of the instruments such as the ear and others into the form of objects such as sound and the like is designated by the word 'functioning' (<s>vṛtti</s>). And that is of many kinds — having the form of valid cognition, erroneous cognition, and doubt. As stated: '<s>tamas</s> (darkness), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom), <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness)' — and so forth.

children.text: 6.1 śrotrādikaraṇānāṃ śabdādiviṣayākāratayā vipariṇāmo vṛttiśabdenābhidhīyate / sā cānekaprakārā bhavati -samyagjñānarūpā viparyayajñānasandeharūpā ca / tad uktaṃ -tamo moho mahāmohas tāmisro 'ndhatāmisra ityādi /

body.text: 6.11 tad yadi śrotrādivṛtteḥ pratyakṣatvaṃ, tadā viparyayādivṛtter api pratyakṣatvaṃ prāpnoti / athābādhitapadopādānaṃ kriyate / tat sūtre na śrūyate / bhavatu vā tasya kalpanā, tathāpy avyabhicāritvaṃ jñātuṃ na śakyate / tac ca naiyāyikapratyakṣalakṣaṇādhikāre prapañcitam / yadi cāvyabhicāripadena viparyayarūpā vṛttir apodyate, tat tadātmatayā vyavasthitā samyagrūpāpi vṛttir apoditā bhavati / tataś ca saṅgrāhyā na labhyate vṛttiḥ /
body.translated_text: [6.11] If the functioning of the ear and other sense organs is perception, then the functioning in the form of error and the like would also be perception. Now if the qualification 'unsublated' (<s>abādhita</s>) is adopted — that is not heard in the <s>sūtra</s>. Even if its postulation is allowed, the non-erringness cannot be ascertained. And that has been elaborated in the section on the <s>Naiyāyika</s> (logician's) definition of perception. And if through the qualification 'non-erring' the functioning in the form of error is excluded, then the functioning in the form of valid cognition too, being established as identical in nature with it, would be excluded. And therefore no functioning is obtained that can be included [in the definition].

children.text: 6.11 tad yadi śrotrādivṛtteḥ pratyakṣatvaṃ, tadā viparyayādivṛtter api pratyakṣatvaṃ prāpnoti / athābādhitapadopādānaṃ kriyate / tat sūtre na śrūyate / bhavatu vā tasya kalpanā, tathāpy avyabhicāritvaṃ jñātuṃ na śakyate / tac ca naiyāyikapratyakṣalakṣaṇādhikāre prapañcitam / yadi cāvyabhicāripadena viparyayarūpā vṛttir apodyate, tat tadātmatayā vyavasthitā samyagrūpāpi vṛttir apoditā bhavati / tataś ca saṅgrāhyā na labhyate vṛttiḥ /

body.text: atha samyagrūpā vṛttir iha saṅgrāhyā, tadāpohyā nalabhyate vṛttīnāṃ svarūpaikatābhyupagamāt / bhedābhyupagame vābhyupetahānam / na hi bhavatāṃ pakṣendriyād bhidyante vṛttayas, tac ced abhinnaṃ, kathaṃ vṛttīnāṃ bhedaḥ? bhedābhyupagamendriyaikatvaṃ hīyate / indriyāvyatirekitvaṃ vā na vaktavyam /
body.translated_text: Now if the functioning in the form of valid cognition is what is to be included here, then no functioning to be excluded is obtained, because all functionings are accepted as having a single nature. Or if difference is accepted, there would be an abandonment of one's own position. For in your position, the functionings are not different from the sense organ — and if that [sense organ] is undifferentiated, how can there be difference among the functionings? If difference is accepted, the unitariness of the sense organ is undermined. Or the non-difference [of functionings] from the sense organ should not be stated.

children.text: atha samyagrūpā vṛttir iha saṅgrāhyā, tadāpohyā nalabhyate vṛttīnāṃ svarūpaikatābhyupagamāt / bhedābhyupagame vābhyupetahānam / na hi bhavatāṃ pakṣa indriyād bhidyante vṛttayas, tac ced abhinnaṃ, kathaṃ vṛttīnāṃ bhedaḥ? bhedābhyupagama indriyaikatvaṃ hīyate / indriyāvyatirekitvaṃ vā na vaktavyam /

body.text: 6.1endriyāvyatirekitve 'bhyupagamyamāne nīlalohitaghaṭādīnāṃ sarvadopalambhaḥ syād, indriyāvasthāne tadavyatiriktāyā vṛtter avasthānasambhavāt / tatsambhave ca ghaṭādyanupalambhānupapattiḥ / atha vṛttisadbhāve 'py anupalabdhir, na kadācid upalabdhiḥ syāt / na hi bhavatāṃ pakṣe kiñcid apūrvaṃ jāyate pūrvaṃ vā nirudhyate / tataś ca sarvasyāstitvopalabdhyanupalabdhī kiṅkṛte? sadopalabdhir anupalabdhir vā / na hy evaṃvādino dvitīyā gatir asti /
body.translated_text: [6.1] When non-difference from the sense organ is accepted, there would be constant apprehension of blue, red, pot, and the like, because when the sense organ persists, the persistence of the functioning that is non-different from it is possible. And when its persistence is possible, the non-apprehension of pot and the like would be impossible. Now if there is non-apprehension even when the functioning exists — then there would never be apprehension. For in your position, nothing new arises and nothing previously existing ceases. And therefore, the existence of everything being constant, what causes apprehension and non-apprehension? There is either constant apprehension or constant non-apprehension. For one who holds this view, there is no second alternative.

children.text: 6.1a indriyāvyatirekitve 'bhyupagamyamāne nīlalohitaghaṭādīnāṃ sarvadopalambhaḥ syād, indriyāvasthāne tadavyatiriktāyā vṛtter avasthānasambhavāt / tatsambhave ca ghaṭādyanupalambhānupapattiḥ / atha vṛttisadbhāve 'py anupalabdhir, na kadācid upalabdhiḥ syāt / na hi bhavatāṃ pakṣe kiñcid apūrvaṃ jāyate pūrvaṃ vā nirudhyate / tataś ca sarvasyāstitva upalabdhyanupalabdhī kiṅkṛte? sadopalabdhir anupalabdhir vā / na hy evaṃvādino dvitīyā gatir asti /

body.text: 6.1b kiṃ ca śabdādayopalabhyante kim anupalabhyasvabhāvopalabhyantāhosvid upalabhyasvabhāvāh?
body.translated_text: [6.1b] Furthermore, are sound and the like apprehended — are they apprehended as having a nature that is non-apprehensible, or as having a nature that is apprehensible?

children.text: 6.1b kiṃ ca śabdādaya upalabhyante kim anupalabhyasvabhāva ūpalabhyantā ahosvid upalabhyasvabhāvāh?

body.text: tad yady anupalabhyasvabhāvopalabhyante, tadopalabdhiḥ katham?
body.translated_text: If they are apprehended as having a non-apprehensible nature, then how is there apprehension?

children.text: tad yady anupalabhyasvabhāva ūpalabhyante, tadopalabdhiḥ katham?

body.text: yady anupalabhyasvabhāvāḥ, katham upatabhyeran? anyathātmāder apy upalabdhiḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: If they have a non-apprehensible nature, how can they be apprehended? Otherwise, even the <s>ātman</s> (self) and the like would be apprehended.

children.text: yady anupalabhyasvabhāvāḥ, katham upatabhyeran? anyathātmāder apy upalabdhiḥ syāt /

body.text: athopalabhyasvabhāvopalabhyante, 'nupalabdhiḥ katham? kiṃ tenaivākāreṇāhosvid ākārāntareṇa?
body.translated_text: If they are apprehended as having an apprehensible nature — how then is there non-apprehension? Is it through that very same form, or through another form?

children.text: athopalabhyasvabhāva ūpalabhyante, 'nupalabdhiḥ katham? kiṃ tenaivākāreṇāhosvid ākārāntareṇa?

body.text: yadi tenaivākāreṇānupalabdhir, ātmāder apy anupalabdhir na prāpnoti / upalabdhau vā bījāntaraṃ vacanīyam /
body.translated_text: If non-apprehension is through that very same form, then even the <s>ātman</s> and the like should not fail to be apprehended. Or if there is apprehension [of the ātman], another reason must be stated [for its non-apprehension].

children.text: yadi tenaivākāreṇānupalabdhir, ātmāder apy anupalabdhir na prāpnoti / upalabdhau vā bījāntaraṃ vacanīyam /

body.text: athākārāntareṇa nopalabhyante, tathāpy upalabhyamānānupalabhyamānayor naikatvaṃ śabdātmākārayor iva / na hy upalabhyasvabhāvāc chabdād anupatabhyasvabhāvātmāvyatirikto dṛṣtaḥ / atha tasyaivābhivyaktasyopalabdhiḥ / tatsvarūpavad abhivyakteḥ sarvadāvasthānāt satatopalabdhiprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: If they are not apprehended through another form, even so there would be no unity between the apprehended and the non-apprehended, just as between sound and the <s>ātman</s>-form. For a sound that has an apprehensible nature is not observed to be non-different from the <s>ātman</s> that has a non-apprehensible nature. Now if the apprehension is of that very thing when it is manifested — because the manifestation, being of the same nature as the thing itself, always persists, the consequence of constant apprehension follows.

children.text: athākārāntareṇa nopalabhyante, tathāpy upalabhyamānānupalabhyamānayor naikatvaṃ śabdātmākārayor iva / na hy upalabhyasvabhāvāc chabdād anupatabhyasvabhāvā atmāvyatirikto dṛṣtaḥ / atha tasyaivābhivyaktasyopalabdhiḥ / tatsvarūpavad abhivyakteḥ sarvadāvasthānāt satatopalabdhiprasaṅgaḥ /

body.text: atha tirodhāne saty anupalabdhis, tadātatsvarūpatādātmyāt satatānupatambhaprasaṅgaḥ / ubhayor vāvasthāne samam upalambhānupalambhau syātām / tataś cedānīm upatabhe pūrvaṃ nopalabha iti vyavahāravirahaḥ syāt / tathā pūrvam upalabhedānīṃ nopalabhety etad api na prāpnoti / athāvayavopacaye saty upalambhaḥ / tasya sarvadā bhāvāt sarvadopalambhaprasaṅgaḥ / athasvalakṣaṇapuṣṭau satyām upalambhaḥ / tasyāḥ sarvadā sattvāt satatopalambhaprasaṅgaḥ / atha saṃsthānotkarṣe saty upalambhaḥ / tasyāpi sarvadā vidyamānatvāt satatopalabdhiḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: If non-apprehension occurs when there is concealment — then because the concealment too is identical in nature with the thing, the consequence of constant non-apprehension follows. Or if both [manifestation and concealment] persist, then apprehension and non-apprehension would occur simultaneously. And therefore the practical usage 'now I apprehend, previously I did not apprehend' would be impossible. Similarly, 'previously I apprehended, now I do not apprehend' — this too would not be possible. Now if apprehension occurs when there is an accumulation of parts — since that always exists, the consequence of constant apprehension follows. If apprehension occurs when the particular characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is nourished — since that always exists, the consequence of constant apprehension follows. If apprehension occurs when the configuration is enhanced — since that too always exists, there would be constant apprehension.

children.text: atha tirodhāne saty anupalabdhis, tadātatsvarūpatādātmyāt satatānupatambhaprasaṅgaḥ / ubhayor vāvasthāne samam upalambhānupalambhau syātām / tataś cedānīm upatabhe pūrvaṃ nopalabha3 iti vyavahāravirahaḥ syāt / tathā pūrvam upalabha idānīṃ nopalabha ity etad api na prāpnoti / athāvayavopacaye saty upalambhaḥ / tasya sarvadā bhāvāt sarvadopalambhaprasaṅgaḥ / athasvalakṣaṇapuṣṭau satyām upalambhaḥ / tasyāḥ sarvadā sattvāt satatopalambhaprasaṅgaḥ / atha saṃsthānotkarṣe saty upalambhaḥ / tasyāpi sarvadā vidyamānatvāt satatopalabdhiḥ syāt /

body.text: tasmād yena yena nimittenopalambhaparikalpanā, tasya tasya sarvadā bhāvāt satatopalambhaprasaṅgaḥ / atha deśakālakārakāpabandhād anupalambhas, tadā tasyāpabandhasya sarvadā bhāvād anupalambhānuparamaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: Therefore, whatever reason is postulated for apprehension, since that reason always exists, the consequence of constant apprehension follows. If non-apprehension is due to the restriction of place, time, and causal factors — then since that restriction also always exists, non-apprehension would never cease.

children.text: tasmād yena yena nimittenopalambhaparikalpanā, tasya tasya sarvadā bhāvāt satatopalambhaprasaṅgaḥ / atha deśakālakārakāpabandhād anupalambhas, tadā tasyāpabandhasya sarvadā bhāvād anupalambhānuparamaḥ syāt /

body.text: 6.2 tathendriyāṇām api karaṇarūpatā nopalabhyate phalavaikalyāt / nanv asti vijñānaṃ phalam / na tasya sarvadā vidyamānatvāt / sarvadā vidyamānayor hetuphalabhāvo nopapadyate, yathā guṇānāṃ parasparam ātmabhedānāṃ vā / na hy ātmātmāntarasya hetur bhavati tatphalaṃ vā, tathehāpyanādyantā sattā na phalaṃ hetur vocyate /
body.translated_text: [6.2] Similarly, the instrumentality (<s>karaṇarūpatā</s>) of the sense organs is also not apprehended, because the result is deficient. Objection: Cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) is the result. That is not so, because it always exists. When both [cause and result] always exist, the cause-effect relation is not established — just as among the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) with respect to each other, or among the <s>ātman</s> and its different [aspects]. For the <s>ātman</s> is not the cause of another <s>ātman</s>, nor its effect — similarly here too, the beginningless and endless existence is neither called an effect nor a cause.

children.text: 6.2 tathendriyāṇām api karaṇarūpatā nopalabhyate phalavaikalyāt / nanv asti vijñānaṃ phalam / na tasya sarvadā vidyamānatvāt / sarvadā vidyamānayor hetuphalabhāvo nopapadyate, yathā guṇānāṃ parasparam ātmabhedānāṃ vā / na hy ātmātmāntarasya hetur bhavati tatphalaṃ vā, tathehāpyanādyantā sattā na phalaṃ hetur vocyate /

body.text: f . kiṃ ca bhūjalādy anekaṃ kāryaṃ, tat kiṃ guṇatrayād vyatiriktam avyatiriktaṃ vā? tad yadi vyatiriktaṃ, tat kiṃ tāttvikam atāttvikaṃ vā?
body.translated_text: [f.] Furthermore, the multiple effects such as earth, water, and the like — are they different from the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) or not different? If different, are they real or unreal?

children.text: f . kiṃ ca bhūjalādy anekaṃ kāryaṃ, tat kiṃ guṇatrayād vyatiriktam avyatiriktaṃ vā? tad yadi vyatiriktaṃ, tat kiṃ tāttvikam atāttvikaṃ vā?

body.text: tad yadi tāttvikaṃ, na tarhi guṇatrayopādānapūrvakaṃ, tato bhinnatvād ātmasvarūpavat / na ca guṇatrayeṇa sahānyatamo 'pi sambandhopapadyate tadbhinnakāryasya / na mātrāmātrikasambandho nāpi sahacarasahacaritabhāvo nāpi nimittanaimittikabhāvopakāryopakārakabhāvo vā / athātāttvikaṃ, kathaṃ tena guṇatrayaṃ pratīyate guṇatrayeṇa saha sambandhānupapatteḥ? na ca sadasatoḥ sambandhopapadyatātmakharaviṣāṇayor iva / tadabhāvān nānumānād guṇatrayapratipattiḥ / nāpi pratyakṣeṇa guṇāvadhāraṇaṃ svayam anabhyupagamāt / tad uktaṃ
body.translated_text: If it is real, then it is not preceded by the material cause of the three <s>guṇas</s>, because it is different from them, just like the nature of the self. Nor can any relation whatsoever be established between the three <s>guṇas</s> and an effect that is different from them — neither the relation of measure and measured, nor the relation of concomitant and concomitance, nor the relation of instrumental cause and effect, nor that of benefited and benefactor. If it is non-real, how can the three <s>guṇas</s> be cognized through it, since a relation with the three <s>guṇas</s> is untenable? A relation between the existent and the non-existent is not tenable, just as between the self and a hare's horn. Due to its absence, the three <s>guṇas</s> cannot be known through inference. Nor can the <s>guṇas</s> be ascertained by perception, since you yourself do not accept that. As stated:

children.text: tad yadi tāttvikaṃ, na tarhi guṇatrayopādānapūrvakaṃ, tato bhinnatvād ātmasvarūpavat / na ca guṇatrayeṇa sahānyatamo 'pi sambandha upapadyate tadbhinnakāryasya / na mātrāmātrikasambandho nāpi sahacarasahacaritabhāvo nāpi nimittanaimittikabhāva upakāryopakārakabhāvo vā / athātāttvikaṃ, kathaṃ tena guṇatrayaṃ pratīyate guṇatrayeṇa saha sambandhānupapatteḥ? na ca sadasatoḥ sambandha upapadyatā atmakharaviṣāṇayor iva / tadabhāvān nānumānād guṇatrayapratipattiḥ / nāpi pratyakṣeṇa guṇāvadhāraṇaṃ svayam anabhyupagamāt / tad uktaṃ -

body.text: guṇānāṃ paramaṃ rūpaṃ na dṛṣṭipatham ṛcchati/ yat tu dṛṣṭipathaprāptaṃ tan māyeva sutucchakam//
body.translated_text: The supreme form of the <s>guṇas</s> does not come within the range of sight; what comes within the range of sight is as trivial as <s>māyā</s> (illusion).

children.text: guṇānāṃ paramaṃ rūpaṃ na dṛṣṭipatham ṛcchati/ yat tu dṛṣṭipathaprāptaṃ tan māyeva sutucchakam//

body.text: tadanavagame ca na bhogyena bhoktur anumānam / tataś ca nātmā na guṇatrayam /
body.translated_text: And when that is not ascertained, there can be no inference of the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) from the experienced (<s>bhogya</s>). Therefore, neither the self nor the three <s>guṇas</s> exist.

children.text: tadanavagame ca na bhogyena bhoktur anumānam / tataś ca nātmā na guṇatrayam /

body.text: athāvyatiriktaṃ, tat kiṃ tāttvikam atāttvikaṃ vā?
body.translated_text: If it is non-different [from the self], is it real or non-real?

children.text: athāvyatiriktaṃ, tat kiṃ tāttvikam atāttvikaṃ vā?

body.text: yadi tāttvikaṃ, tadā kāryāṇām aparisaṅkhyeyatve guṇānām apy aparisaṅkhyeyatā / tataś ca trayo guṇeti na vaktavyam / atha guṇānāṃ tritvaṃ, tadā kāryasyāpi tritvaṃ prāpnoty, ānantyaṃ hīyate / tathā kāryasya pratyakṣatve guṇānām api pratyakṣatvam / kiṃviṣayaṃ pradhānānumānam? guṇa
body.translated_text: If real, then since effects are innumerable, the <s>guṇas</s> too would be innumerable. Therefore, it should not be said 'there are three <s>guṇas</s>.' If the <s>guṇas</s> are three, then effects too would absurdly be three, and infinity would be lost. Similarly, if effects are perceptible, the <s>guṇas</s> too would be perceptible. What then is the object of the inference of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter)?

children.text: yadi tāttvikaṃ, tadā kāryāṇām aparisaṅkhyeyatve guṇānām apy aparisaṅkhyeyatā / tataś ca trayo guṇa īti na vaktavyam / atha guṇānāṃ tritvaṃ, tadā kāryasyāpi tritvaṃ prāpnoty, ānantyaṃ hīyate / tathā kāryasya pratyakṣatve guṇānām api pratyakṣatvam / kiṃviṣayaṃ pradhānānumānam? guṇa

Examination of ātmānumāna
\ppl
8.1 naiyāyikādisaṃmatasyātmānumānasya nirāsaḥ
tathātmānumānaṃ sukhadveṣajñānādinā na saṃbhavati, tena saha sambandhānavagamāt, tadanavagatau cānumānānarthakyam / kiṃ cātra sādhyate ?
body.translated_text: Similarly, the inference of the self (<s>ātman</s>) through pleasure, aversion, knowledge, and the like is not possible, because the relation between them is not ascertained; and when that is not ascertained, inference is purposeless. Moreover, what is being proved here?

children.text: tathā ātmānumānaṃ sukhadveṣajñānādinā na saṃbhavati, tena saha sambandhānavagamāt, tadanavagatau ca anumānānarthakyam / kiṃ cātra sādhyate ?

body.text: kiṃ  jñānasukhādīnām āśritatvam, āhosvid āśrayāśritaṃ vāḷjñānasvarūpam ? athāśritatvaṃ sādhyate / tadātmāḷnaivāvabodhitaḥ tato 'nyatvād āśritatvasya /
body.translated_text: Is it the dependent nature (<s>āśritatva</s>) of knowledge, pleasure, and the like, or is the substrate-dependent nature the nature of cognition itself? If dependent nature is being proved — then the self itself has not been established, because dependent nature is different from it.

children.text: kiṃ -- jñānasukhādīnām āśritatvam, āhosvid āśrayāśritaṃ vāḷjñānasvarūpam ? athāśritatvaṃ sādhyate / tadā ātmāḷnaivāvabodhitaḥ tato 'nyatvād āśritatvasya /

body.text: athātmāḷsādhyate / tad evaṃ bhavati  asty ātmāḷvijñānāt, na ca vyadhikaraṇasya gamakatvaṃ vidyate /
body.translated_text: If the self is what is being proved — then it would be: 'the self exists, because of cognition.' But what resides in a different substrate does not have probative force.

children.text: athā atmāḷsādhyate / tad evaṃ bhavati -- asty ātmāḷvijñānāt, na ca vyadhikaraṇasya gamakatvaṃ vidyate /

body.text: athāśritaṃ jñānasvarūpaṃ sādhyate / tac ca pratyakṣeṇāvagatam / anyo 'numānasya viṣayo vaktavyaḥ / kathaṃ jñānasukhādy ātmasambandhitvena vyapadiśyate  kiṃ sattāmātreṇāho tajjanyatayā tajjanakatvana vā tatsamavāyitvena vā tatsvarūpatādātmyād vā ?
body.translated_text: If what is being proved is the dependent nature of cognition — that has already been ascertained through perception. Some other object of inference should be stated. How are knowledge, pleasure, and the like designated as belonging to the self? Is it by mere existence, by being produced by it, by being its producer, by inhering in it (<s>samavāya</s>), or by identity with its nature?

children.text: athā aśritaṃ jñānasvarūpaṃ sādhyate / tac ca pratyakṣeṇāvagatam / anyo 'numānasya viṣayo vaktavyaḥ / kathaṃ jñānasukhādy ātmasambandhitvena vyapadiśyate -- kiṃ sattāmātreṇā aho tajjanyatayā tajjanakatvana vā tatsamavāyitvena vā tatsvarūpatādātmyād vā ?

body.text: tad yadi sattāmātreṇa sukhaṃ vijñānaṃ vātmano 'padiśyate tadātmavat sarve bhāvāś cetanāḥ syur vijñānasattāviśeṣāt / tathā sarve sukhino bhaveyur ānandasattāviśeṣāt /
body.translated_text: If pleasure or cognition is designated as belonging to the self merely by existence — then, just like the self, all entities would be conscious, since there is no difference regarding the existence of cognition. Similarly, all would be happy, since there is no difference regarding the existence of bliss.

children.text: tad yadi sattāmātreṇa sukhaṃ vijñānaṃ vā ātmano 'padiśyate tadā ātmavat sarve bhāvāś cetanāḥ syur vijñānasattāviśeṣāt / tathā sarve sukhino bhaveyur ānandasattāviśeṣāt /

body.text: atha tajjanyatayāḷvijñānam ātmano 'padiśyate ; tadā nayanālokapaṭāś cetanāḥ syus tair janyamānāviśeṣāt /
body.translated_text: If cognition is designated as belonging to the self by being produced by it — then the eye, light, cloth, and the like would be conscious, since there is no difference in what is produced by them.

children.text: atha tajjanyatayāḷvijñānam ātmano 'padiśyate ; tadā nayanālokapaṭāś cetanāḥ syus tair janyamānāviśeṣāt /

body.text: atha tajjanakatvena tasyeti cet, tad ayuktaṃ na vijñānenātmotpādyate bhavatāṃ pakṣe, utpādena vā smaraṇānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: If it is by being the producer of that — that is unjustified, because in your position the self is not produced by cognition; or if it is produced, then memory would be untenable.

children.text: atha tajjanakatvena tasyeti cet, tad ayuktaṃ na vijñānenā atma ūtpādyate bhavatāṃ pakṣe, utpādena vā smaraṇānupapattiḥ /

body.text: athātmasamavāyitvena vijñānam ātmano 'padiśyate na tadabhāvāt / bhavatu vā samavāyo hy akhaṇḍitātmā sarvātmavastrādisādhāraṇaḥ / tataḥ sarve cetanāḥ syuḥ / atha vijñānopalakṣitasya nānyatra saṃbhavo 'sti tad ayuktaṃ tad upalakṣitasyānyatra saṃbhavāt tatsaṃbhavaś ca tasyaikatvāt / asaṃbhave vā samavāyānekatvaprasaṅgaḥ asamavāyitvaṃ vānyeṣām /
body.translated_text: If cognition is designated as belonging to the self by inhering in it (<s>samavāya</s>) — that is not so, because <s>samavāya</s> does not exist. Or even if <s>samavāya</s> exists, being of undivided nature, it is common to all selves, cloth, and the like. Therefore, all would be conscious. If it is said that what is characterized by cognition cannot occur elsewhere — that is unjustified, because what is characterized by that can occur elsewhere, and its occurrence follows from its being one. Or if it does not occur, the consequence of multiplicity of <s>samavāya</s> follows, or the other things would lack <s>samavāya</s>.

children.text: athā atmasamavāyitvena vijñānam ātmano 'padiśyate na tadabhāvāt / bhavatu vā samavāyo hy akhaṇḍitātmā sarvātmavastrādisādhāraṇaḥ / tataḥ sarve cetanāḥ syuḥ / atha vijñānopalakṣitasya nānyatra saṃbhavo 'sti tad ayuktaṃ tad upalakṣitasya anyatra saṃbhavāt tatsaṃbhavaś ca tasya ekatvāt / asaṃbhave vā samavāyānekatvaprasaṅgaḥ asamavāyitvaṃ vānyeṣām /

body.text: tathā vijñānasamavāyātmanaḥ samavāyaḥ kiṃ  sattāmātreṇāhosvid ātmajanakatvena tajjanyatvena tatsamavāyitvenātmasvarūpatādātmyād vā ?
body.translated_text: Similarly, does the <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) of cognition-inherent-self belong to the self by mere existence, by being the producer of the self, by being produced by the self, by inhering in it, or by identity with the self's nature?

children.text: tathā vijñānasamavāyā atmanaḥ samavāyaḥ kiṃ -- sattāmātreṇā ahosvid ātmajanakatvena tajjanyatvena tatsamavāyitvenā atmasvarūpatādātmyād vā ?

body.text:
tad yadi sattāmātreṇātmanaḥ samavāyo 'padiśyate ; tadā jñānasamavāyasattāviśeṣāt sarveṣāṃ jñānasamavāyitvaprasaṅgaḥ / atha tajjanyatvena ; tad ayuktaṃ na hy ātmanā samavāyotpādanaṃ kriyate nityatvābhyupagamāt / atha tajjanakatvenātmanaḥ samavāyaḥ ; tad anupapannam ātmano nityatvāt / athātmani samavetas tenātmasamavāyo 'bhidhīyate / tad ayuktam / samavāyāntarānabhyupagamāt / athātmatādātmyena vartatety ātmasamavāyaḥ ucyate /
tadātmā vidyate nānyaḥ samavāyo 'sti tatsvabhāvānupraveśāt / evaṃ vijñānānandādīnāṃ samavāyasambandhena na niyatātmavyapadeśopapadyate /
body.translated_text: If <s>samavāya</s> is designated as belonging to the self by mere existence — then, since there is no difference regarding the existence of cognition-<s>samavāya</s>, the consequence follows that everything would have <s>samavāya</s> with cognition. If by being produced by it — that is unjustified, because the self does not produce <s>samavāya</s>, since it is accepted as eternal. If <s>samavāya</s> belongs to the self by being its producer — that is untenable, because the self is eternal. If it is said that <s>samavāya</s> is called 'belonging to the self' because it inheres in the self — that is unjustified, because another <s>samavāya</s> is not accepted. If it is said that <s>samavāya</s> is called 'belonging to the self' because it operates through identity with the self — then there is only the self and no other <s>samavāya</s>, because of the entry into its nature. Thus, the designation of cognition, bliss, and the like as definitively belonging to the self through the relation of <s>samavāya</s> is not established.

children.text:
tad yadi sattāmātreṇā atmanaḥ samavāyo 'padiśyate ; tadā jñānasamavāyasattāviśeṣāt sarveṣāṃ jñānasamavāyitvaprasaṅgaḥ / atha tajjanyatvena ; tad ayuktaṃ na hy ātmanā samavāyotpādanaṃ kriyate nityatvābhyupagamāt / atha tajjanakatvenā atmanaḥ samavāyaḥ ; tad anupapannam ātmano nityatvāt / athā atmani samavetas tenā atmasamavāyo 'bhidhīyate / tad ayuktam / samavāyāntarānabhyupagamāt / athā atmatādātmyena vartata ity ātmasamavāyaḥ ucyate /
tadā ātmā vidyate nānyaḥ samavāyo 'sti tatsvabhāvānupraveśāt / evaṃ vijñānānandādīnāṃ samavāyasambandhena na niyatātmavyapadeśa upapadyate /

body.text: athātmatādātmyenopajāyamānaṃ vijñānānandādikam ātmano 'padiśyate tadā vikārī prāpnoty anayā bhaṅgyātmā / tataś ca smaraṇānumānapratyabhijñānānupapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: If cognition, bliss, and the like that arise through identity with the self are designated as belonging to the self — then, by this reasoning, the self would be subject to modification. And therefore, memory, inference, and recognition would be untenable.

children.text: athā atmatādātmyenopajāyamānaṃ vijñānānandādikam ātmano 'padiśyate tadā vikārī prāpnoty anayā bhaṅgyā ātmā / tataś ca smaraṇānumānapratyabhijñānānupapattiḥ /

body.text: ito 'py ātmā sukhādikāryādhikaraṇo 'vagantuṃ na pāryate / kiṃ tenātmanānupajātātiśayena tāpādi kāryāṃ kriyatāhosvid upajātātiśayenāpi, kiṃ vyatiriktopajātātiśayena, avyatiriktopajātātiśayena vā?

children.text: tad yady anupajātātiśayenotpādyate tāpādi kāryaṃ, tadā sarvadā kuryād, anupajātabalasya kāryakāraṣābhyupagamān, na tāpādivikalaḥ syāt, samaṃ sukhādi kāryaṃ prasajyate / athāvyatiriktopajātātiśayenotpādyate tāpādi kāryaṃ, tadāvyatiriktopajātātiśayeti kiṃ bhaṇitaṃ bhavati? ātmopajāyate / tataś ca smaraṇānumānapratyabhijñānānupapattiḥ / atha vyatiriktopajātātiśayena janyate tāpādi kāryaṃ, sa tenātmanā saha sambaddho vā, na vā / yadi na sambaddhaḥ, sa tasyātiśayaḥ katham? atha sambaddhaḥ, kiṃ janakatvenātha janyatvena tatsamavāyitvena vā? tad yadi janakatvena sambaddhas, tadātmā tenātiśayenotpadyateti smaraṇānupapattiḥ / atha janyatvena, so 'pi tena katham utpādyate? kim anupajātātiśayena vyatiriktopajātātiśayena veti prāptā praśnaparamparā / atha tatsamavāyitvena, na, tasya sarvasādhāraṇatvāt, tadabhāvāc ca / athaikakāryajanakatvena sambaddhas, tad evedaṃ cintayitum ārabdhaṃ kim idaṃ janakatvaṃ nāmeti / kiṃ ca yad evānupajāte 'tiśayātmano rūpaṃ tad eva jāte 'pi, tat kathaṃ kāryaṃ kuryāt? atha pūrvarūpasyātadavasthyaṃ, susthitaṃ nityatvam! atha tādavasthyaṃ, tathāpi na karoti kāryam / evaṃ naiyāyikādimatenātmanopabhogasmaraṇādikaṃ na jāghaṭīti /
children.translated_text: If effects such as heat are produced without any capacity arising — then it would always produce them, since producing effects without arisen power is accepted; it would never be devoid of heat and the like; and effects such as pleasure would follow equally at all times. If effects such as heat are produced with a non-different arisen capacity — what is meant by 'non-different arisen capacity'? It means the self itself arises. And therefore, memory, inference, and recognition would be untenable. If effects such as heat are produced with a different arisen capacity — is that capacity related to the self or not? If not related, how is it a capacity of the self? If related — is it by being its producer, by being produced by it, or by inhering in it? If related by being its producer, then the self is produced by that capacity — and memory is untenable. If by being produced by it — how is it produced by the self? With a capacity that has not arisen, or with a different arisen capacity? — and an infinite series of questions is reached. If by inhering in it — no, because <s>samavāya</s> is common to all, and because it does not exist. If related by producing a single effect — this is precisely what we began to examine: what is this thing called 'productivity'? Moreover, whatever form the self has before the capacity arises is the same even after it arises — how then can it produce an effect? If the prior form changes its state, farewell to eternality! If it remains in the same state, even so it does not produce an effect. Thus, in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> and other positions, experience, memory, and the like do not work for the self.

body.translated_text: For this further reason too, the self as the substrate of effects such as pleasure and the like cannot be ascertained: Does the self produce effects such as heat without any capacity arising in it, or with a capacity arising in it? If with a capacity arising, is the arisen capacity different from it, or non-different?

children.text: ito 'py ātmā sukhādikāryādhikaraṇo 'vagantuṃ na pāryate / kiṃ tenātmanānupajātātiśayena tāpādi kāryāṃ kriyatā ahosvid upajātātiśayenāpi, kiṃ vyatiriktopajātātiśayena, avyatiriktopajātātiśayena vā?

body.text: Refutation of the Mīmāṃsa inference of the self

tathā mīmāṃsakamatenāpy ātmānumānaṃ na pravartate pramāṇāntarānavadhāritārthaviṣayatvābhyupagamāt pramāṇānām / niyataviṣayāṇi hi pramāṇāni pratipadyante pratyakṣāvaseye nānumānaṃ pravartata, anumānāvaseye ca na pratyakṣaṃ pravartate / tataś cetaretaravyāvṛttiviśeṣaviṣayāṇi / tad ayuktaṃ (read: uktaṃ) ``viśeṣe 'nugamābhāvaḥ / " viśeṣo niyatapramāṇagrāhyo 'rthaḥ / tathābhūte 'rthe 'ṅgīkriyamāṇe 'numānasyānugamābhāvaḥ / anugamaḥ sambandhas, tadgrahaṇānupapattiḥ / arthe (read: atha) pratyakṣādyavadhārite 'py 'rthe 'numānaṃ pravartate; nanv evaṃ pratyakṣānumānasādhāraṇo 'rthaḥ prasaktaḥ / sādhāraṇatā samānatā / ``sāmānye siddhasādhyatā'' pratyakṣāvagatatvāt / anadhigatārthagantṛviśeṣaṇaṃ cāpārthakam / athavā sāmānye
siddhe sādhanam ityanyo 'rthaḥ / sāmānyayor gamyagamakabhāvo 'bhyupagamyate mīmāṃsakena / na ca tat
sāmānyaṃ vidyate / yathā ca na vidyate tathā prāg evoditam / tataś ca siddhasya sādhanaṃ vidyamānasya sādhanam / na cāgnitvam asti / tadabhāve kasyedaṃ jñāpakam? athavā siddhaṃ sādhanaṃ siddhasādhanam ity anyo 'rthaḥ / vidyamānaṃ sādhanam / na ca dhūmatvasāmānyam asti / tac ca vidyamānaṃ (Sukhlal: tattva; read: tac cāvidyamānaṃ) sāmānyaṃ kathaṃ sāmānyaṃ (read: sāmānye) sādhanaṃ bhavitum arhati? athavā siddhasādhanaṃ jñātam anumānaṃ sādhanaṃ bhavati / na ca dhūmatvaṃ jñātaṃ svayamasattvāt, athavā grahaṇopāyābhāvāt, tasyānusyūtaṃ rūpam / na ca tad ātmany anusyūtam / nāpy ekasyāṃ vyaktāv, api tu bahvīṣu vyaktiṣu / na ca bahvyo vyaktayopalabhyante / api tv ekaiva dhūmavyaktir upalabhate / na caikasyāṃ vyaktāv anugatātmatayā sāmānyasaṃvittir asti / na cākārāntarasāmānyam
(perhaps: ākārāntaraṃ sāmānyasya) /
body.translated_text:
Similarly, even according to the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> view, the inference of the self does not operate, because it is accepted that the means of knowledge have as their domain objects not ascertained by another means of knowledge. For the means of knowledge operate with fixed domains — inference does not operate regarding what is to be ascertained by perception, and perception does not operate regarding what is to be ascertained by inference. Hence they have as their domains objects that are specific exclusions from each other. It is stated: 'In the specific, there is absence of connection.' The specific is an object grasped by a fixed means of knowledge. When such an object is accepted, there is absence of connection for inference. Connection is relation; its grasping is untenable. If inference operates even regarding an object ascertained by perception and the like — then the absurd consequence of the object being common to perception and inference follows. Commonality is sameness. 'In commonality, there is the fault of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>),' because it is already cognized by perception. And the qualification 'reaching an object not previously cognized' is pointless. Or alternatively, 'the means of proof is established in the universal' — this is another meaning. The <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> accepts the relation of the indicated and the indicator between the two universals. But that universal does not exist. And that it does not exist has already been stated before. And hence, the proof of what is established is the proof of what exists. But fire-ness does not exist. In its absence, what does this indicate? Or alternatively, 'an established means of proof is <s>siddhasādhana</s> (a proven instrument)' — this is another meaning. An existing means of proof. But the universal smoke-ness does not exist.
And that non-existent universal — how can it serve as the means of proof in the universal relation? Or alternatively, <s>siddhasādhana</s> means that a known inferential mark serves as the means of proof. But smoke-ness is not known, because it does not exist in itself, or because there is no means of grasping it. Its form is what pervades the instances. But that is not pervading in itself, nor in a single individual, but rather in many individuals. But many individuals are not apprehended. Rather, only a single smoke-individual is apprehended. And in a single individual there is no awareness of the universal as the pervading nature. Nor is there another form of the universal.
